# Cronomicon Changelog

All notable changes to the Cronomicon Script Orchestrator are documented here in reverse chronological order. Each version represents a distinct phase of development, derived from the implementation plans and design reviews kept in the maintainers' planning archive.

From 1.0.0 on, this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/)
and this file follows [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/). Entries
before 1.0.0 are kept in their original prose form.

> **Name change.** The product was renamed from Amadeus to Cronomicon in
> [2.0.0]. Entries before 2.0.0 keep their original text and name the product,
> its binaries, environment variables and other identifiers by their former
> name.

---

## [2.0.1] - 2026-09-25

The repository now holds the application only. The deployment stack that
surrounded it, including the CI-fronted image pipeline introduced in 1.5.45, is
no longer shipped: how you build the image, host the container and put a
reverse proxy and identity provider in front of it is your deployment's
concern. The application, its API, its schema (v1150) and the runner protocol
(13) are unchanged.

### Removed

- **Breaking:** Remove the reference deployment stack. The root
  `docker-compose.yml` (Traefik, Authelia, Cronomicon and Apprise, with the
  registry image default and the external data volume from 1.5.45) and its
  `traefik/` and `authelia/` configuration are gone. If you deploy from that
  file, keep your own copy before upgrading your checkout.
- Remove the CI-fronted deployment procedure: `deployment-guide.md`, including
  its "CI-fronted deployment" section (the kaniko build, the registry push, the
  DockHand webhook and the release/rollback steps), the `go-no-go.md` release
  checklist and `verify-deployment.sh`. The GitLab CI pipeline that 1.5.45
  describes is not carried in this repository; build and publish the image
  from your own pipeline.
- Remove the runner container images `Dockerfile.runner` and
  `Dockerfile.runner.fat`. The server image still bundles the runner binaries
  at `GET /agents/{filename}`, and the systemd install path through
  `runner-install.sh` is unchanged.
- Remove the Vault Agent sidecar kit (`deploy/vault-agent/`) and
  `vault-runbook.md`. The in-app Vault source is unaffected; the administrator
  manual's Vault section covers a host-side agent.
- Remove the day-2 runbooks (`runbook.md`, `migrations-runbook.md`) and the k6
  load tests (`deploy/loadtest/`).

### Changed

- Rewrite `backend/deploy/README.md` as an index of what the application still
  ships there, with the consumer of each file. `ci-validate-template.yml`, the
  drop-in `cronomicon validate` job for a job-definitions repository, stays.
- Rewrite the administrator manual's Deployment chapter to describe a
  reference topology (Compose, systemd or Kubernetes) instead of the bundled
  files. The runner guides, the env examples, the Dockerfile comments and the
  runner agent's reverse-proxy error now point at the manuals, not at removed
  files.
- Drop internal version and decision codes ("since v0.57.26", "A12") from the
  README, both manuals, the runner and language guides and the training
  courses, so each page reads as a description of the current product.
- Show only the emblem and the name in the sidebar. The tagline, now "Ancient
  rites of scheduling, made easy", appears on the login card only. The README
  demo is re-recorded to match and switches from light to dark mode halfway.
- Document the `develop`/`release` branch flow in `CONTRIBUTING.md`: branch
  from `develop` and open pull requests against it.

## [2.0.0] - 2026-09-25

**BREAKING — the Cronomicon edition.** Every identifier a process reads, an
operator types or a user writes into a repository changes name in this release,
with **no compatibility readers**: this is the first release under the new name
and nothing was deployed under the old one. The changelog entries below 2.0.0
keep their original text and refer to the product and its identifiers by their
former name, Amadeus.

### Changed

- **Environment prefix `AMADEUS_` → `CRONOMICON_`**, for every server knob
  (`CRONOMICON_DB_PATH`, `CRONOMICON_KEK*`, `CRONOMICON_OIDC_*`, …) and every
  runner-agent knob (`CRONOMICON_RUNNER_*`, including `CRONOMICON_RUNNER_CONFIG`).
  The full list is `backend/deploy/env-matrix.md`; an old-prefixed variable is
  simply not read.
- **Injected run environment `AMADEUS_*` → `CRONOMICON_*`**: `CRONOMICON_RUN_*`,
  `CRONOMICON_VAR_<key>`, `CRONOMICON_SECRET_<key>`, `CRONOMICON_KEY_<label>`,
  `CRONOMICON_WATCH_{PATH,FILE,SIZE}`, `CRONOMICON_REACTED_TO_*`. The
  reserved-name refusal now covers `CRONOMICON_*` only. Scripts, inventories and
  `authKeyEnvVar` fields must use the new spelling.
- **YAML `apiVersion: amadeus.io/v1` → `cronomicon.io/v1`**; the inventory
  pragma `# amadeus:v1` → `# cronomicon:v1`; the inventory sidecar
  `inventory/<name>.amadeus.yaml` → `<name>.cronomicon.yaml`; the per-host
  inventory variable `amadeus_auth_key_env_var` → `cronomicon_auth_key_env_var`.
  `cronomicon validate` rejects the old apiVersion like any unsupported one.
- **Output marker `::amadeus-output name=KEY::VALUE` →
  `::cronomicon-output name=KEY::VALUE`.** The old form is an ordinary log line.
- **Token prefixes** `amt_reg_` → `crn_reg_` (registration), `amt_run_` →
  `crn_run_` (runner API key), `amasvc_` → `crnsvc_` (service account). Update
  secret-scanner patterns (`backend/deploy/security-review.md`).
- **The `source` value `amadeus` → `cronomicon`** (API enums and defaults, YAML
  `source:`, the `?source=` filters, the badge). Migrations are rewritten in
  place — every CHECK constraint, default and comment — rather than layered,
  since no database ever ran them under the old text. **Schema version is
  unchanged (v1150). Delete any development database and let the server create
  a fresh one.** Migration `410` is renamed `410_ssh_hosts_cronomicon_inv`.
- **Runner inventory mode value** `CRONOMICON_RUNNER_INVENTORY=amadeus` →
  `=cronomicon` (`local` is unchanged).
- **Binaries and directories** `amadeus` → `cronomicon`, `amadeus-runner` →
  `cronomicon-runner`; `cmd/cronomicon`, `cmd/cronomicon-runner`; the agent
  artifacts `cronomicon-runner-linux-{amd64,arm64}` under `/agents/`.
- **Paths and files**: `/var/lib/cronomicon/cronomicon.db` (default DB),
  `cronomicon.log`, `cronomicon-<date>.db` snapshots, `cronomicon.env`,
  `cronomicon-runner.env`, `/etc/cronomicon-runner/`, `/var/lib/cronomicon-runner/`,
  `/usr/local/bin/cronomicon-runner`, the `cronomicon-runner` system user,
  `cronomicon-runner.service`, `cronomicon-vault-agent.service`,
  `/usr/share/cronomicon/agents`, `/app/cronomicon`, `~/.local/share/cronomicon/`.
- **Container and compose**: image `registry.example.com/cronomicon`, override
  `CRONOMICON_IMAGE`, compose project/service `cronomicon`, volume
  `cronomicon-data`, secret mount `/run/secrets/cronomicon_kek`.
- **S3 key prefix** for database backups `amadeus-backups/` → `cronomicon-backups/`.
- **Cookies** `amadeus_session_v3` → `cronomicon_session_v3`, `amadeus_csrf` →
  `cronomicon_csrf`. Every browser session is signed out once.
- **Prometheus metrics**, all eighteen:

  | Before | After |
  |---|---|
  | `amadeus_active_runners` | `cronomicon_active_runners` |
  | `amadeus_backup_failures_total` | `cronomicon_backup_failures_total` |
  | `amadeus_backup_last_success_timestamp_seconds` | `cronomicon_backup_last_success_timestamp_seconds` |
  | `amadeus_http_request_duration_seconds` | `cronomicon_http_request_duration_seconds` |
  | `amadeus_http_requests_total` | `cronomicon_http_requests_total` |
  | `amadeus_log_archive_failures_total` | `cronomicon_log_archive_failures_total` |
  | `amadeus_log_archive_last_success_timestamp_seconds` | `cronomicon_log_archive_last_success_timestamp_seconds` |
  | `amadeus_log_archive_pending` | `cronomicon_log_archive_pending` |
  | `amadeus_log_ingest_bytes_total` | `cronomicon_log_ingest_bytes_total` |
  | `amadeus_log_ingest_chunks_total` | `cronomicon_log_ingest_chunks_total` |
  | `amadeus_redaction_dictionary_rebuilds_total` | `cronomicon_redaction_dictionary_rebuilds_total` |
  | `amadeus_redaction_dictionary_size` | `cronomicon_redaction_dictionary_size` |
  | `amadeus_runs_finished_total` | `cronomicon_runs_finished_total` |
  | `amadeus_runs_started_total` | `cronomicon_runs_started_total` |
  | `amadeus_schedule_publishes_total` | `cronomicon_schedule_publishes_total` |
  | `amadeus_sla_breaches_total` | `cronomicon_sla_breaches_total` |
  | `amadeus_ssh_orphans_reconciled_total` | `cronomicon_ssh_orphans_reconciled_total` |
  | `amadeus_webhook_syncs_total` | `cronomicon_webhook_syncs_total` |

- **Identities**: GitLab bot `cronomicon-bot` / `cronomicon-bot@cronomicon.io`,
  the SSH probe user `cronomicon-keyscan`, the seeded demo groups
  `cronomicon-{admins,operators,viewers}`, the notification sender default
  `cronomicon@example.com`, the process-log prefix `cronomicon:`.
- **Wire protocol 13.** No message shape changed; the bump exists so an agent
  built before the rename is refused at registration (`426 protocol_too_old`)
  instead of assembling a run environment under the old prefix and scanning
  for a marker no script emits any more. `MinProtocolVersion` tracks it.
- **Documentation** — both manuals, the runner guides, the language guides, the
  training courses, the README, the deploy tree and both OpenAPI copies use only
  the new spellings. The historical prose about the pre-1.5.41 `_SECRET_KEK*`
  alias is removed from the env matrix and the KEK config comment.

### Removed

- The `amadeus`-named binaries, units, example files and the published
  `amadeus-runner.env.example`; nothing replaces them under the old name.

## [1.5.45] - 2026-09-18

### Added

- **A GitLab CI pipeline builds and publishes the image (`.gitlab-ci.yml`).**
  DockHand had been building from a working copy it kept across deploys, which
  retained files git had deleted (`internal/gitlab/migrate.go`, gone in
  v1.5.41) and mixed revisions after a bad fetch — the same blind failure as
  v0.52.26, and the reason v1.5.43's Dockerfile grew its exit-code assertions.
  CI clones fresh for every job: merge requests and `main` run `make verify`
  and `tsc -b` + vitest; a `vX.Y.Z` tag then builds with kaniko, pushes
  `registry.example.com/amadeus:vX.Y.Z` + `:latest`, and calls the
  DockHand stack webhook so DockHand re-pulls. DockHand's "Build images on
  deploy" is now OFF for this stack.
  `docker-compose.yml` defaults `image:` to that registry tag
  (`AMADEUS_IMAGE` overrides — `amadeus:local` to build from a clean clone,
  a version tag to roll back) and declares the data volume `external: true`
  by name so a redeploy can never create an empty one. The deployment
  guide's "CI-fronted deployment" section has the stack settings and the
  release/rollback procedure. The Dockerfile's stale-checkout repair and
  assertions stay until the first CI-built deploy proves them unnecessary.
  Getting here took three pipeline runs: the runners are not privileged (no
  docker:dind) and the GitLab instance has no container registry, which is
  why the internal registry and kaniko are the answer.

### Changed

- **The docs stop promising the per-feature protocol gates and the KEK aliases
  (DM-6).** `runner-manage.html` carried eleven claims that an older agent is
  gated feature by feature, that Resync needs protocol v4+, that Scan keys is
  disabled below v5, and that managed settings skip "old agents"; the install
  guide and the user manual carried five more. All now state the one rule that
  replaced them: the server's floor tracks the current wire protocol and is
  checked at registration, at redeclare and on every poll, so an agent below it
  is refused outright rather than silently degraded. `backend/README.md` and
  `deploy/env-matrix.md` stop saying the `AMADEUS_SECRET_KEK*` aliases still
  dual-read — the rollout section now marks renaming them a **prerequisite** for
  upgrading, not an option. The README's retention row also said "seven
  per-table knobs"; there are eleven.
- **The administrator manual is reconciled to v1.5.45**, not merely restamped.
  Its protocol section names all three places the floor is enforced, and the
  upgrade-notes table gains a v1.5.40–v1.5.44 entry: this is the one upgrade
  there that can stop a runner working, an agent left behind answers
  `426 protocol_too_old` and keeps its identity, `AMADEUS_SECRET_KEK*` must be
  renamed first, and installs seeded after ~v0.57.25 should check that Recycle
  Bin and Definition History read 30 and 365 rather than 0.
- **Seven Go comments describing deleted gates as live (DM-7).** The register
  request's own field doc still said an absent `protocolVersion` was "accepted
  with a warning" seventy lines above the code that refuses it; `resync.go`,
  `keyscan.go` and four `runnerproto.go` entries still described the v2/v3/v4/v6
  hard-fails in the present tense; `gitlab/sync.go` still pointed at
  `migrate.go`, deleted in v1.5.41. Each now reads as history where it is
  history. Also removed: `Config.Warnings`, which has had no writer since
  v1.5.41 (and two tests that asserted it was empty), and the stale rationale on
  the reserved-KEK name bar, which outlived the collision it was written for and
  now says so.

## [1.5.44] - 2026-09-18

### Fixed

- **Two retention knobs were seeded as "keep forever" on every fresh install
  (DM-4).** `SeedAuditComplianceFromEnv` — the one route from the documented
  `AMADEUS_RETENTION_*` env to the stored blob — hand-listed the fields it
  wrote and had fallen two behind the struct since PF-3 added them, so
  **Recycle Bin** and **Definition Revisions** were stored as `0`, which every
  sweep reads as keep-forever (`days <= 0` returns early). Neither the recycle
  bin nor the revision history was ever reaped until someone happened to press
  Save on Audit & Compliance. The seed now derives from the defaults and
  overrides only the six knobs the env actually feeds, so a future knob is
  correct without anyone remembering this; a new test seeds with the default
  env values and requires the stored blob back byte-equal to the defaults.
  Two existing tests encoded the same omission in their expectations, which is
  why the suite was green on it. **Operators:** only installs first seeded
  after ~v0.57.25 are affected — an older deployment's blob simply omits the
  keys, and absent keys keep their defaults. If yours is one, open Settings →
  Audit & Compliance and check that Recycle Bin and Definition Revisions read
  30 and 365 rather than 0.
- **LB17's fix was itself unreachable; the SSH probe stops matching errors by
  substring (DM-5).** v1.5.36 corrected `credMsg`'s match string on the stated
  grounds that a bastion key loading inside `dial()` could still produce the
  "no auth configured" error. It cannot: `dial()` calls `loadSigner` for the
  bastion only when the bastion has a credential or key name. All four
  probe-side call sites guard the empty case first, so both the `credMsg`
  branch and `classifyDialErr`'s `authKeyEnvVar` substring are deleted, and
  LB17 stands closed on the probe's two-tier routing — where it always actually
  stood. The error itself becomes a sentinel (`errNoAuth`): it stays live
  through the executor, which calls `loadSigner` unguarded and writes the
  message to the run log. A new test pins each guard, so if one is ever dropped
  the test fails rather than an operator seeing "unparseable private key" for a
  host with no key at all.

## [1.5.43] - 2026-09-18

### Fixed

- **The Apprise target column had two readers and they disagreed (DM-1;
  migration 1150).** `internal/notify` read `apprise_targets` through its own
  SELECT and its own copy of the parser, so when v1.5.41 dropped the pre-rich
  bare-string form from the *settings* reader only, a stored row still in that
  form showed **zero targets in Settings while every alert was still being
  delivered to it** — and the first Save of the Notifications card rebuilt the
  column from the empty parsed list and silently stopped delivery. Migration
  1150 rewrites any bare string to the object form (enabled, since a bare URL
  was always delivered to; objects pass through untouched, `enabled: false`
  included), and the dispatcher now calls `settings.ParseAppriseTargets` — one
  column, one parser. A regression test fails if a second one ever appears.
- **The runner protocol floor is enforced on every poll, not just at
  registration (DM-2).** An agent registers **once** and resumes a saved
  identity on every later start, so a runner registered before a server upgrade
  kept polling at its old protocol forever — and with v1.5.40's per-feature
  `agent_too_old` gates deleted, nothing refused it. Such an agent was handed
  secret files, check-mode flags and per-run SSH identities that its binary
  drops as unknown fields: **a dry run would apply for real.** The poll now
  answers `426 protocol_too_old` naming both versions, after refreshing
  `last_seen_at` so the runner reads as alive-but-refused rather than offline.
  The agent recognises the 426, keeps its identity (re-registering would declare
  the same protocol and be refused identically) and logs the upgrade
  instruction on every poll. **Operators:** a runner that has not been upgraded
  since before v1.5.40 stops receiving work at this release and says so in its
  own log; upgrade the binary and restart it — no deregistration needed.
- **The API contract now declares the register shape it actually enforces
  (DM-3).** `POST /runners/register` documented `required: [name, os,
  capabilities, version]` with no `protocolVersion` and no 426, while the
  server had refused an absent value since v1.5.40 — a client built from the
  spec got a status the operation did not define. The field is now required
  (`minimum: 12`) with a documented 426, `/poll` documents its new 426,
  redeclare's stale `minimum: 4` is corrected, and the `Runner` schema and
  control-op enum stop promising the retired v4 gate. First conformance test
  to pin the register request shape.

## [1.5.42] - 2026-09-18

### Fixed

- **DD band residue: the contract and the docs stopped promising what the
  code stopped doing.** A review of the finished band re-ran each phase's
  own proof greps and found five leftovers the green gates could not see.
  Both `openapi.yaml` copies still documented `409 agent_too_old` on the
  resync and keyscan endpoints and protocol-gate refusals in three manifest
  descriptions, all retired by Phase B (client regenerated). Five source
  comments cited the deleted SEAMS files as if they existed. The
  administrator manual said the server "accepts any agent from v1 up",
  that a pre-v6 agent parks a run, and that the Runners page disables a
  button for older agents — none true since the floor tracks the current
  protocol. `deploy/security-review.md` listed `AMADEUS_SECRET_KEK_FILE`
  as a live alias. And the review doc's subcommand count was off by one
  (six remain after `migrate-scripts`, not five).

## [1.5.41] - 2026-09-15

### Removed

- **Four compatibility shims that only the private history needed, Phase D
  of the DD band (DD-13, DD-14, DD-15a, DD-16).** The `AMADEUS_SECRET_KEK*`
  env aliases (dual-read since v0.48.0 with a startup warning; the KEK reads
  only as `AMADEUS_KEK`, `AMADEUS_KEK_FILE`, `AMADEUS_KEK_VERSION` and
  `AMADEUS_KEK_<N>[_FILE]` now, and `docker-compose.yml` no longer flows the
  old spelling through). The pre-rich bare-string form of Apprise targets
  (`["slack://x"]`; such an entry is skipped like any other unparseable one).
  The boot-time SSH-credential backfill that lifted env-var-named keys into
  credential rows (idempotent and long since a no-op; hosts whose material
  Cronomicon never held stay on the executor's name-fallback path, which is
  unchanged). And `amadeus migrate-scripts` with its 700-line engine — the
  one-time June conversion of inline job bodies to `scripts/` files, which no
  public reader has a repository to run against. **Operators:** a deployment
  still setting `AMADEUS_SECRET_KEK*` fails its first stored-secret operation
  with "no KEK configured" — rename before upgrading.

### Changed

- **Kept, deliberately:** `SeedAuditComplianceFromEnv`, which the plan listed
  for deletion. It is not an upgrade shim — it is the only path by which the
  documented `AMADEUS_RETENTION_*` env vars reach a fresh database (the
  retention sweep reads the stored blob; the env is its once-only bootstrap).
  Deleting it would have made three documented knobs inert on every new
  install.

## [1.5.40] - 2026-09-15

### Changed

- **The runner protocol floor tracks the current protocol, Phase B of the DD
  band (DD-5..8).** `MinProtocolVersion` was 1 against a current version of
  12, which kept twelve separate `409 agent_too_old` refusals alive for
  agents that could not exist in any fleet upgraded with its server. The
  floor is now 12: an agent declaring anything older — or nothing — is
  refused at registration and redeclare with `426 protocol_too_old`, and
  everything past registration assumes the current wire shape. Every
  per-feature gate (manifest inventory/checkout/secrets/identity/options/
  become-file, the keyscan and resync endpoint and poll-time gates, the
  file-watch distribution gate, the "flagged but pre-v6" claim exclusion)
  is deleted, along with the two per-button protocol gates on the Runners
  page. **Operators:** a runner older than v1.5.0 (protocol 12) will be
  refused at its next registration with an actionable message; use the
  Runners page's upgrade command first. Runners already registered are
  unaffected until they re-register.

### Removed

- The `keyscanMinProtocol` / `resyncMinProtocol` constants and every
  `protocol_version` read that existed only to feed a gate; the `protocol
  >= N` wording in the runner security guide, the administrator manual and
  the deploy security review.

## [1.5.39] - 2026-09-15

### Removed

- **The four deprecated alert-rule fields, Phase C of the DD band (DD-9..12,
  migration 1140).** `jobTags`, `triggerCount`, `triggerWindow` and
  `notifyTriggerer` had been marked `deprecated` in the spec since v0.52.23
  ("retained for stored legacy rules; not used for matching") — the
  dispatcher never selected them. They are gone from `AlertRuleInput`,
  `AlertRule`, the generated client and the Notifications card, and the
  columns are dropped from `alert_config` along with `name` and `condition`,
  two older NOT NULL columns whose only values were ever derived from the
  target and trigger. A client that still sends the four fields is not
  refused; they are ignored. The down migration re-adds all six empty.

## [1.5.37] - 2026-09-15

### Changed

- **Frontend dead exports dropped, Phase E of the DD band (DD-17).**
  Twenty-one symbols across twelve files carried `export` but were imported
  by nothing — constants like `MAX_NOTES`, `INTERVAL_PRESETS`,
  `INPUTS_PER_PAGE`, `RAIL_BREAKPOINT`, the Score plot geometry, helpers like
  `browserZoneLabel`, `parseIntervalMs`, `useViewportWidth`, and the `TabSpec`

## [1.5.36] - 2026-09-15

### Removed

- **Dead code, Phase A of the DD band (DD-1..4).** Ten Go symbols that `deadcode -test` proved unreachable even
  with the test suite as roots (`auth.RoleRank`, `auth.IsServiceActor`,
  `envref.IsReference`, `scheduler.QueueDepths`, `settings.ValidMemberKind`,
  the `api.roleValid` passthrough, `Server.snapshotRevisionDB`,
  `settings.sortedCopy`, `agent.logBuffer.total`, `redactdict.Default`), and
  five exports that only tests reached: `secrets.NewVaultClient` (the test
  now calls the `WithOptions` form production uses), `cronutil.FormatInterval`
  (nothing rendered intervals — the API stores the authored string),
  `cronutil.NextWindowed` (its four firing claims now run through
  `NextNWindowed`, the entry point the scheduler actually uses),
  `runref.ScanNames`, and the `auth.BuiltinRoles` wrapper. `ValidMemberKind`
  was checked before deletion: the write path validates through the
  string-typed `ValidAgencyMemberKind`, so nothing lost a check.

### Fixed

- **LB17 — SSH Test on a keyless host said "not a parseable private key".**
  The friendly "no SSH key configured" message existed but matched a string
  no error ever carried. The two-tier probe had already routed keyless
  target and bastion rows to the reachability tier, so the only way to
  reach the message was a bastion key loading inside dial — that route now
  matches the error `conn.go` actually emits.
- A stale `Allow|Forbid|Replace` comment on the YAML job spec now names the
  940 CHECK (`Allow|Forbid|Queue`).

### Added

- **`make deadcode`** in `backend/` — the unreachable-symbol report with
  tests as roots. Advisory, not part of `verify`; read a symbol before
  deleting it.

## [1.5.35] - 2026-09-10

### Removed

- **SSH-executor key delivery, dropped rather than built (KB band,
  the ssh-key-refusal plan).** A job that binds an SSH key
  (`AMADEUS_KEY_*`) and ran on the in-app SSH executor used to get a warning
  line in its run log and then run without the key — the executor connects
  from Cronomicon and cannot place a key file on the target, and remote-target
  delivery (the P1.4 twin of the runner's D8 delivery) would have needed a
  per-host trust flag, a cleanup path for killed sessions and a Windows
  story, for a gap the runner path already covers and a Secret binding
  already works around. The warn-and-skip is gone.

### Changed

- **A key-bound run that resolves to the SSH executor is refused at
  enqueue, by every producer.** The executor is decided per run (per-run
  override, then the job's executor, then the global default, then run-type
  capability), never at compose, so the check sits where every producer
  already runs the unbound-reference probe and tests the RESOLVED executor:
  a manual or token run gets `422 key_binding_requires_runner` naming the key
  and both ways out (a runner, or a Secret binding written to a file by the
  job body); a scheduled fire records a skipped run (reason-keyed episode
  de-dupe); a workflow step fails the step; a reaction records a delivery
  error and no run row; a file arrival is refused. A binding added while a
  run was queued or parked fails the run at dispatch, before it connects,
  after the injection audit. Stored reasons are sentences, since History
  shows them verbatim.
- **The key surfaces say so.** The Jobs detail key field, the Composer's key
  picker and the Run dialog's references panel state the refusal (and that it
  is per-run when the job's executor is unset) with the Secret-binding way out
  inline; the Run dialog shows the 422 message and stays open without forcing
  the runner choice. The spec names the code on both trigger endpoints. User
  manual §11.6 and the glossary reconciled; stamped v1.5.35.

## [1.5.34] - 2026-09-10

### Added

- **The compliance audit stream is masked (AM band,
  the audit-redaction plan).** `audit.log` and the three tables it
  exports (`change_log`, `activity`, `auth_events`) had a masking hook since
  the logging update and nothing ever installed one, so the stream was durable
  and unredacted. A new **process-wide redaction dictionary**
  (`internal/redactdict`) — every stored secret, stored SSH credential,
  encrypted integration setting and multi-line variable the server can
  decrypt, in every scope — is now installed at boot and applied to each
  free-text column (`target`, `summary`, `details`, `reason`) before the row is
  stored, so the row, the streamed line and the CSV export carry the same
  text. It rebuilds after every write to those stores (a rotation's own audit
  row is masked with the *new* value) with a five-minute backstop, and keeps
  the last good build when a rebuild fails. A build that cannot decrypt some
  values — a KEK version not configured, a missing KEK after a restore —
  masks with what it could build and writes **one** self-describing row,
  `system / Audit / redactor-unavailable`, per outage, and one
  `redactor-restored` on recovery; the gap is never silent. Two metrics:
  `amadeus_redaction_dictionary_size` and
  `amadeus_redaction_dictionary_rebuilds_total{outcome}`. Masking is
  unconditional, as for run logs. Vault-sourced values remain the documented
  residual (dispatch-time only); the process log (`amadeus.log`) is unchanged
  and deferred to a follow-up.
- **Three source-scanning guards** pin the invariants the masker depends on:
  only `internal/auditlog` inserts into the audit tables; every writer of a
  redaction source notifies the dictionary; and the seven encrypted settings
  columns come from one table shared with `rewrap-secrets`.

### Fixed

- **Four encrypted settings values were rotated but never masked** — the
  GitLab webhook secret, the S3 log-storage key, the Vault role id and the
  observability bearer token. `rewrap-secrets` listed all seven encrypted
  settings columns; the run-log redaction dictionary listed three. Both now
  read `secrets.EncryptedSettingsColumns`, so these four are masked in run
  logs as well as in the audit stream.
- **The audit writers trimmed before masking**, so a secret straddling the
  4096-byte length cut would have survived as a prefix once a masker was
  installed. The order is now mask, then trim, on every writer.
- **`target` and `reason` were outside the masked set** on the audit writers
  (`details`, and `summary` on the activity path, were the whole of it).
- **The break-glass `grant-admin` CLI wrote its `auth_events` row with raw
  SQL**, bypassing the masker and the length bound. It now goes through the
  shared writer.

### Changed

- **Administrator manual reconciled to v1.5.34**: §6.2 states what the audit
  stream masks and what it cannot, §8.8's callout turns from "durable and not
  redacted" to the degraded-build behaviour and the new metrics, and
  `deploy/security-review.md` splits the LU-4/LU-10 residual (the process
  log's stands; the audit stream's is closed) and gains an AM controls table.
- **Observability auth type `basic` removed** from the spec, generated client,
  validator and Integrations card — it was accepted nowhere and rejected at
  save. Basic auth on the scrape path is a reverse-proxy job; the deployment
  guide gains a "Protecting `/metrics`" section with the Traefik shape.

## [1.5.33] - 2026-09-09

### Added

- **The S3 log archive (SL band).** The
  `s3` log-storage backend had been a settings shell since migration 060 —
  selectable, stored, and refused with 422 on save. It is now **Local + S3
  archive**: local disk stays the only write target during a run (live
  tailing needs an append-only file with stable offsets), and a **scheduled
  sync** copies every sealed log to the bucket afterwards — terminal runs
  with no archive marker, oldest first, sixty seconds after completion.
  Migration **1130** adds `runs.log_archived_at` / `log_archive_state`
  (`missing` | `failed` | `expired`), a partial index for the pending query,
  and the timetable, counters and last-sync status on `log_storage_config`.
  The sweep (`internal/logsync`) is **single-flight** (a tick that fires
  during a tick is skipped; the interval is measured from the end of the last
  one, read from the stored finish time so restarts resume the wait),
  **budgeted** (200 files or 10 minutes, leftovers carry), and
  **verify-by-size** (the marker is stamped only when the upload's reported
  size matches the local file, in the same transaction as the counter bump).
  Timetable: every 5/15 minutes, hourly, 6-hourly, or **daily at HH:MM
  UTC**; default 15 minutes. **Sync now** (`POST /settings/log-storage/sync`,
  202 / 409 / 422) runs one tick on demand, `?reconcile=1` restores markers
  from objects already in the bucket after a database restore.
- **History reads archived logs through the server.** `GET
  /runs/{traceId}/log` falls back to the bucket when the local file is gone
  and the row is marked — same body, same `X-Log-Offset`, a ranged read for a
  mid-object offset — and never redirects (the spec's never-implemented 302
  is gone; a 503 `log_archive_unavailable` names the case where the store is
  unconfigured or refusing). Run rows carry `logArchivedAt`; the drawer shows
  **Log archived to S3**.
- **Retention learns there are two copies.** While the archive backend is
  on, the local reaper never removes a log the sync has not yet copied,
  however old. The **eleventh** Audit & Compliance knob, **Archived Run Logs
  (S3)** (`retentionDays.archivedLogFiles`, default **0 = keep forever**),
  makes the sync expire bucket objects itself — which needs
  `s3:DeleteObject`; at 0 Cronomicon never deletes and a lifecycle rule may.
- **Private S3 nodes.** Any S3-compatible endpoint (`host[:port]`, empty for
  AWS), **Use SSL** off for plain HTTP, and a pasted **CA Bundle** (PEM) for
  an internal CA — stored, no container trust-store change, no restart. The
  backup uploader shares the client and gains `AMADEUS_BACKUP_S3_CA_FILE`.
  Static keys are both-or-neither; both empty uses the ambient AWS chain.
  The save **probes the bucket** with the credentials it would store and
  answers 422 with the S3 error rather than persisting a dead connection.
- **Observability.** `amadeus_log_archive_last_success_timestamp_seconds`,
  `amadeus_log_archive_failures_total`, `amadeus_log_archive_pending`; an
  `ERROR` log line on the third consecutive failed tick; one Activity row per
  tick that did work. The Log Storage card shows last sync, pending count and
  last error, and lists the archived tier beneath the disk classes.

### Changed

- `internal/backup` builds its MinIO client through `logarchive.NewClient`,
  so the SSRF egress guard and the IMDS credential carve-out are applied in
  exactly one place. `cronutil.UntilWallClock` is the shared wall-clock
  helper the retention sweep's `untilNext` now delegates to.
- `openapi.yaml`: `LogStorageConfig` gains `s3.useSsl`, `s3.caPem`, `sync`
  and the read-only `archive` status; `syncLogStorageNow`; `Run.logArchivedAt`;
  `getRunLog` loses the 302 and gains the 503; `AuditComplianceSettings`
  describes eleven knobs.
- Both manuals stamped v1.5.33: the administrator manual gains §8.6.1 and a
  restore step (reconcile after a snapshot restore); the user manual's
  Settings table describes the archive backend and the drawer field.

### Fixed

- The Log Storage card's daily-sync time is a plain HH:MM field: a native
  time picker rendered a clipped 12-hour "02:00 AM" in the browser's locale
  for a value that is 24-hour UTC.

### Notes

- Migration 1130's `log_archive_state` CHECK admits `expired`. Without it,
  expiring an object cleared the marker, put the run back in the pending
  set, and — with local 90d / archive 30d — re-uploaded what the window had
  just deleted.
- Test infrastructure: `internal/logarchive/fakes3`, an in-memory S3 that
  decodes minio-go's aws-chunked streaming-signature PUT bodies, plus a TLS
  variant for the CA-bundle case. `make test` needs no MinIO or network.

## [1.5.32] - 2026-09-09

### Changed

- **The Run confirmation window restates every declared input, defaults
  included** (RC-3). Since RC-2 the window listed only deviations — the
  settings the operator changed in the dialog — so a job whose answers all
  came from defaults confirmed with no inputs on screen at all. A default is
  exactly the value nobody typed in this dialog, which is why it most needs to
  be seen before it is sent. The window now opens with an **Inputs** list:
  every declared prompt, the value that will be sent, and where it came from
  — `(default)` quiet, `(you)` / `(override)` in the warning tone, and
  `(required — not filled)` when nothing will be sent. The rows come from the
  same run-summary model the "This run" rail renders, so the two surfaces
  cannot disagree about a value or its provenance. The deviations list is
  unchanged beneath it under a **Changed settings** heading (**Settings** when
  nothing changed); per-run environment overrides and added References stay
  only there, since they are already deviations and listing them twice
  teaches skipping. A job that declares no prompts sees the window exactly as
  before. The list carries its own role and label ("Inputs this run will use").

## [1.5.31] - 2026-09-09

The **Run dialog band** (RD/RC-2/SR): a visual pass over the ad-hoc Run
dialog that grew into a restructure of how a run is reviewed and confirmed,
plus a denser Score readout on the Dashboard. Frontend-only except for two
additive audit keys.

### Changed

- **The Run dialog is five top-level sections** (RD-5): **Inputs** (declared
  run inputs, per-run overrides, and References, which moved in from the old
  targeting fold — they are things the run *receives*), **Targets** (scope,
  host and group limits), **Method** (executor, runner pin, Connect as),
  **Timing** (the former "When to run") and **Advanced** (unchanged, still the
  quiet tone). "Where it runs" split at its own Targeting/Connection seam; the
  subheadings are gone because the sections now carry that meaning. The
  "This run" rail mirrors the same five names — Inputs / Targets / Method /
  Timing / Advanced — so the section an operator opens and the group that
  restates it share one word. The RV review gate for jobs with declared inputs
  now keys on **Targets** having been opened. Audit: `reviewedSections`
  records `targets` and `method` in place of `where-it-runs` (the server
  accepts both new keys and still accepts the old one from older clients;
  both spec copies carry the enum).
- **Every ad-hoc run goes through the confirmation window** (RC-2). The
  original two-tier scheme confirmed a default-settings run inline by pressing
  the armed "Run now" button twice — "Press again — all 4 hosts in Prod via
  SSH" — and only a deviating run got the window. Two presses of a button are
  not being told anything; the window is. The armed state, its six-second
  revert, the label and the settings signature that existed only to disarm a
  stale recap are all gone. A default-settings run shows the one-sentence
  statement of what will happen plus "No settings changed — this run uses the
  job exactly as configured." where the deviations list would sit. The
  paused-job rule (FX-Q1: a pause override must be confirmed through the
  window) is now simply the general case. Every confirmed run records
  `confirmation` in its audit metadata.
- **The confirmation window's deviation list is one bounded box**, not a stack
  of cards: a fixed label column lines the values up, hairlines separate rows,
  and the box scrolls on its own past ~40vh so a long list can never push
  Confirm off the panel or hide an entry. It carries a list role and label.
- **Modal polish, app-wide** (every dialog shares `Modal`). The scrolling body
  keeps a 14px gutter and a stable scrollbar gutter, so the bar no longer sits
  flush against right-aligned section summaries — the "cramped" feel the pass
  started from. A hairline under the title and another above the footer mark
  the scrollport's edges. The close glyph is a real `<button>` with an
  accessible "Close" label. The dialog surface is **translucent** — the panel
  colour at 88% over a 14px frosted blur, identical in both themes and on
  every dialog. A bottom fade was tried twice and removed twice: as a painted
  overlay it stacked the tint into a visibly denser band on the translucent
  surface, and as a mask it clipped the last row of a body too short to
  scroll (the confirm window lost its final deviation to it).
- **The Dashboard Score readout states more about each run** (SR-1). Hovering
  a set of dots used to list job · status · duration and leave the card mostly
  empty. Each row is now on a shared grid — name, status, **its own start time
  with seconds** (a "set of dots" is a cluster within one notehead's width, not
  one instant, so "did these run together or in sequence" is answerable),
  **how it was triggered** (by *person*, schedule *name*, reaction, token or
  file, workflow step), **executor and runner** ("SSH" or "Runner · name"; the
  runner name is resolved client-side from the runners list, which every
  session may read), duration, the **trace id** (shortened on screen, full
  value copies on click), and a **View run** link into History's trace deep
  link (a real href, so middle-click works). Projections carry none of the new
  columns and they collapse to nothing. Two pure helpers, `triggerLabel` and
  `executorLabel`, own the phrasing and are unit-tested; an unknown trigger
  kind is shown raw rather than relabelled. The rows are a real `<table>`
  with column heads (Job · Status · Started · Trigger · Executor · Duration ·
  Trace) that fills the card and opens out as the window widens, with the
  View-run column anchored to the right edge; a projection's table carries
  only Job · Status · Fires rather than labelling columns nothing fills.

### Fixed

- Two backend authorization tests hard-coded 2026-09-01 as a "future" deferral
  instant and began failing with 422 the day it passed. They now use a time
  relative to now.

### Docs

- Not yet reconciled: the user manual and operator training course still say
  "Where it runs" / "Run inputs" (fourteen places) and describe the armed
  second press in the "Run confirmation" section. One docs pass covers both.

## [1.5.30] - 2026-08-26

The **DR band** (DR-1..7): what a disaster
recovery actually depends on, found by drilling one and reading the code the
drill led to. None of it is about the database. Companion design in
the ha-disaster-recovery plan.

### Security

- **BREAKING (startup): a world-readable KEK file refuses to boot** (DR-6).
  `loadKEK` did a plain `os.ReadFile` and never looked at the mode, so a
  `0644` key that decrypts every stored secret loaded without a word. Now any
  *other* bit is fatal — the refusal names the file and the fix
  (`chmod 0400 <path>`, owned by the account the server runs as) — and any
  *group* bit warns once and continues. Evaluated at boot, not on the first
  secret operation hours later, and memoised so it costs one `Stat` per
  process. **Check the mode of `AMADEUS_KEK_FILE` before upgrading**: a
  deployment at `0644` will not start until it is fixed. An env-supplied
  `AMADEUS_KEK` has no mode and is not checked.
- **A job can no longer read the runner agent's own configuration** (DR-1).
  `env_passthrough` names were resolved straight out of the agent's environment
  with no denylist, so a job could name `AMADEUS_RUNNER_REGISTRATION_TOKEN` and
  be handed this runner's credentials — and because a passthrough value is not
  a declared secret binding, nothing registered it with the per-run redactor,
  so it printed in the run log in plaintext. Harmless while the only such value
  was a spent single-use `amt_reg_*`; a permanent leak the moment an operator
  adopts `AMADEUS_RUNNER_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN`. The `AMADEUS_RUNNER_*` namespace is
  now refused by **every** route to the child env — the passthrough loop,
  `-env-base-extra` (which reaches every child, not only runs declaring a
  passthrough), and the derived-reference bare-name fallback, which read a
  *different* key than the one denied and was found only by an adversarial
  pass over the finished diff. A denied name fails the run with its own error
  rather than the missing-var one, whose "set it as an env var" advice is
  exactly the wrong remedy. Nothing in the tree passed such a name, so the
  refusal breaks nothing today.

### Added

- **`amadeus rewrap-secrets` — KEK rotation can now be finished** (DR-5).
  Rotation was zero-downtime but *lazy*: a value moved to the new version only
  when rewritten, and there was no bulk re-wrap, so retiring a superseded key
  meant hand-touching every stored secret, every SSH credential and every
  settings integration. Until then the old key still decrypted everything
  untouched. The subcommand runs **online** from inside the deployment
  (`docker exec <amadeus> amadeus rewrap-secrets`), so the container's mounted
  KEK is used and no person handles key material; it is idempotent and covers
  all **three** stores — `secrets`, `ssh_credentials`, and the seven
  `EncryptString` settings columns (verified exhaustively against every call
  site, including `vault_config.role_id`, which is encrypted despite the
  name). `--dry-run` reports what is outstanding per store and version
  *without decrypting*, so it still answers "is rotation complete?" when the
  old key is gone — that answer is what licenses dropping `AMADEUS_KEK_<N>`. A
  row whose historical key is missing is named and counted rather than
  aborting the pass, and the command exits non-zero so a partial pass cannot
  read as complete. Re-wrapping is hygiene, not remediation: if the old key
  leaked, whoever held it held the plaintexts, and the fix is rotating the
  underlying credentials.
- **A re-registered runner is offered its lost placement back** (DR-7,
  migration **1120**). A runner that loses its identity — deregistered, or its
  row absent after a restore — re-registers with a *new* id, so its agency
  membership and tags, both keyed to the deleted id, are gone. It then reports
  online, advertises correct capabilities, and **silently changes which work
  it is eligible for**: dispatch is a disjoint two-branch rule, and a runner in
  no agency is the *general pool*, claiming every untagged run and no
  departmental one. Losing placement is an isolation change, not lost
  capacity. `runner_placement_history` now snapshots name, agencies, tags,
  capabilities and the observed client IP **before** the row is deleted — on
  *both* deletion paths, since the reaper's offline sweep (default 14 days) is
  the one that fires during an outage — inside the same transaction, because
  `runner_agencies` cascades with the row and a capture after the `DELETE`
  would record an empty set every time. The Runners view marks such a runner
  `general pool · was placed` and the expanded row offers **Restore
  placement**, naming every agency and tag it would apply and labelling each
  signal *observed* or *self-declared*. **Never applied automatically**: the
  name is chosen by the agent, so a silent heal would let any agent inherit
  another runner's placement by claiming its name. `POST
  /runners/{id}/placement` accepts it, gated on `configureApp` plus the
  ability to grant *every* agency named; one refusal fails the whole accept.
  `runners.last_client_ip` is stamped at registration and refreshed on the
  heartbeat, resolved through the trusted-proxy allowlist — never
  `RemoteAddr`, which behind a proxy is the proxy for every runner.
- **`runner-install.sh --token-file <path>` and `--token -`** (DR-2). The
  registration token was accepted only as an inline `-t` value, which lands in
  shell history and `ps` — a fair trade for a single-use 24-hour token, not
  for a bootstrap token that never expires. Mirrors the checkout token's
  existing file/hidden-prompt pair. `-t` still works and warns.
- `secrets.TokenKEKVersion` — reads an `EncryptString` token's KEK version
  without decrypting it.

### Changed

- **`amadeus-runner.env.example` stops teaching operators into an
  unrecoverable runner** (DR-3). It said "the token is dead after that first
  registration — you may blank this line", which is true and guarantees the
  runner cannot self-recover. The drill that opened this band showed the
  consequence: deregister a runner and it discards its key, re-registers, and
  fails `token_used` — offline until someone mints a token, edits the file and
  restarts the unit. The text now states both postures and their recovery
  cost, and points a bootstrap token at the agent's JSON config file, where a
  value never enters the process environment.
- **The restore runbook covers runner recovery** (DR-4). `backup-restore.md`
  ended at the file swap and the readyz check; it now says which runners
  resume on their own, which re-enroll and on what condition, that a
  re-registered runner returns *unbound* (and what that means for isolation),
  and how to verify from journald — the three log strings checked verbatim
  against the agent.
- Administrator manual **§6.6 "Recommended security posture"** is new, and
  `env-matrix.md`'s rotation procedure gained the re-wrap step. Its old
  `SELECT DISTINCT kek_version FROM secrets` check covered one store of three
  and would have declared victory with the other two still on the old key.
- Deleting a runner — by an operator or the reaper — now captures its
  placement first. A capture failure on the operator path aborts the
  deregistration (retryable); on the reaper path it leaves the runner for the
  next sweep.

### Fixed (review of this band before merge — the dr-readiness-fix plan)

- **Accepting a placement suggestion carried the manual path's target check
  but not its source gate**, so a departmental `configureApp` holder could pull
  a general-pool runner into their agency with one click when RF-Q3 forbids it
  by hand. The accept endpoint now runs the same `requireEntityAgency` as
  drain/resync/deregister; for the unbound runner a suggestion targets, that is
  unrestricted-only (DRF-9).
- Accepting or dismissing a suggestion, and deregistering a runner by either
  path, now write an activity row — the feed can answer "who placed / removed
  runner X?" (DRF-1, DRF-4). The reaper's row names the offline window.
- Restoring a placement **merges** tags with the runner's current ones rather
  than replacing them; a merge that breaks the tag caps is refused 422 rather
  than truncated (DRF-2).
- **Dismiss is durable.** It marks the snapshot on the server
  (`POST /runners/{id}/placement/dismiss`, columns folded into migration 1120
  before it shipped), so a dismissed placement is never offered again to any
  runner, on any reload (DRF-3).
- **Manual placement's feed row now says something.** `PUT /runner-agencies`
  wrote `membership-updated runner agencies` with no runner name — present,
  and invisible to the Actor/runner filter. It now writes one row per runner
  whose set *changed*, findable by `?runner=`, reading `agencies set: Carson,
  Reno` or `removed from all agencies (now general pool)`; the Change Log's
  request-level row keeps its vocabulary and gains details (DRF-5).

- **Runner placement history is the tenth retention knob.** Settings → Audit
  & Compliance gains `runnerPlacementHistory` (default **30 days** —
  deliberately shorter than the 90-day row windows, and counted from when the
  runner was *reaped*, so it adds to `AMADEUS_RUNNER_DEREGISTER_AFTER` rather
  than competing with it). A blob saved before the knob existed reads the
  default rather than 0, so upgrading cannot silently switch the table to
  keep-forever (DRF-7).

## [1.5.29] - 2026-08-25

### Changed

- **The Activity time frame is a Range select, not a one-way ratchet** (AS-2).
  AS-1's "Showing the last 72 hours · + Show older" pair had five faults, and
  the first is disqualifying: it could **widen but never narrow**, so the only
  way back to 72 hours was reloading the page. It also split one setting across
  two elements, hand-rolled an affordance where its two neighbours (Kind, Actor)
  are labelled `<Select>`s — against the "one component per vocabulary" rule —
  hid the 90-day ceiling until you hit it, and sat far right where it read as a
  page control rather than a filter. It is now a **Range** select beside the
  other two: Last 72 hours / 7 days / 30 days / 90 days (everything retained).
  Reversible, every option visible up front, ceiling stated rather than
  discovered. Net deletion: the button, its disabled state, its tooltip and its
  two empty-state copies all go.
- The empty state keeps an escape hatch, but it jumps **straight to the full
  retention** ("Search all 90 days") instead of stepping — an operator who found
  nothing wants to stop guessing at window sizes, not guess again one size up.

### Added

- **A custom absolute range** (AS-2). "Custom range…" reveals From/To
  `datetime-local` inputs and finally sends **`?to=`** — the half of the
  endpoint's range support that had never been wired by anything. "What
  happened on the 14th?" is a real operator question no relative window can
  express. **Either end may be blank**: the server treats `from`/`to`
  independently, so "everything since the 14th" and "everything before the
  14th" are both valid queries rather than an incomplete form. The inputs name
  the zone they take input in (the browser's), because the app can be
  configured to DISPLAY another and the offset would otherwise be silent.
  Conversion follows the AR run-scheduler's existing datetime-local seam rather
  than inventing a second convention.
- A relative window deliberately sends **no `to=`**: it means "…until now", and
  freezing the upper edge at page-load time would silently hide every event
  that arrived afterwards.

## [1.5.28] - 2026-08-25

### Added

- **The Activity page can be filtered by person or runner** (AA-3; the AA band
  is now CLOSED). An **Actor** dropdown sits beside Kind, grouped
  **Users / Runners / System** from `GET /activity/actors` and scoped to the
  same window as the feed — widen the window with **+ Show older** and the
  menu widens with it. Empty groups are omitted rather than rendered as a
  heading over nothing.
- **One filter, two affordances.** The picker and the **My triggers** chip are
  the same filter, so each clears the other: leaving both set would send
  `actor=<me>` AND `runner=<x>`, which the API honours as an AND — a query no
  click asked for. Option values carry their group (`u:`/`r:`/`s:`), so which
  param a choice sends is decided by where it came from, not re-derived from
  the string; a runner and a user sharing a name can never produce the wrong
  query.
- **A runner chip on every card that has one.** The runner shows by NAME.
  Where the actor is the redundant `runner:<id>`, it demotes to the chip's
  tooltip rather than printing a UUID — but on a run an operator STOPPED, both
  the person and the runner show, because both facts are true and neither
  displaces the other. This is the readable half of what the original
  "sort by runner" request would have bought: the eye finds the runner without
  sorting a chronological feed.
- The filtered empty state names who it searched for ("No activity by
  `runner-east` in the last 72 hours") and **Clear filters** resets the picker.

## [1.5.27] - 2026-08-25

### Added

- **`GET /activity/actors`** (AA-2) — the option list for the Activity feed's
  actor filter, grouped **users / runners / system**. Classification is
  server-side so no client grows its own copy of "does this actor look like a
  person": users contain `@`, runners come from `runner_name` (never from
  parsing `actor`), and everything else is the fixed system vocabulary.
  Window-scoped via the same `from`/`to` as the feed (AA-Q5), so the picker
  offers the population the feed is showing rather than every runner that ever
  polled. Empty groups serialize as `[]`, never `null`.
- **`GET /activity?runner=`** — exact match on `runner_name`, composing with
  every other filter. Independent of `actor` rather than an alternative
  spelling of it: the picker sends one or the other, but both set is a legal
  query, and both must then match.
- `ActivityEntry.runnerName` on the wire; both spec copies updated and the
  frontend client regenerated.

### Fixed

- **Stopped runs now carry a runner name** (the gap AA-1 recorded). The kill
  handler writes its run-end row with the OPERATOR's email as the actor, so
  migration 1100's `actor LIKE 'runner:%'` backfill predicate never matched it
  — meaning "everything runner X ran" silently excluded exactly the runs
  somebody intervened in. Two halves: the handler now resolves the runner
  through the `runs`/`runners` join it was already querying (a LEFT JOIN — an
  SSH run and an unclaimed queued run both stay NULL), and **migration 1110**
  re-backfills history on the right predicate. `runs.runner_id` is authoritative
  about where a run executed, whoever happened to write the activity row;
  keying on the actor was a proxy for a different question. 1110 is idempotent
  (`runner_name IS NULL`) and its down is a deliberate no-op — nothing
  distinguishes a row it stamped from one 1100 stamped, so unstamping would
  corrupt the column; reverting the column is 1100's down.
- A runner's raw `runner:<uuid>` actor no longer falls into the actors
  endpoint's `system` group. The runner is already offered by NAME, and the
  catch-all branch was absorbing the exact unreadable value the band exists to
  replace — caught by an exclusion assertion, since every positive assertion
  passed against the bug.

## [1.5.26] - 2026-08-25

### Added

- **`activity.runner_name` — a runner you can read** (AA-1, migration **1100**,
  the activity-actors plan). Activity had no runner column: both
  identities an operator searches by (the person, the machine) lived in
  `actor`, where a runner appears as `runner:<uuid>` — filterable, unreadable.
  The new column is a **snapshot**, deliberately not an FK: a runner can be
  deregistered by the RL-band reaper, and `ON DELETE SET NULL` would erase the
  answer at exactly the moment someone asks what the retired runner ran. Same
  reasoning as `runs.agency` (450) and `runs.entity_code` (710). `actor` keeps
  its `runner:<id>` meaning untouched — the audit stream reads it, and renaming
  there would be a silent contract change (AA-Q6).
- Nine writers stamp it: run-start (claim) and run-end (finalize) resolve it
  once through the new `runnerNameOf` helper; the reaper and drain-timeout
  sweeps resolve it **once per sweep, outside their per-run loops**; drain,
  keyscan, resync-request, resync-declare and the re-admit notice already held
  the name and pass it straight through. The two `token.go` writers target the
  runners *collection* (a registration token binds to no runner until used) and
  are deliberately unstamped.
- Migration 1100 backfills in the 1010 tradition — **stamp only where the join
  is exact**: run rows through `runs.runner_id`, lifecycle rows by stripping the
  `runner:` prefix already in `target`. A run whose runner is gone stays NULL
  rather than acquiring a guess, and the test asserts that refusal on three
  separate shapes. Adds `idx_activity_runner_at` (partial) and
  `idx_activity_actor_at` — the latter unrelated to runners: `?actor=` has been
  a supported filter since the endpoint shipped and every "My triggers" click
  was a full table scan.

### Fixed

- `internal/gitlab`'s test fixture hand-rolls the `activity` table instead of
  running migrations, so it silently drifted from the real schema again — the
  shared writer's INSERT names every column, SQLite compiles the whole
  statement up front, and a subset table therefore breaks **every** activity
  write in that package (best-effort writes, so the symptom surfaces somewhere
  unrelated — here, `TestRecordPush`). The fixture's own comment already warned
  about this for migrations 030 and 1010; it now warns for 1100 and says the
  rule out loud.

## [1.5.25] - 2026-08-25

### Fixed

- **Operator-initiated runner actions recorded no operator** (AA-4,
  the activity-actors plan). `HandleDrain`, `HandleKeyscan` and
  `HandleResync` wrote the LITERAL string `"operator"` as the activity actor
  while holding an authenticated session — the identity was in scope via
  `auth.IdentityFrom` and thrown away — so "who drained runner X?" was
  unanswerable from the feed for every runner-lifecycle event. The host-key
  APPROVAL handler in the same file (`keyscan.go`) had always resolved it
  correctly; the three request handlers never adopted the two lines above it.
  That code is now the package helper `sessionActor(r)` (`service.go`) and all
  three call it. `operator` survives ONLY as the no-session fallback — these
  routes are session-gated at the mux, so it cannot fire in real traffic, and
  a writer that cannot know the actor should say so rather than assert a name
  it guessed. An identity carrying an empty email now also falls back, so the
  actor column is never written blank.

### Changed

- The two already-correct copies of the same three lines
  (`token.go` — registration-token mint and revoke) collapse onto
  `sessionActor` as well, so there is one implementation rather than three
  and a half. No behaviour change at those two sites.

## [1.5.24] - 2026-08-25

### Fixed

- **Activity search only ever searched the newest 50 events** (AS-1). The
  page fetched bare `/activity` — page 1 at the default `pageSize` of 50 —
  and ran its search box and "My triggers" chip over that array in the
  browser. There was no pager and no count, so a search for anything older
  returned silence with nothing to say a boundary existed. The empty state
  promised "the last 72 hours"; nothing implemented that window on either
  side. Meanwhile the endpoint had carried `q`, `kind`, `actor`, `scope`,
  `from`/`to` and `page`/`pageSize` since its first cut — six filters and a
  pager, all built, none wired. Same shape as v1.5.23's Jobs fix: the
  capability existed, the path the user was on did not reach it.

### Changed

- **Activity is server-searched and server-paged** (AS-1). Every control is a
  query param now: the search box is a debounced `?q=` (spans the whole
  window, not the page), a **Kind** dropdown sends `?kind=` over the seven
  wire kinds (start/end pairs kept separate — the outcome badge only exists
  on the end row, so "which runs failed" is a run-end question), **My
  triggers** sends `?actor=<me>` (it waits for `/me` so the first query is
  never sent blind), and a `Pager` reads the filtered `totalItems` so
  "1–25 of 312 events" is a true statement about the search.
- **A real retention window, one step at a time.** The feed opens on
  `?from=` 72h ago — now a fact about the query, not the empty-state copy —
  and **+ Show older** widens it 72h → 7d → 30d → 90d. At the widest step
  the control disables with the reason (FX-7) rather than vanishing. The
  empty state names the window it searched and offers the widen there too.
- The `All` / `My triggers` chips are keyboard-reachable `role="button"`
  toggles with `aria-pressed`; they were bare clickable spans.
- Repeat-collapsing (VU-13) now groups per **page**: an identical run that
  straddles a page boundary renders as one collapsed row on each side —
  honest, if plain — rather than being folded across a boundary the feed
  never showed.

## [1.5.23] - 2026-08-25

### Fixed

- **The Jobs catalog lands unsorted** (TS-24). The Jobs page opens in *browse*
  mode — the folder tree, before you type anything into the search box — and
  browse mode never sorted. Two independent faults stacked into one symptom:

  1. `jobDisplayPath` fell back to `jobName(j)`, which resolves to the **DB
     id**. An amadeus-authored job has no `sourcePath`, so every such job
     entered the folder tree labelled with a **UUIDv7** — and UUIDv7 is
     time-ordered, so the default view listed jobs in *creation* order while
     the NAME column rendered `metadata.name`. On screen that reads as no
     order at all. `Workflows` and `Schedules` always fell back to the name;
     Jobs was the only catalog that did not. It now falls back to `j.name`,
     with `jobName` still supplying tree *identity* via `getName`.
  2. Browse mode rendered its shared header with `sortEnabled={false}`, so
     there were no carets and no way to sort by any column without first
     typing a search term.

  The default sort spec (`{ key: "name", dir: "asc" }`) had been correct since
  v0.55.9 — it just never reached the view an operator actually lands on.

### Changed

- **Browse mode sorts, in all four folder-tree catalogs** (TS-24 — Jobs,
  Workflows, Scripts, Schedules). `childrenOf` takes `leafOrder`, and
  `FolderBrowser` takes `preserveLeafOrder`: a catalog hands in its
  already-sorted rows and the tree renders each folder's leaves in that order
  instead of re-sorting them by label. **Folders stay alpha-first regardless**
  — they carry none of the row columns, so a column sort over them means
  nothing. This reverses TS-8's "a column sort is meaningless against the
  folder tree", which was true only of the folders, not of the leaves inside
  the open one. `TableHead`'s `sortEnabled` prop survives for callers
  rendering the header over rows they do not control, but nothing in the app
  passes `false` today, and the `tableHeader(sortEnabled)` helpers in
  Workflows/Schedules lost their now-dead parameter.

## [1.5.22] - 2026-08-24

### Changed

- **One writer for `runs`** (RR-2/RR-3,
  the run-row-unification plan; band CLOSED). Every producer now
  builds a `scheduler.RunRow` and calls `scheduler.InsertRun` — the single
  `INSERT INTO runs` in production code. `RunRow` embeds `EnqueueParams` and
  adds what the other writers needed: `Status`/`QueuedReason`, `Terminal` (a
  suppressed fire or skipped step: `started_at = completed_at = created_at`,
  and NO dispatch-policy snapshot — a row that cannot dispatch carries none),
  `SuppressedByCalendar`, `CreatedAt` (the missed-run detector's override),
  `Kind`, `EntityCode` and `DurationMs`. Post-insert side effects (the
  RA-20(b) stamp, `run_agencies` materialization) stay in their callers.
  `EnqueueRun` is now a one-line wrapper over `EnqueueRunWithID`; both names
  survive for their callers, but there is one body.

  **Six writers, not five.** Converting surfaced one the survey had missed:
  `api/ssh_test_run.go`, the "Test connection" probe mirrored into History as
  a `kind='ssh-test'` row. It is a genuinely different row (no job, system
  entity code, measured duration, NULL `job_source`), so `RunRow` grew the
  three fields rather than the conformance test growing an exemption.

  Proof: all eight RR-1 goldens unchanged, byte for byte, across the
  conversion — the sixth was cut against the old writer first.
  `run_writer_conformance_test.go` (RR-3) walks `internal/` and `cmd/` and
  fails the build if a second `INSERT INTO runs` appears outside seed data
  and tests; its failure message says to add the field to `RunRow`, not a
  new INSERT. Net −150 lines in the two engine files.

## [1.5.21] - 2026-08-24

### Fixed

- **Scheduled runs now explain why they cannot be claimed** (RR-0d,
  the run-row-unification plan). RA-20(b)'s advisory
  `queued_reason` stamp ("no runner is online", "no runner carries tag X",
  …) was applied by the manual/token path and the workflow engine but never
  by cron's `EnqueueRun` — the highest-volume producer. A scheduled fire
  queued with no eligible runner sat with a blank reason while the same job
  clicked from the Run dialog explained itself. Found by RR-1's parity
  golden; diagnostics only, dispatch unchanged.

### Added

- **Byte-identity goldens for every `runs` writer** (RR-1). A new test-support
  package `internal/rowgolden` snapshots a complete row — all 45 columns,
  NULL kept distinct from `''` — and compares it to a checked-in
  `testdata/*.golden`. Seven goldens cover the five producers (cron fire,
  manual/token enqueue, the explicit-unpin variant, suppressed scheduled
  fire, workflow step child run, skipped workflow step) against a job seeded
  with every column a writer reads, plus a parity test holding `EnqueueRun`
  and `EnqueueRunWithID` to the same row for the same params. These are the
  net under RR-2: the refactor is correct iff no golden changes. Regenerate
  with `ROWGOLDEN_UPDATE=1`; a golden diff is a behaviour diff and is
  reviewed as one.

## [1.5.20] - 2026-08-24

### Added

- **A linter, gating new code** (GM-4,
  the go-modernization plan). `backend/.golangci.yml` enables ten
  linters — `govet`, `staticcheck`, `errcheck`, `ineffassign`, `unused`,
  `gosec`, `bodyclose`, `contextcheck`, `errorlint`, `modernize` (the last
  keeps GM-3's sweep from regressing). CI's new `lint` job runs with
  `--new-from-rev`, so a finding fails only when it sits on a line the branch
  touched; the pre-existing backlog (168 findings at introduction) is visible
  via `make lint` and blocks nothing. `errcheck` excludes read-side `Close`
  (an already-succeeded read has nothing actionable to report) but
  deliberately keeps write-side `Close` — `*os.File` opened for writing,
  `*sql.Tx`, `*ssh.Session` — where a short write surfaces.

### Fixed

- **26 `err == sql.ErrNoRows` comparisons became `errors.Is`** across 22 files.
  All 26 were correct today — every one reads an error straight from
  `Row.Scan`, which returns the sentinel unwrapped — so this fixes no live
  bug. It removes a pattern that breaks silently the moment any of those reads
  moves behind a helper that wraps with `%w`, which is the kind of change
  nobody thinks to audit for.
- Two `staticcheck` findings in tests: a determinism check written as
  `f(x) != f(x)` (worked, but read as a tautology) and an
  `if _, _ = f(); true { }` empty branch. Both now say what they mean.
- A stray empty statement in `sshexec.track`, left by GM-3's `wg.Go` rewrite.

## [1.5.19] - 2026-08-24

### Changed

- **Go 1.26 idioms across the backend** (GM-3,
  the go-modernization plan). One mechanical, behaviour-preserving
  pass with the upstream `modernize` analyzer, 126 files, net −146 lines.
  395 findings → **0**. Nothing here changes runtime behaviour; the commit is
  deliberately isolated so it can be skipped in `git blame` and reverted whole.

  The bulk: `interface{}` → `any` (182), C-style loops → `range n` (35), manual
  search loops → `slices.Contains` (22), `m[k]=v` loops → `maps.Copy` (17),
  `range strings.Split` → `SplitSeq` (17), `errors.As` → `errors.AsType[T]`
  (21), `wg.Add(1)`/`go func` → `wg.Go` (9), `Index`/`SplitN`/`HasPrefix+
  TrimPrefix` → `Cut`/`CutPrefix`/`CutSuffix` (15), plus `min`/`max`,
  `atomic.Int32`, `slices.Sorted`, `reflect.TypeFor` and `slices.Backward`.

  Done by hand alongside it:
  - **Twelve pointer helpers deleted.** `ptr`, `strp`, `strptr`, `intp`,
    `intp2`, `boolp`, `slicep` — seven names for "take a pointer to this
    value", spread across seven test packages. Go 1.26's `new(expr)` replaces
    all of them, which is the same one-vocabulary rule the frontend atoms
    follow.
  - **`sshexec.fanOut`** drops its pre-1.22 `go func(i, t)` parameter passing
    for `wg.Go`, with a comment noting the semaphore acquire stays *outside*
    the goroutine — that is what bounds fan-out.
  - **`poll_claim_bench_test.go`** uses `for b.Loop()`, keeping an explicit
    index since the body rotates through runner fixtures.

  `notify.Dispatcher.send` was deliberately left alone: its `wg.Add(1)` is
  conditional, so it is not the `wg.Go` shape, and the "synchronous Add so it
  can't race a concurrent Wait()" comment still describes what it does.

  Verified: `make verify` green under `-race` (36 packages, no data races),
  `modernize ./...` reports zero, and the diff touches only `.go` files.

## [1.5.18] - 2026-08-24

### Changed

- **The build gates tell the truth** (GM-2,
  the go-modernization plan). Three changes to how the tree is
  checked, no runtime change:
  - **`make verify` now runs `go test -race`**, matching what CI has always
    run. The target's own comment claimed it mirrored CI while running the
    race detector's opposite; a tree with ~30 goroutine launch sites, 20
    mutexes and a bounded-parallelism workflow engine was leaving race
    detection to the push. `make test-fast` is the no-race inner loop, and
    is deliberately not a gate.
  - **CI gained a `vuln` job** running `govulncheck`, hard-failing on a
    vulnerability *reachable* from Cronomicon code. Nothing had ever run it;
    GM-1 found nine reachable advisories on the first try. Findings in
    required-but-uncalled modules are reported without failing.
  - **`make vuln`** runs the same check locally. It is deliberately NOT part
    of `verify`, which must work on an air-gapped build box — `govulncheck`
    fetches the vulnerability DB at run time. It is now a release-time item
    in `deploy/go-no-go.md`, because the DB moves independently of the code:
    a commit that was clean when merged can be affected by an advisory
    published afterwards.

## [1.5.17] - 2026-08-24

### Fixed

- **Workflow steps and non-cron runs were dispatched on incomplete policy**
  (RR-0, the run-row-unification plan). Runner claim and the
  manifest read dispatch policy from the **run row**, and two of the five
  `INSERT INTO runs` writers had drifted from the others:
  - **RR-0a** — the RA-20a `become-file` requirement (v0.57.3) was injected
    only by the cron path (`EnqueueRun`). Manual, token, file-watch and
    promoted-pending runs of a become-password job (`EnqueueRunWithID`)
    could be claimed by a pre-v9 runner and 409 at manifest time — the
    exact failure RA-20a was written to prevent. Both producers are now
    pinned to the same answer by a parity test.
  - **RR-0b** — workflow child runs carried no `requires_json`,
    `checkout_sha` or `checkout_entry`. A step whose job required `vault`,
    a collection, a checkout project or a become password was claim-gated
    on nothing and handed to any runner in the agency.
  - **RR-0c** — workflow child runs carried no `runner_tag`. A job pinned
    to a tag (RT, v1.3.x) ran **unpinned** as a workflow step.

  **Operator note.** After this release a workflow step whose job requires
  a capability or a runner tag will **wait** for a runner that satisfies
  it, where before it ran on any runner in the agency and failed later (or
  ran somewhere the pin was meant to exclude). A department whose
  workflows "worked" because a capable runner happened to be online will
  now see those steps park while it is offline — the run's
  `queued_reason` names what it is waiting for. This is the documented
  contract; the previous behaviour was the bug.

## [1.5.16] - 2026-08-24

### Security

- **Dependency bumps closing nine reachable vulnerabilities** (GM-1,
  the go-modernization plan). The first `govulncheck` run
  against the tree found nine advisories reachable from Cronomicon code, all
  in two modules, all fixed by patch-level upgrades with no API change:
  - `golang.org/x/crypto` v0.51.0 → **v0.55.0** — GO-2026-5013, 5015,
    5017, 5018, 5019, 5020 (`x/crypto/ssh` panics, deadlocks and DoS on
    `NewClientConn` / `Session.Run` / `ParsePrivateKey`, reached from the
    SSH executor, the runner agent's dialer and the SSH credential store's
    validate-on-save), and **GO-2026-5021** — `knownhosts` did not enforce
    `@revoked` entries. That last one sits under the host-key pinning
    contract (bastion pinning, migration 640; the id-qualified TOFU
    capture in `sshexec/conn.go`): a revoked host key was still accepted.
  - `github.com/go-git/go-git/v5` v5.19.1 → **v5.19.2** — GO-2026-6213
    (worktree operations followed symlinks; reached from the Git-sync
    clone/reset/submodule path that the secret scan and both executors
    consume) and GO-2026-6214 (path traversal via crafted reference names;
    reached from the publish path's commit and push).

  Four direct dependencies one minor behind rode along: `go-oidc`
  v3.18→v3.20, `go-sqlite3` v1.14.45→.50 (bundled SQLite bump — the full
  migration up/down suite is the regression net), `minio-go` v7.2→v7.3,
  `prometheus/client_golang` v1.20.5→v1.24.1. Transitives via `go mod tidy`.
  `govulncheck` now reports zero reachable vulnerabilities. The CI job that
  keeps it that way is GM-2, next.

## [1.5.15] - 2026-08-20

### Added

- **Python usage guide** (`/python-guide.html`, PY1.0). The run type had been
  first-class since migration 490 with no guide beside its Ansible/Bash/
  PowerShell siblings. Shaped like the PowerShell guide — shared shell-family
  plumbing stated briefly with deep links into the Bash guide, depth only
  where Python differs: the `python3 -c` / `python3 -` + `os.environ`-prelude
  invocation (env over stdin, never argv), why `input()` raises `EOFError`
  (the program IS the stdin) and run inputs replace it, the exception-exit
  honesty model (`except: pass` is the anti-pattern, not silent failure), the
  variable-detection heuristic (`os.environ['X']` = required, `getenv` with a
  default = optional), the fleet's-oldest-interpreter rule, stdlib-first
  dependencies, secrets off child argv, and a Python-specific troubleshooting
  table. Registered everywhere the other guides live: the wrap pipeline
  (`GUIDES`), the palette guard (`DOC_FILES`), both manuals' sidebar Guides
  sections, the Bash guide's companion line, and `guideForRunType` — so the
  Composer's Script field now links it when a Python script is selected,
  covered by the doc-link drift guard.
