## 0.52.2 — Agency membership tables + the pre-flight report (Agencies Phase 2)

**Date:** Jul 26, 2026

Phase 2 of the agencies plan (decisions **AG-Q2b**, **AG-Q5**, **AG-Q6**,
**AG-Q9**; tasks T2.1–T2.12). **Schema v680** (migrations `670_agency_membership`,
`680_runs_agencies_json`).

Four entity types carry isolation by **four different mechanisms on two unrelated
axes**: runners are M:N with agencies, scopes are 1:1, secrets and variables are keyed
by *scope* and are not on the agency axis at all, and SSH keys have no isolation
whatsoever. Answering "will this job get this secret?" means holding five facts at once.
This release puts every one of them on the same axis.

**It changes no behavior, on purpose.** The tables exist and are backfilled, but nothing
dispatches or resolves against them: `claimRun` still matches the scalar `runs.agency`
and reference resolution still runs on scope. That is not a half-finished state — it is
the point of splitting Phases 2 and 3. It makes this release reversible, and it lets the
pre-flight report below be read against **real production data** before any predicate
changes. Merging the two phases would mean discovering AG-Q5's tightening in production
instead of in a report.

Backend `go test ./...` + `go vet` green; frontend `tsc -b`, **226** vitest and full
build green; both `openapi.yaml` copies byte-identical + client regenerated;
`backend/web/dist` rebuilt; Administrator Manual §6.1c added; verified end-to-end in the
running app (seeded membership, a report that fires on both halves, the dual-written run
snapshot, and the inertness check).

> ### ⚠️ Upgrade note
>
> - **Nothing changes on deploy.** No run dispatches differently and no reference
>   resolves differently. If you observe otherwise, that is a bug, not the design —
>   `TestPhase2ChangesNoResolution` asserts it directly.
> - **Run the pre-flight report before you upgrade past this release.**
>   `GET /api/v1/agency-preflight` (ConfigureApp) lists every binding that works today
>   and would stop working under Phase 3, split into `referenceFindings` (AG-Q1(b)) and
>   `keyFindings` (**AG-Q5 — a tightening**: today any job may bind any key, so a working
>   key binding can stop).
> - **An empty report right after upgrading is expected and is NOT a safety signal.** The
>   backfill deliberately assigns no membership that narrows anything, so the report has
>   nothing to bite on yet. Read `membershipAssigned` alongside the findings; it acquires
>   teeth only as you assign membership.
> - **`runs.agency` and `scopes.agency_id` are dual-written for one release**, so a
>   rolled-back server reads a correct scalar and stays entirely correct. Both are dropped
>   in Phase 3's migration 690, once no reader remains.
> - **The 670 down-migration loses only membership rows** — never a scope, secret,
>   variable or key. Membership that has *diverged* from `scopes.agency_id` since the
>   migration is the one thing a down cannot reconstruct.

### Added

- **Migration `670_agency_membership` (T2.1/T2.2).** `scope_agencies`,
  `secret_agencies`, `env_var_agencies` and `ssh_credential_agencies`, each mirroring
  `runner_agencies` (mig. 440) exactly: composite PK, `ON DELETE CASCADE` on both FKs,
  plus an index on the agency side for the delete guard and the Phase-4 matrix.

  The backfill is behavior-preserving **by construction**, and the cases that matter are
  the ones an "obvious" backfill gets wrong. A **scoped** secret/variable inherits the
  agency of the scope it names — that scope's agency is the one membership that changes
  nothing, since such a row is reachable today exactly by runs in that scope. An
  **unscoped (global)** row gets **no rows at all**: an empty set means "no agency
  restriction" under AG-Q1(b), and that is precisely what keeps a global secret global.
  Giving global rows membership in every agency would be a different predicate with a
  different failure mode. **SSH keys get none** either — `ssh_credentials` has no scope
  to infer from, and backfilling would enact AG-Q5's tightening a release early, before
  the report an operator is meant to read first.
- **Migration `680_runs_agencies_json` (T2.3, AG-Q2b).** `runs.agencies_json`, the SET
  form of the per-run agency snapshot, backfilled from the scalar (`NULL`/`''` → `[]`,
  else a single-element array). A JSON array rather than a join table because it
  **mirrors `runs.requires_json`, which already does exactly this `json_each`
  intersection inside the very same claim query** — a proven pattern in a proven place —
  and because it preserves mig. 450's deliberate denormalization, so re-homing a scope
  cannot silently retarget runs that are already queued. `NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'` so
  `json_each` never has to special-case NULL. The backfill uses `json_array()`, not
  string concatenation: an agency name containing a quote or backslash would otherwise
  produce invalid JSON, and invalid JSON there makes `json_each` throw **inside the claim
  query**, which stops dispatch fleet-wide. `TestMigrate680RoundTrip` pins that case.
- **`PUT`/`GET /api/v1/{scope,secret,env-var,ssh-credential}-agencies` (T2.6).**
  Replace-per-row membership matrices mirroring `PUT /runner-agencies`. Every entity and
  agency id is validated **before any write**, so a bad id cannot leave half a bulk
  matrix applied (422 `unknown_member` / `unknown_agency`). One generic store behind all
  four, so the four cannot drift apart.
- **`GET /api/v1/agency-preflight` (T2.12).** The report described in the upgrade note,
  computed against live data. It resolves each binding through the **same scope
  predicate** dispatch uses — a report that ignored scope precedence would describe a
  system that does not exist — and reports script-owned bindings as a **count** rather
  than a guess, because a script has no scope of its own.
- **Audit on every membership change (T2.7).** Membership decides which runs can reach
  which secrets, so it belongs in `change_log` next to the agency CRUD it sits beside.
  Ids and counts only, capped so a bulk matrix save cannot write an unbounded row.
- **`execspec.ScopeAgencies` + `MarshalAgencies` (T2.5).** The N:M successor to
  `ScopeAgency`, and the source of the `agencies_json` snapshot written at both enqueue
  sites alongside the scalar. Sorted, so two enqueues of the same scope produce
  byte-identical JSON.
- **Tests.** Migration round-trips for both 670 and 680 (backfill correctness including
  every "gets no rows" case, cascade on both sides, down/up idempotence, the JSON
  escaping case); membership round-trip across all four kinds with fail-closed
  validation; the dual-write in **both** directions; the delete guard per entity kind;
  a git-sync membership-preservation test; six pre-flight cases; and
  **`TestPhase2ChangesNoResolution`**, which assigns membership that *would* break a
  reference under Phase 3 and asserts the reference still resolves today. If that one
  ever fails, a predicate has been switched on early and the report is no longer a
  preview but a post-mortem.

### Changed

- 🔴 **The agency delete guard now counts membership (T2.8).** It previously counted only
  scope and runner references, so an agency whose only members were a **secret** and a
  **key** deleted cleanly — and the `ON DELETE CASCADE` dropped that membership with no
  409 and nothing to notice. The scope case was caught before only because
  `scopes.agency_id` happens to have no cascade, which is luck rather than design.
- **Git sync must neither insert nor delete `scope_agencies` rows (T2.9/AG-Q6).** The
  join table inherits the rule that has always governed `scopes.agency_id`. A sync that
  "reconciled" membership would silently drop every operator assignment on **every pull**,
  because the scope upsert runs against every scope on every sync — total and immediate
  damage. There is deliberately no reconciliation code; `TestSyncPreservesScopeAgencies`
  pins its absence over two consecutive syncs and covers the multi-agency case the
  `agency_id` test structurally cannot.
- **`seed.go` seeds the join tables (T2.10)** from a single scope→agency map that feeds
  both the legacy column and the new table, so dev preview can never show a database
  where the two disagree. Adds a second SSH key so the Phase-4 matrix has one per agency
  — operator-assigned membership, since the migration deliberately backfills none.

### Deviation from the plan

- **T2.6 specifies `ManageEnvVars`; the endpoints ship ConfigureApp-gated.** Membership is
  an isolation-zone assignment, and every sibling operation on that axis — the agency
  catalog, runner membership, the scope binding — is already ConfigureApp, including the
  `PUT /runner-agencies` precedent the plan itself points at. Gating the secret side on
  the weaker permission would let a secrets manager re-home a zone an admin owns, and
  would be an outright privilege inversion for SSH keys, whose own CRUD is ConfigureApp.
  One axis, one gate.

### Not in this phase

The Phase-3 predicate switch — `claimRun` on the `agencies_json` intersection (behind its
benchmark gate), `runref` on the AG-Q1(b) predicate, the AG-Q5 key tightening, and
migration 690 dropping `runs.agency` / `scopes.agency_id` — is untouched, as is the
Phase-4 membership matrix UI. **There is no UI for membership yet**: the endpoints are
live and the tables are populated, but the at-a-glance surface is Phase 4 (T4.1). For now
membership is assigned through the API, which is the right shape for a phase whose
findings are meant to be reviewed before anything is switched on.

## 0.52.1 — Reference bindings become legible before a run (Agencies Phase 1)

**Date:** Jul 26, 2026

Phase 1 of the agencies plan (decisions **AG-Q4**, **AG-Q9**; tasks
T1.0–T1.12). **No schema change.**

An operator lost a debugging session to an ansible job that would not run. The chain was
five correct behaviors in a row, and the last one is the subject of this release: a job
declares a reference binding, **nothing checks it**, and the first signal is a failed run
whose message deliberately withholds the distinguishing fact — *"reference
`AMADEUS_SECRET_RH8_BECOME_PASS` is unavailable for this run"*. Typo or scope mismatch?
The message will not say, by design.

That design is right **for runs** and is unchanged here. What was never weighed is the
**authoring** surface, where the operator is looking at the job editor and can already
list the rows in question. So the same question is now answered where the binding is
declared, before any run exists — and answered precisely.

Backend `go test ./...` + `go vet` green; frontend `tsc -b`, **226** vitest (11 new)
and full build green; both `openapi.yaml` copies byte-identical + client regenerated;
`backend/web/dist` rebuilt; both manuals reconciled.

> ### ⚠️ Note on what the validator will and will not tell you
>
> - **The oracle rule is not relaxed — it is replaced with a tighter one.**
>   `runref.OperatorMessage` still collapses out-of-scope and missing into one sentence on
>   the run surface (M2), so a run cannot be used to probe secret names one run at a time.
>   The new validator is bound by a different, mechanical rule: **it may reveal nothing
>   the caller's own `GET /env-vars` / `GET /env-secrets` would not already show them.**
> - **Precision therefore degrades row by row, not actor by actor.** Both of those lists
>   are scope-filtered per actor, so a row living in a scope you may not read comes back
>   as the generic `not_found`, byte-identical to a name that exists nowhere. A restricted
>   actor keeps full precision for the scopes they *can* read.
> - **T1.0 was verified, not assumed.** `handleListEnvVars` filters on
>   `auth.ScopeReadable`; `GET /env-secrets` filters through
>   `secrets.Service.List(grant.CanRead)`. The validator inherits exactly that predicate.
> - **No value is ever returned**, in any form, and a validation never decrypts key
>   material — the key verdict is pure existence.

### Added

- **`POST /api/v1/references/validate` (T1.1/T1.2).** Body `{scope, references[]}` →
  one `{ok, outcome, reason, resolvedScope, otherScopes}` verdict per reference, in
  request order. `outcome` is `resolved` | `out_of_scope` | `not_found` | `invalid`.
  Session-gated rather than `ManageEnvVars`-gated — the verdict is bounded by the
  caller's own visibility, and the chips must render for the read-only operators who look
  at job detail. CSRF-gated despite being read-only, so a cross-origin page cannot probe
  names against a live session; capped at 200 references per request. A `scope` the
  caller may not read is `403`.
- **`runref.Validate` / `ValidateAll` reuse the dispatch predicate, they do not
  reimplement it.** `lookupScopedID` was refactored into `lookupScoped`, which now also
  returns the winning row's scope; both the resolver and the validator call it. A ✓ at
  authoring time and a successful injection therefore cannot disagree —
  `TestValidateAgreesWithDispatch` asserts that across {global, in-scope, out-of-scope,
  missing} × {global, dev, prod} run scopes.
- **`GET /api/v1/reference-usage` (T1.9).** Per-reference counts of the jobs and scripts
  that bind it. Job counts are scope-filtered to the caller's grants (an unfiltered count
  would let a restricted actor infer that an out-of-scope job binds a given name); script
  bindings carry no scope and are counted for every session, matching the existing
  `GET /script-reference-bindings` read gate. Counts only — never which job, never a value.
- **Reference chips carry a verdict and the resolved scope (T1.4–T1.6).** A saved chip in
  the job/script bindings editor shows ✓/✗ plus a pill naming the row that actually won:
  `global`, a scope name, `only <scope>`, `missing`, or `invalid`. The reason is written
  out in words *underneath* the chips as well as in the chip's title — the originating
  session was lost precisely because the explanation was somewhere you had to go looking
  for. The verdict also reaches a screen reader; the glyph alone does not carry it.
- **Run-dialog reference preflight (T1.7, closing G6).** The Run dialog re-checks the
  job's **and its referenced script's** bindings (deduped by kind+name, mirroring
  dispatch's `collectRunBindings`) against the **effective** scope, inside the *Where it
  runs* panel. This is the only surface that can be right: a job whose own scope is *All*
  can be run against a specific scope via the override, and references resolve against the
  **run's** scope, so job detail cannot predict the answer. An unresolved count appears in
  the collapsed panel summary and springs the panel open — the same treatment an
  incompatible scope already gets, so a fold can never hide a run that will fail closed.
- **Env Vars scope filter with an explicit "Global only" option (T1.8)** on both the
  Variables and Secrets tabs.
- **"Used by" column on Variables and Secrets, "Bound By" on SSH Keys (T1.9).** Zero is
  rendered as `—` and stated in the tooltip rather than blanked: "nothing binds this" is a
  real, actionable answer (the scope edit is free), while a blank cell reads as missing
  data. On SSH Keys this is deliberately a *second* column beside the existing **Used
  By** — that one counts hosts/bastions the key authenticates, which is a different
  question, and a key can have one without the other.
- **Tests.** `runref`: a 13-case truth table over {in-scope, global, out-of-scope,
  missing, invalid} × {secret, variable, key} × {unrestricted, scoped, zero-grant}
  actors, asserting the restricted-actor degradation directly; plus the dispatch-agreement
  guard and order preservation. `api`: the actor-filter wiring, the scope guard, the CSRF
  gate, and — the important one — that an out-of-scope row and an absent name produce
  **reasons identical modulo the caller-supplied name** for a restricted actor. Frontend:
  9 tests covering every chip state and that the preflight **re-posts when the scope
  override moves** rather than reusing the first answer, plus 2 `RunDialog` tests pinning
  the collapsed-fold regression below.

### Fixed — two bugs the new check found on first contact

- **The Env Vars form's default scope wrote a row that could never resolve.** The
  Variables/Secrets scope selector offers **All** as its first and default option, and
  submitted that sentinel **verbatim** — producing a row whose scope is the literal
  string `"All"`. Nothing in the backend has ever recognized such a sentinel (there is no
  match for `"All"` anywhere in `internal/`), so the resolver treats it as a named scope
  like any other, and the row resolves for **no run at all** while the table cheerfully
  displayed "All". The form now maps the sentinel to the global scope on write, and a
  global row round-trips back to showing **All** when reopened for edit. **Pre-existing
  rows stored with `scope = "All"` are not migrated** — they are now visibly wrong (the
  Scope column shows `All`, and any binding to them reports `only "All"`) rather than
  invisibly wrong, which is the right first step; re-save such a row to correct it.
- **The Run-dialog preflight never ran while its fold was collapsed.** `Disclosure`
  renders `{open && children}`, so mounting the check inside the *Where it runs* panel
  meant it only evaluated once the operator opened the fold — and an unresolved reference
  **opening** that fold is the entire point. Restructured into
  `useRunReferencePreflight` (owned by the dialog, always mounted) plus a purely
  presentational `ReferencePreflightPanel` inside the fold. Two `RunDialog` regression
  tests now assert the count reaches the *collapsed* summary.

  Every unit test passed with that check dead. It was caught by driving the real app —
  the same lesson as the Run dialog being handed a list row with no `prompts`.

### Changed

- **Env Vars: an unscoped row now reads `global` rather than a blank cell (T1.8).** The
  distinction is load-bearing — a global row is visible from, and injectable into, *every*
  scope — and a blank cell was indistinguishable from "not loaded". The same word is used
  by the reference chips, from one shared constant.
- **The pre-existing ⚠ on a binding chip now only marks an *unsaved* chip.** A saved chip
  carries a real verdict; the ⚠ was a client-side guess ("no Env Vars row with this name")
  that the server now answers properly, and showing both would say the same thing twice
  with less authority.
- **Both manuals.** User manual §11.3/§11.5 (the new columns and filter) and a new
  §11.6 subsection tabulating every chip state with what to do about it; Administrator
  manual §6.1b states the oracle rule and its new authoring-side counterpart in full, so
  the next reader does not "fix" the validator back into vagueness — or out of it.

### Deviations from the plan

- **T1.1 specifies a single-reference body `{kind, name, scope}`; this ships the batch
  shape** `{scope, references[]}`. Every caller needs the set: job detail resolves all
  chips on load, and the Run dialog re-resolves the whole set on each scope override. A
  single reference is a one-element array.
- **T1.1/AG-Q4 propose gating the endpoint on `ManageEnvVars`; it ships session-gated.**
  Gating it on `ManageEnvVars` would have left the chips dark for exactly the read-only
  operators who most need them. The information bound is unchanged and in fact tighter:
  the response is capped by the caller's own list visibility, and both of those list
  endpoints are themselves session-gated, so no actor learns anything new.

### Not in this phase

Phases 2–4 of the plan — the `*_agencies` join tables, the `runs.agencies_json` snapshot,
the claim-predicate switch (which needs the T3.1 benchmark baseline first), the AG-Q5 SSH
key tightening and its pre-flight report, and the agency membership matrix — are
untouched. Phase 1 was deliberately built to stand alone: nothing here depends on them,
and nothing here presumes their decisions.

## 0.52.0 — Runner upgrade command + Run dialog redesign

**Date:** Jul 26, 2026

### Runner detail: "Copy upgrade command" (RU1)

Upgrading an installed agent had no in-app path — the operator had to reconstruct the
download, checksum and restart steps by hand from the install guide, which is how a
runner ends up stranded on an old protocol (a v5 agent silently stops claiming runs whose
job declares reference bindings, because dispatch-time secret injection requires v6+).

The runner detail's Agent version row now offers a one-paste block that downloads this
server's published binary for the host's architecture, verifies it against the served
`SHA256SUMS`, swaps `/usr/local/bin/amadeus-runner` and restarts the unit. Registration,
runner id, API key and local config are untouched — it is a binary swap, not a reinstall.

- Download + verification mirror `runner-install.sh --download` exactly (arch mapping,
  `/agents/` URLs, `grep <file> SHA256SUMS | sha256sum -c`) so the two can't drift. A
  checksum mismatch is a hard failure, never a fallback.
- The previous binary is kept at `.prev` and the failure path prints the rollback
  command — once an agent won't start, the control channel can't help.
- Delivered as a quoted heredoc (`sudo bash -s <<'SH'`), so the shell the operator pastes
  into expands nothing of the script's own `$VAR` / `$(…)`.
- Offered regardless of the "up to date" badge: that badge compares version *strings*, so
  a locally-built agent can read current while still speaking an older protocol.

Deliberately **not** a server-pushed self-update. A poll control op only reaches agents
already speaking the protocol version that introduced it, so a push would be dark on
exactly the runners most in need of upgrading; this also adds no remote-code-execution
surface to the control plane and needs no new privilege model on the runner host. The
self-update design (opt-in flag, signed manifest, root-owned updater unit) is deferred.

New `frontend/src/views/runner-upgrade-cmd.ts` + 8 unit tests. The generated script was
additionally verified by execution against a local agent-distribution server: fresh host
with no prior binary, upgrade over an existing binary, tampered binary, and a missing
`SHA256SUMS` entry — the last two abort with the installed binary untouched. That run
caught a `set -e` bug (`[ -f "$BIN" ] && cp …` aborts the upgrade when no binary exists)
that no string assertion would have.

### Run dialog redesign — answers first, targeting second

The Run dialog had grown into seven equally-weighted sections stacked flat, with each
declared input carrying two redundant warning lines and the primary action pushed below
the fold on any job declaring more than a handful. An operator who was not the job's
author could not tell where to start. Reworked so that one thing is loud — what this run
still needs — and everything else is quiet:

- **Answers this run needs** leads the dialog, with a readiness count and a segmented
  meter carrying one segment per declared input. Each input is a card with a colored
  state edge and a plain-language state word — *Needs a value* / *Using a default* /
  *Ready* / *Optional* — so state is never carried by color alone.
- **Long input lists paginate** (above five) alongside a "Show only what needs an answer"
  filter. The meter always spans *every* input regardless of page, so a required input on
  page 2 can never hide.
- **Where it runs** folds scope, executor, host/group targeting and per-run overrides
  behind one disclosure that states the destination in plain words
  (`Staging · Runner · all 2 hosts`) without being opened. It auto-opens when the chosen
  scope doesn't declare the job's run-type.
- **The commit zone is pinned** to the bottom of the modal: destination, what's still
  missing, and the action stay on screen while the input list scrolls under them.
- **The author's label leads** and the raw env var name moves to the tooltip and the
  audit line, so a non-technical operator reads "Target environment" rather than
  `TARGET_ENV`. The per-row audit line (`will send NAME=value · source`) is kept on every
  row that sends something — it is the run's paper trail — but demoted to a footnote.
- Copy throughout moved to plain, active language: *Run without 2 answers*,
  *2 answers are still missing*, *Use this*. Author-facing copy in the Job Composer and
  the run-history acknowledgment note were updated to match.

Behavior is unchanged: the gate, the `warn`/`block` enforcement split (JR-Q5/Q10), the
provenance precedence (JR-Q1) and the `promptAnswers`/`promptAcknowledged` audit payload
(T2.4) all work exactly as before. New `frontend/src/views/jobs/RunInputs.tsx`; frontend
`tsc -b` and **207** vitest (5 new) green; `backend/web/dist` rebuilt.

## 0.51.7 — Run inputs: opt-in hard enforcement (`block`)

**Date:** Jul 24, 2026

Phase 3 — the final phase — of the job-run-update plan (decisions **JR-Q5**,
**JR-Q9**, **JR-Q10**; tasks T3.1–T3.8). A job can now be opted in to **refusing** a run
while a declared required input has no value, instead of running anyway and recording a
warning. Every existing job keeps the warn-only behavior — the flag is per job and
defaults to `warn`.

**Schema v660** (migration `660_prompt_enforcement`). Backend `go test ./...` + `go vet`
green; frontend `tsc -b`, **202** vitest (2 new), and full build green; both
`openapi.yaml` copies byte-identical + client regenerated; `backend/web/dist` rebuilt.

> ### ⚠️ Upgrade note
>
> - **No behavior change on deploy.** `jobs.prompt_enforcement` defaults to `'warn'`, so
>   every job — git-synced or composed — keeps exactly the UDV4 semantics it had. An
>   admin opts a specific job in. Nothing that runs today starts failing.
> - **An unrecognized value degrades to `warn`, deliberately.** This flag decides whether
>   Cronomicon *refuses* to run someone's job, so it fails **open**: a typo in
>   `spec.prompt_enforcement` in Git can never silently take a job offline at 3am. The
>   Composer offers only the two valid choices and a DB `CHECK` constraint is the backstop.
> - **`block` is not escapable (JR-Q10).** `promptAcknowledged` does **not** bypass it —
>   an escapable block would just be `warn` with extra steps. The Run dialog **hides** its
>   "Run anyway" affordance for such a job rather than offering an override the server
>   will reject.
> - **Widening the vocabulary later needs a table rebuild.** The `CHECK` pins
>   `('warn','block')`; SQLite cannot alter a CHECK in place — the same trap
>   `jobs.run_type` carries.

### Added

- **`promptEnforcement: warn | block` per job (T3.1, JR-Q5/JR-Q9).** A scalar
  `jobs.prompt_enforcement` column — not overloaded into `prompts_json` — so "which jobs
  can hard-fail?" is a `WHERE` clause rather than a JSON scan. Carried on `JobYAML.Spec`
  (`prompt_enforcement`), `JobComposeInput`, and `Job`; normalized on **both** write and
  read through a shared `gitlab.NormalizePromptEnforcement`, so the git and compose paths
  cannot diverge.
- **`422 prompt_required` (T3.2).** `POST /jobs/{jobId}/run` refuses a `block` job while a
  declared required input has no value in the run's effective env; the message names them.
  A `warn` job is never rejected for this.
- **Composer enforcement control (T3.4).** Appears once a job declares a required input,
  with copy stating exactly what each mode does — and what `block` does *not* yet cover.
- **Compose-time warning for scheduled jobs (T3.6/G7).** A scheduled job that declares a
  required input with **no default** that neither the job env nor the schedule's env
  supplies is flagged at authoring time — nobody is present to answer when a schedule
  fires, so it would be recorded unfilled on every single run.
- **The same warning read-only on the Jobs page (T3.7).** Surfaced in the job's **Run
  inputs** panel, which already has the prompts, env, and schedules loaded — no extra
  fetch. (Deviation from the plan, which proposed the Schedules/Upcoming view; that would
  need an N+1 detail fetch per row for data the job panel already holds.)
- **Tests.** `TestMigrate660RoundTrip` (existing rows default to `warn`; `block` accepted;
  the CHECK rejects anything else; clean down/up) and `TestRunJobPromptBlockEnforcement`
  — `warn` unchanged (202), `block` unfilled → 422, `block` filled → 202, an unrecognized
  mode degrades to `warn`, and **`block` + `promptAcknowledged` → 422 anyway**, asserted
  explicitly so a future "be helpful" change can't quietly reintroduce the escape. Plus 2
  `RunDialog` component tests covering the hidden-escape behavior.

### Changed

- **Run dialog adapts to a `block` job (T3.3).** The "Run anyway" checkbox is replaced by
  an explanation, the button reads *"N required inputs missing"* rather than promising a
  run it can't perform, and a server `prompt_required` rejection is surfaced inline with
  the dialog kept open so the operator can fill the values in place.
- **User manual** documents the enforcement selector, the not-yet-covered paths, and the
  workflow-step finding below.

### Known limitation

- **`block` covers requested runs, not scheduled or workflow-triggered fires.**
  Enforcement lives at the run endpoint; the scheduler and workflow engine enqueue through
  a different path and are **not** refused. T3.6/T3.7's authoring-time warnings are the
  mitigation. This is called out plainly in the Composer copy and the manual rather than
  left as a false promise — extending enforcement to the enqueue path needs a decision
  about how a refused scheduled run should surface (a failed run with a reason, versus a
  silent skip), which is deliberately not being made in passing.
- **T3.8 finding: a workflow step CAN supply a run input.** `workflow.childEnvJSON`
  layers job env → parent workflow env → the step's A12 inputs, so a step input satisfies
  a declared required input normally. No change needed; documented.

## 0.51.6 — Run inputs: script-declared inputs + the audit loop closed

**Date:** Jul 24, 2026

Phase 2 of the job-run-update plan (decision **JR-Q6**, tasks T2.1–T2.10).
Two halves: a **Script** can now declare the run inputs it consumes, and a job composed
from it **inherits** them — the root-cause fix for inputs going undeclared, since the
required set is now correct by default instead of depending on an admin remembering a
button. And the audit loop closes: `promptWarnings` has been written to every affected
run since v0.38.0 and read by **nothing**; History now surfaces it, alongside two new
records of what the operator actually did.

**Schema v651** (migration `651_script_prompts`). Backend `go test ./...` + `go vet`
green; frontend `tsc -b`, **200** vitest (2 new), and full build green; both
`openapi.yaml` copies byte-identical + client regenerated; `backend/web/dist` rebuilt.

> ### ⚠️ Upgrade note
>
> - **Migration `651`, not `650` — the gap is deliberate.** The reverted PK-1 work
>   (commit `2203fbd`, reverted in `4c6a3f7`) shipped a migration `650` and **stamped
>   real databases with that version**. Reusing `650` would make migrate treat
>   `scripts.prompts_json` as already applied on those databases and silently skip it,
>   leaving the column missing at runtime. A version gap is harmless to golang-migrate;
>   a silent skip is not. **`650` remains free for PK-1 if it is re-landed.**
> - **A dev database already stamped at `650` still fails to open** ("no migration found
>   for version 650") — that is the reverted commit's residue, not this change. Reset it
>   or re-land PK-1.
> - **`scripts.prompts_json` defaults to `'[]'`.** Existing rows read as "declares
>   nothing" until the first sync after deploy recomputes them. Advisory throughout — a
>   malformed list never blocks a sync and never enters `content_hash`.

### Added

- **Scripts declare their own run inputs (JR-Q6, T2.5–T2.8).** `spec.prompts` in
  `scripts/*.yaml` reuses the exact `PromptSpec` shape a Job already carries, persists to
  `scripts.prompts_json` via the **same `MarshalPrompts`** the jobs path uses (so the two
  cannot drift), and is exposed as `Script.prompts` on **both** the list and detail
  projections. Distinct from `scripts.variables`, which stays the heuristic body
  extraction used only as an authoring aid — declared beats inferred (UDV1).
- **Composer auto-seeds Run inputs from the selected Script (T2.9).** Deliberately
  conservative: seeds only into an **empty** list and only once per script selection, so
  it never clobbers what an author has edited or cleared on purpose. Editing an existing
  job is unaffected — its saved inputs populate the list first. The heuristic "Import
  detected variables" button remains the fallback for scripts that declare nothing.
- **History surfaces unfilled required inputs (T2.2/T2.3).** An amber `⚠ N unfilled`
  badge on the executions **row** — so an auditor can spot affected runs without opening
  each one — plus a **Run inputs** block at the top of the detail drawer naming them.
- **`promptAnswers` + `promptAcknowledged` on the run envelope (T2.4).** Optional request
  fields on `POST /jobs/{jobId}/run`: where each input's value came from (`you` /
  `default` / `override` / `job env`), and whether the operator knowingly proceeded past
  an unfilled required input via "Run anyway". This is what makes a run someone requested
  through a third party defensible after the fact, and it is the field Phase 1 explicitly
  could not express (JR-Q8). History states plainly which case applies: *"The operator was
  shown this and chose 'Run anyway'"* vs *"No operator acknowledgment was recorded — this
  may have been triggered by a schedule, a workflow, or the API."*
- **Contract (T2.1).** `promptWarnings` / `promptAnswers` / `promptAcknowledged` declared
  on the run-detail `overrides` schema, the two request fields on the run body, and
  `Script.prompts` — in both byte-identical `openapi.yaml` copies, client regenerated.
- **Tests.** `TestMigrate651RoundTrip` (DEFAULT applies to pre-migration rows; declared
  list round-trips; clean down/up), `TestUpsertScripts_DeclaredPrompts` (sync + nameless
  rows dropped + `[]` when none), `TestScriptPromptsOnTheWire` (**both** projections,
  never `null`), `TestRunJobPromptWarnings` extended (undeclared keys dropped; an
  acknowledgment does **not** suppress the server-derived warning; omitting both fields
  behaves exactly as before), and 2 `RunDialog` component tests for the audit payload.

### Changed

- **Both manuals reconciled for Phases 0–2.** The user manual's Run-dialog, Composer,
  History, primitives-table, and glossary sections were describing v0.38.0 behavior. Most
  importantly it still documented the **scope-Env-Var satisfaction that v0.51.4 removed as
  false** — that claim is now replaced with a callout explaining why an Env Vars row of the
  same name never satisfied a run input.

### Security

- **`promptAnswers` keys the job does not declare are dropped server-side**, so a caller
  cannot stuff the run's audit envelope with arbitrary content. `promptWarnings` stays
  **server-derived** and is never suppressed by a client-supplied acknowledgment — the two
  are deliberately separate: one records what the server observed, the other what the
  operator claims.

## 0.51.5 — Run inputs: state-first Run dialog, default confirmation, and the gate

**Date:** Jul 24, 2026

Phase 1 of the job-run-update plan (decisions **JR-Q2/Q4/Q7/Q8**) — the
ad-hoc Run dialog becomes **state-first**, so an operator running a job someone else
composed is told plainly what it needs before anything else. Declared prompt variables
are renamed **Run inputs** across all three surfaces, each one shows the value that will
actually be sent and where it came from, defaults must be **confirmed** rather than
silently inherited, and an unfilled required input **gates** the Run button behind an
explicit "Run anyway".

**Frontend-only** — no schema, no migration, no OpenAPI, no API behavior change. Backend
`go test ./...` + `go vet` green; frontend `tsc -b`, **198** vitest (9 new), and full
build green; `backend/web/dist` rebuilt. Verified in the running app in **both themes**.

> ### ⚠️ Upgrade note — a long-dead feature comes back to life
>
> **Declared run inputs have never rendered in the Run dialog.** `prompts` and `env` are
> **detail-only** fields, but the dialog was handed the Jobs **list** row — which carries
> neither — so `job.prompts` was always `undefined` and the entire UDV1 run-time surface
> (shipped in 0.38.0) silently displayed nothing. The read-only panel in the expanded job
> row worked, because it fetches its own detail; the dialog did not. The dialog now
> fetches its own detail, so jobs that have declared inputs all along will start asking
> for them. This is the feature working, not a new requirement — but expect operators to
> see prompts on jobs that never showed any.
>
> **A required input now gates the Run button.** It is never a dead end: ticking **Run
> anyway** proceeds and records the input as unfilled, exactly as before. UDV4 is intact —
> the server still accepts either way and never returns 422.

### Added

- **Summary banner (T1.2).** `"5 inputs — 1 needs a value — 2 awaiting confirmation"`,
  warning-toned while anything is unfilled. Suppressed entirely when a job declares none.
- **Effective value + provenance chip per input (T1.4).** Every input shows
  `Will send KEY=value` with a chip naming the source — **you** (typed), **default**
  (pre-filled, untouched), **override** (a per-run Environment-overrides row, which wins
  in `submit()`), or **job env** (`jobs.env_json`, the base layer of the server's
  `envmerge.Merge(jr.Env, body.Env)`). No more blank control with a footnote claiming the
  value is handled. Job-level env now correctly counts toward satisfaction — it genuinely
  reaches the run, unlike the scope Env Vars row removed in 0.51.4.
- **Per-row default confirmation (T1.5, JR-Q7).** A required input whose value came from
  its default is **unconfirmed** until the operator clicks "Use default ✓" or edits it —
  a distinct, softer state than **unfilled**, tracked separately in the banner and
  deliberately **not** blocking. Editing a row auto-confirms it.
- **The gate (T1.7/T1.8, JR-Q4b).** An unfilled required input disables "Run now", names
  the offending keys inline, and offers an explicit **Run anyway** checkbox. The button
  label reflects reality: `Run with 1 unfilled input`.
- **Composer lint: blank job-level env row (T1.11).** A job-level env row with **no value**
  is the classic mis-modeled required input — it ships an empty string to every run and
  nobody is ever asked. Now flagged with a one-click **"Convert to a Run input"** that
  moves it across and pre-checks `required`. Advisory; never blocks a save.
- **Composer lint: credential-shaped input names (T7.2).** A run input named like a
  credential (`*_TOKEN`, `*_PASSWORD`, `*_SECRET`, `*_KEY`, `*_PAT`, …) warns that answers
  are stored and sent in **plaintext** and points at the Secret Store.
- **9 `RunDialog` component tests** (`frontend/src/views/Jobs.RunDialog.test.tsx`) covering
  the gate, the escape, provenance precedence, default confirmation, banner counts — and a
  regression test that inputs arriving from the **detail fetch** render, which is precisely
  the failure the old unit-test shape could not see.

### Changed

- **"Run prompts" → "Run inputs" (T1.3, JR-Q2).** One term across the Run dialog, the
  expanded job row's read-only panel, and the Composer — plus the editor's add/remove
  controls ("+ run input") and the panel footnote.
- **Run inputs moved to the top of the Run dialog (T1.1).** Above Target scope: it is the
  only section that is job-specific and genuinely needs the operator; everything else has
  a working default.
- **Composer section titles contrast the two surfaces (T1.10).** "Environment (job-level)"
  → **"Environment (fixed values, applied to every run)"**, "Run prompts" →
  **"Run inputs (asked at run time)"**, each pointing at the other. This is the G2
  mis-modeling — an admin looking for a "required" flag on an env var — addressed at the
  point it happens.
- **Plaintext caveat repeated on the Run inputs section (T7.1)**, not only on Environment
  overrides further down.
- **Drift lint copy (T1.12)** names the renamed sections.
- **`RunDialog` is now exported** from `Jobs.tsx` for component testing.

### Fixed

- **The Run dialog never showed declared run inputs.** It rendered `job.prompts` from the
  Jobs **list** row, where `prompts`/`env` are absent (detail-only). It now fetches
  `GET /jobs/{jobId}` itself and seeds prompt defaults when the detail lands, so the
  feature works regardless of what the caller hands it. See the upgrade note.
- **A declared default outside `options` is now selectable (T1.6).** A `<select>` input
  whose `default` wasn't among its `options` could not display the value the chip claimed
  would be sent; the default is now prepended to the option list.

## 0.51.4 — Run dialog no longer claims a scope Env Var satisfies a required run input

**Date:** Jul 24, 2026

Phase 0 of the job-run-update plan (decision **JR-Q1**) — a correctness fix
to the ad-hoc Run dialog's required-input check. The dialog told operators a required
declared prompt (UDV1) was **satisfied** when an Env Vars row of the same name existed in
the effective scope. It isn't: Env Vars reach a run **only** through an explicit reference
binding and **only** under the derived `AMADEUS_VAR_<name>` key, so the variable was
absent at run time and the server recorded it as unfilled anyway. The UI and the run's own
audit record directly contradicted each other, and the operator had been told not to worry.

**Frontend fix + backend test/comment only** — no schema, no migration, no OpenAPI, no
API behavior change. Backend `go test ./...` + `go vet` green; frontend `tsc -b`, 189
vitest, and full build green; `backend/web/dist` rebuilt.

> ### ⚠️ Upgrade note — expect *more* prompt warnings, not fewer
>
> Runs that previously looked clean in the Run dialog may now show `● required` and be
> recorded with `promptWarnings`. **Nothing about how those runs execute has changed** —
> the variable was already absent and the warning was already being written to
> `runs.override_json`. Only the dialog's (incorrect) reassurance is gone. If a job relied
> on a scope Env Var reaching the script under its bare name, it was **never** doing so;
> declare the value as a job-level env row, supply it as a run input, or reference it
> explicitly as `AMADEUS_VAR_<name>`.

### Fixed

- **`promptSatisfied` no longer counts a scope Env Vars row (JR-Q1).** In
  `frontend/src/views/Jobs.tsx`, `RunDialog`'s satisfied-check dropped the
  `definedAtScope.has(name)` clause; a declared prompt is now satisfied only when the
  dialog will actually **send** a value for it — a filled field (including an untouched
  default, UDV8) or a non-empty override row with the same key. This mirrors exactly what
  the server checks when it writes `promptWarnings`
  (`backend/internal/api/execution_mount.go`), so the two surfaces can no longer disagree.
- **Removed the misleading "Satisfied by a scope env var." note** and its `satByScope`
  branch from the Variables section.
- **Dropped the now-dead `GET /env-vars` fetch** from the Run dialog (the
  `envVarsQ`/`definedAtScope` memo and the unused `EnvVar` type alias) — one fewer request
  on every dialog open.

### Changed

- **Comments corrected on both sides of the seam.** `execution_mount.go`'s UDV4/UDV6 block
  no longer describes scope-level satisfaction as "advisory and surfaced by the UI" (the
  UI no longer claims it); `Jobs.tsx` documents why a bare-named Env Vars row cannot
  satisfy a prompt, with a pointer to `internal/runref`.

### Added

- **The job-run-update plan** — the full four-phase plan for clear
  required-input prompting at run time (gap analysis G1–G7, decisions JR-Q1…JR-Q11,
  tasks T0.1–T7.3). This release is Phase 0 only.
- **JR-Q1 regression coverage** in `TestRunJobPromptWarnings`
  (`backend/internal/api/job_prompts_test.go`): seeds an `env_vars` row named identically
  to the required prompt and asserts `promptWarnings` is **still** recorded — pinning the
  corrected semantics server-side so a future "be helpful" change can't silently
  reintroduce the contradiction.

---

## 0.51.3 — Post-launch follow-ups: host-key pin UI, tag filtering at scale, restore tooling

**Date:** Jul 23, 2026

The triaged post-launch follow-ups (the feature-updates plan) — FU-1
(bastion/target host-key pinning UI), FU-2 (tag-filter scalability), and FU-3
(backup/restore DR). No new migrations; all changes are additive except the
removal of one inert API field (see upgrade note).

> ### ⚠️ Upgrade note — read before deploying
>
> - **No migrations.** Host-key pinning reuses the existing `ssh_hosts.host_key`
>   (070) and `bastions.host_key` (640) columns; tag filtering reuses the existing
>   `tags` columns.
> - **`AuditComplianceSettings.backup` removed (FU-3 Phase B).** The DB-stored S3
>   backup config was **inert** — the uploader has always been driven solely by
>   `AMADEUS_BACKUP_S3_*` env, and nothing read the DB copy. The field is gone from
>   `GET/PUT /api/v1/settings/audit-compliance`; any stale `backup` object in a
>   stored settings blob is silently dropped on next save. No behavior change to
>   actual backups. Env remains the sole backup-config surface.
> - **Re-key without raw SQL.** A legitimately re-keyed SSH host/bastion can now be
>   re-pinned from **Settings → SSH** (Clear pin → next connect re-captures via
>   TOFU) or `DELETE /api/v1/ssh/{hosts,bastions}/{id}/host-key`, replacing the old
>   `UPDATE … SET host_key=NULL`.

### Added

- **FU-1 — SSH host-key pin visibility & management (the deferred SU-4 UI item).**
  `SshHost`/`SshBastion` now expose read-only, non-secret pin metadata
  (`hostKeyPinned`, `hostKeyFingerprint` (SHA256), `hostKeyType`); the raw
  known_hosts line is never surfaced. **Settings → SSH** shows a Pinned ✓ / ⚠
  Unpinned badge with the short fingerprint (hover for the full SHA256 to compare
  out-of-band), the **Test connection** result now reports the pinned fingerprint,
  and a **Clear pin** action re-keys a host without raw SQL. New endpoints
  `DELETE /api/v1/ssh/hosts/{hostId}/host-key` and `.../bastions/{bastionId}/host-key`.
- **FU-2 — server-side, multi-tag catalog filtering.** All eight tagged list
  endpoints (jobs, scripts, schedules, workflows, env-vars, secrets,
  ssh-credentials, runners) now accept repeated `?tag=` (+ `?tags=csv`) and
  `?tagMatch=any|all`, matched per whole JSON element via a shared
  `tagutil.Filter` (`json_each`/exact) — not a substring `LIKE`. The catalog Tag
  filter is now a **multi-select** with an **Any/All (OR/AND)** toggle across all
  eight catalogs. The **Scripts** catalog routes tag filtering **server-side** when
  it exceeds its load cap (>1000), so it sees the whole catalog; the other catalogs
  filter the loaded page client-side (unchanged from the prior single-select — the
  server-side `?tag=` is available for future wiring). The exact-match jobs fix has
  an end-to-end regression test (`jobs_tag_filter_test.go`).
- **FU-3 Phase C — `amadeus restore` subcommand.** Fetches a snapshot from the S3
  backup bucket (latest or `--from <name>`, `--list` to enumerate), swaps it into
  place (removing stale WAL/SHM sidecars), and runs `PRAGMA integrity_check` +
  a row-count sanity check. Refuses an obviously-active DB (best-effort
  write-lock probe) and confirms before overwriting (`--yes` to skip). Replaces
  the by-hand `aws s3 cp` steps. Adds a read-side `backup.Downloader` (the
  uploader was put-only). See `backend/deploy/backup-restore.md`.

### Changed

- **FU-2 — jobs `?tag=` is now an exact-element match.** The previous
  `j.tags LIKE '%prod%'` matched `["production"]` (a latent wrong-results bug); it
  now matches whole tags via `json_each`.
- **FU-3 Phase B — env is the sole backup-config surface.** The inert
  `settings.BackupConfig` (and its `AuditComplianceSettings.backup` API field) was
  removed; the admin manual no longer implies an env-overrides-DB merge for
  backups. Kills the "configured S3 backup in the UI but nothing happened" trap.
- **FU-1 Phase 4 — doc fix.** `sshexec.ProbeBastion`'s stale comment (claimed the
  bastion hop uses "insecure-ignore … TC.9 tracks pinning") now describes the
  SU-4 strict-compare/TOFU pinning the code actually does.

### Deferred (documented, not shipped)

- **FU-1 Phase 3 — opt-in approve-before-trust** (`AMADEUS_SSH_REQUIRE_HOSTKEY_APPROVAL`):
  a larger pending-approval subsystem for the in-app SSH path; silent-TOFU remains
  the default and is now visible + clearable, which covers the immediate need.
- **FU-3 Phase A — execute the DR drill:** an operator task requiring a live
  stack; the runbook now carries the tooling and an explicit "not yet executed"
  callout. **FU-3 Phase D — automated integrity verification** (periodic
  test-restore): optional hardening, not yet built.

## 0.51.2 — Security update Phase C: bastion pinning, session revocation, zeroization

**Date:** Jul 22, 2026

Phase C of the 2026-07-22 security remediation
— the hardening & cleanup findings.

> ### ⚠️ Upgrade note — read before deploying
>
> - **Two migrations (640, 641).** `640` adds `bastions.host_key`; `641` adds the
>   `auth_session_epoch` singleton. Both are additive and applied automatically.
> - **Bastion host keys are now verified (TOFU).** The first connect (or a
>   Settings → SSH → bastion **Test connection**) captures & pins each bastion's key;
>   thereafter a changed key aborts the connection. If a bastion is legitimately
>   re-keyed, clear its `host_key` to re-capture. Runs that inject secrets over a
>   bastion to an **unpinned target** are refused until the target key is pinned.
> - **RBAC changes now revoke sessions.** Editing an AD-group→role mapping or a
>   role's scope grants invalidates all *other* OIDC sessions immediately (the admin
>   making the change stays logged in). Session TTL also drops from 12h to 8h.

### Security

- **SU-4 (MED) — Bastion SSH host key pinned & verified.** The jump-host hop used
  `InsecureIgnoreHostKey()` (accept-any → first-connect MITM + secret exfil). It now
  strict-compares a pinned `bastions.host_key`, else TOFU-captures the first-seen key
  — mirroring the target host-key path. As an interim guard, a run that injects
  secrets is refused when it routes over a bastion to an *unpinned* target (the
  remaining first-connect MITM window).
- **SU-5 (LOW) — Server-side session revocation.** OIDC sessions carry a server-side
  epoch stamped at login; it is bumped on any RBAC change (AD-group mapping / scope
  grant), so pre-change sessions are rejected on their next request and must
  re-authenticate — the admin making the change keeps their own session via a
  same-request cookie re-issue. `sessionTTL` dropped 12h → 8h as a backstop.
- **SU-10 (INFO) — Best-effort key zeroization.** The unwrapped DEK (and the loaded
  KEK) are wiped on return from each envelope encrypt/decrypt, narrowing the window
  key material sits recoverable in memory. Best-effort only (Go GC/heap growth can
  leave copies); the encryption construction is unchanged.
- **SU-11 (INFO) — Legacy mock token neutralized.** The realistic-looking runner
  token literal in the frozen `amadeus-data.jsx` prototype is now `amt_reg_EXAMPLE`
  (in-place, honoring the "keep as frozen reference" policy). Not a live secret; no
  rotation.

### Added

- **Migration `640_bastion_host_key`** (`bastions.host_key`) and **`641_session_epoch`**
  (the `auth_session_epoch` singleton), each with a down-migration round-trip test.

---

## 0.51.1 — Security update Phase B: git-token argv leak + SSRF egress guard

**Date:** Jul 22, 2026

Phase B of the 2026-07-22 security remediation
— the process/token-handling findings.

> ### ⚠️ Upgrade note — read before deploying
>
> - **New SSRF egress guard on operator-configured outbound targets** (Vault, GitLab,
>   S3/MinIO, Apprise, OIDC). Cloud-metadata / loopback / link-local are now blocked.
>   **RFC-1918 / private ranges remain ALLOWED by default** (`AMADEUS_OUTBOUND_ALLOW_PRIVATE=true`),
>   so internal Vault/GitLab keep working with no action. Two cases need a config change:
>   a **Vault-agent loopback sidecar** (Vault on `127.0.0.1`) requires
>   `AMADEUS_OUTBOUND_ALLOW_LOOPBACK=true`; the stricter posture that also blocks
>   private ranges is `AMADEUS_OUTBOUND_ALLOW_PRIVATE=false`.
> - **The Vault status probe now honors `AMADEUS_VAULT_CA_FILE`** (it previously ignored
>   it and used system roots). A private-CA Vault that showed "degraded" on the settings
>   page will now probe correctly.

### Security

- **SU-3 (MED) — Checkout deploy token kept out of git argv.** The runner-side pinned
  checkout previously embedded the credential (`oauth2:<token>@host` or `user:pass@host`)
  in the `git clone`/`fetch` URL, exposing it via `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` and auditd
  execve. The credential is now delivered out-of-band via `GIT_ASKPASS` (the password
  comes from the helper's environment, not argv); only the non-secret username rides in
  the URL. Git stderr is additionally scrubbed of any `://user:pass@` — the runner-local
  deploy token is never in the server redactor dictionary, so a credential-bearing URL
  in a git error would otherwise persist un-redacted.
- **SU-7 (LOW) — SSRF guard on operator-configured outbound targets.** A shared guarded
  dialer (`internal/httpx`) resolves each outbound host and refuses cloud-metadata
  (`169.254.169.254`, `fd00:ec2::254`), loopback, and link-local addresses, dialing a
  checked IP directly to also close DNS-rebind. It is wired into all seven server-initiated
  clients — Vault KV, the Vault status probe, the GitLab REST client, go-git
  clone/fetch/push (via a custom go-git HTTP client that also gives go-git a timeout and
  redirect refusal it previously lacked — closing the SU-8 gap for go-git), S3/MinIO
  backup, and OIDC discovery/JWKS + token exchange — plus the Apprise push. RFC-1918 is
  allowed by default (SU-Q4(a)) since Vault/GitLab are internal; the S3 IAM-role
  credential provider is exempt so EC2/ECS IMDS still works.

### Fixed

- **Vault status probe ignored `AMADEUS_VAULT_CA_FILE`** — it used system roots
  (inconsistent with the KV client), so a private-CA Vault always read "degraded". The
  probe now builds the same CA-pinned, egress-guarded transport as the KV client.

### Added

- **`AMADEUS_OUTBOUND_ALLOW_PRIVATE`** (default `true`) and **`AMADEUS_OUTBOUND_ALLOW_LOOPBACK`**
  (default `false`) config knobs for the SSRF egress posture. Documented in
  `deploy/env-matrix.md` and `deploy/amadeus.env.example`.

## 0.51.0 — Security update Phase A: output-leak, scope reads, ingest cap, session keys, redirects

**Date:** Jul 22, 2026

Phase A of the 2026-07-22 security remediation
— the five highest-value, lowest-risk findings, each mirroring a pattern the codebase
already enforces elsewhere. Two close leaks that are inconsistent with protections in
place on the sibling path (a Vault-secret leak the runner path already blocks; a
cross-scope read the run/log path already gates). All five ship with regression tests.

> ### ⚠️ Upgrade note — read before deploying
>
> - **Out-of-scope job/schedule detail now returns `404`.** A scope-restricted operator
>   requesting a job (`GET /jobs/{id}`) or first-class-owner schedule outside their
>   granted scopes previously saw the full detail (script body + plaintext env); it now
>   returns **404** (no existence oracle) and out-of-scope rows are dropped from the
>   job / workflow-run / schedule listings. Unrestricted operators are unaffected.
> - **New `AMADEUS_MAX_RUN_LOG_BYTES` knob (default 512 MiB).** Caps a single run's
>   ingested log; past the cap, ingest returns `413`. Set `0` to disable. Existing
>   deployments need no action unless a run legitimately exceeds 512 MiB of log.
> - **Weak session keys are now rejected, not silently used.** A `AMADEUS_SESSION_HASH_KEY`
>   shorter than 32 bytes is replaced with a random ephemeral key (sessions won't survive
>   restart) and a non-base64 value is rejected in a production auth mode. If you see the
>   broadened "session keys unset, too short, or invalid" warning at boot, set both keys
>   to base64-encoded 32-byte values.

### Security

- **SU-1 (HIGH) — SSH executor fails closed on an output that leaks an injected secret.**
  The in-app SSH executor now matches the runner ingest path: a captured
  `::amadeus-output name=X::<injected-secret>` value (the natural
  `echo "::amadeus-output name=TOKEN::$AMADEUS_SECRET_FOO"` idiom) drops the outputs and
  fails the run with reason `output_secret_leak`, so the secret never lands in
  `outputs_json`, a workflow child step's plaintext `env_json`, or the runs API. The
  leak detector `firstOutputLeakingSecret` was promoted to
  `execspec.FirstOutputLeakingSecret` so both execution paths share one implementation.
- **SU-2 (MED) — Job/schedule read endpoints are scope-filtered.** `getJob` — and
  `pauseJob`/`resumeJob`, which return the same job detail — now return `404` for an
  out-of-scope actor (no existence oracle, matching `putJobBindings`); `listJobs`,
  `listWorkflowRuns`, `listSchedules`, and `listUpcomingSchedules` filter to the actor's
  readable scopes (the schedule handlers resolve each row's owner→`jobs.scope` in the
  existing query, no extra round-trip). Mirrors the `listRuns`/`getRun` gating.
- **SU-9 (LOW) — Per-run log-ingest byte cap.** The log-ingest endpoint (exempt from the
  2 MiB body cap because a run streams many chunks) is now bounded by
  `AMADEUS_MAX_RUN_LOG_BYTES`; a rogue/compromised runner streaming past the ceiling gets
  `413` and nothing further is persisted.
- **SU-6 (LOW) — Session hash-key length validated; raw-key fallback disabled in prod.**
  A `<32`-byte hash key is substituted with a random one (ephemeral, warned) instead of
  weakening HMAC, and a non-base64 key is rejected outside dev rather than used as raw
  bytes (a typo'd passphrase can no longer become a short, low-entropy key).
- **SU-8 (LOW) — Credentialed outbound clients refuse redirects.** The Vault
  (`X-Vault-Token`) and GitLab REST (`Private-Token`) clients set
  `CheckRedirect = ErrUseLastResponse`, because Go's stdlib does **not** strip custom
  headers on a cross-host redirect — a redirect to an attacker host would otherwise
  carry the token/PAT.

### Added

- **`AMADEUS_MAX_RUN_LOG_BYTES`** config knob (default `536870912` = 512 MiB; `0`
  disables). Documented in `deploy/env-matrix.md` and `deploy/amadeus.env.example`.

### Docs

- `deploy/security-review.md` gains a Phase-A section: the five resolved controls (with
  their automated verifications) plus the accepted residual notes — the deliberate
  404-vs-403 asymmetry (SU-Q2), the unscoped first-class schedule-defs catalog (SU-Q7),
  the latent `workflow_runs.scope` filter, and the findings deferred to Phases B/C.

## 0.50.3 — A5 scope model: backfill migration + re-login (Phase 5)

**Date:** Jul 22, 2026

Final phase of the A5 scope-model fix — the
upgrade-safety work that lets the behavior change ship without locking anyone out.
**With this release the A5 "empty ≡ unrestricted" sentinel is fully resolved.**

> ### ⚠️ Upgrade note — read before deploying
>
> - **What changed (0.50.0–0.50.3):** a role with **no** scope grants now has **zero**
>   scope access. Before, an empty grant silently meant **all** scopes.
> - **No lockout on upgrade.** Migration `630` backfills the explicit `"*"` (all-scopes)
>   grant for **every role that is unrestricted today** (i.e. has no `allowed=1` rows),
>   so nothing tightens on deploy — everyone unrestricted stays unrestricted, everyone
>   scoped keeps their exact scopes.
> - **One-time re-login required.** The session cookie name is bumped
>   (`amadeus_session` → `amadeus_session_v2`), so every operator re-authenticates once
>   and their identity re-resolves with the backfilled grant. (Trusted-header
>   deployments resolve per request — nothing to do.)
> - **Then review the matrix.** In **Settings → Users & Access → Scope Restrictions**,
>   turn **off** "All scopes" for any role that should actually be limited — that is now
>   the safe direction (empty = no access).

### Added

- **Migration `630_scope_star_backfill`** — backfills `scope_restrictions(role, '*', 1)`
  for every built-in role with zero `allowed=1` rows (behavior-preserving, DEC-2(i)).
  The down migration removes all `"*"` rows. Test `TestScopeStarBackfill630` covers
  both: empty roles gain `"*"`, an explicitly-granted role is untouched.

### Changed

- **Session invalidation:** `sessionCookieName` bumped to `amadeus_session_v2`. Because
  the cookie name is part of securecookie's HMAC, pre-migration frozen cookies no longer
  decode — forcing the one-time re-login that re-resolves scopes with the backfill.

### Docs

- Predecessor plans updated: the vault-integration §8 A5 sentinel note and the
  follow-up plan's A5 dependency + M3 name-leak residual are marked **resolved** (M3's
  closure is no longer A5-blocked).

## 0.50.1 — A5 scope model: RBAC admin surface for the "*" grant (Phase 3)

**Date:** Jul 22, 2026

Phase 3 of the A5 scope-model fix teaches the
role → scope matrix the new model, so an admin can actually grant, read, and audit
"unrestricted" as an explicit `"*"` rather than the old empty-means-all trap.

### Changed — `PUT /api/v1/scope-restrictions`

- **Accepts the `"*"` (all-scopes) grant** and **validates it is exclusive** — mixing
  `"*"` with a named scope is rejected `422`. An empty `allowedScopes` now persists as
  **zero rows ⇒ zero scope access** (the meaning that landed in 0.50.0), not "all".
- **Per-role change-log audit:** each posted role writes a `change_log` row with its
  resulting grant summary (`all scopes (*)` / the joined set / `no scope access`),
  replacing the single opaque "updated scope restrictions" line.
- **Last-unrestricted-admin invariant:** the write refuses (`409 last_admin_lockout`)
  any state leaving no role with either `"*"` or `ManageRoles` reach. Note: because
  `ManageRoles` is a static, non-scope-gated permission the built-in `admin` always
  holds, this invariant is always satisfied today — it is explicit defense-in-depth
  for a future with editable roles, and it does **not** block scoping `admin` to a
  partial set (a supported control).

### Changed — `GET /api/v1/scope-restrictions`

- Each role now reports **`unrestricted: bool`** (true iff its grants carry `"*"`), so
  the UI can tell the three states apart: unrestricted (`"*"`) / a granted set / empty
  (= zero). The OpenAPI `ScopeRestriction` schema is updated in both spec copies.

### Deferred

- **Phase 4** — frontend "All scopes" toggle + corrected matrix copy (consumes the new
  `unrestricted` field).
- **Phase 5** — the behavior-preserving `"*"` backfill migration and one-time session
  invalidation on deploy.

## 0.50.0 — A5 scope model: "unrestricted" gets a distinct signal (Phases 1–2)

**Date:** Jul 22, 2026

The A5 scope-model fix (decision **Option C**).
Historically the scope layer represented **"unrestricted (all scopes)"** and
**"restricted to zero scopes"** with the *same* value — an empty allowed-scopes set —
and every guard read that empty set as *unrestricted*. The consequence: an operator who
cleared a role's scope access in the RBAC matrix (intending "no access") silently
granted that role **full** access. This release introduces an explicit signal for
"unrestricted" and routes every guard through it, so **empty now means zero**.

> **Behavior change (fail-closed).** A role with **no** scope grants now has **zero**
> scope access instead of full access. The behavior-preserving `"*"` backfill migration
> and the one-time re-login land in Phase 5 (see below) — until then, deploy on a
> non-empty `scope_restrictions` table only after reviewing the matrix. The direction is
> always fail-closed: the worst case is an over-broad role that must be re-granted
> (recoverable), never a silent widening.

### Added — `internal/auth` (Phase 1)

- **`AllScopes = "*"` sentinel** and **`Identity.Unrestricted()`** — a role is
  unrestricted iff its resolved grants contain `"*"`. The signal is **role-agnostic
  and data-derived**, not tied to the role name, so a scope-restricted `admin` stays
  restricted (preserving the injection RBAC controls H3/M1/M3/M4). The tri-state is now
  explicit: `"*"` ⇒ all · a set ⇒ exactly those · **empty ⇒ zero access**.
- **`ScopeReadable(id, scope)` / `ScopeWritable(id, target)`** — Identity-taking
  predicates that are the single source of truth for A5 read/write access. An empty
  grant reads only GLOBAL (`""`) rows and writes nothing; a restricted actor may not
  write GLOBAL.
- **`ScopeGrant{Unrestricted, Allowed}` + `CanRead`/`CanWrite`, and `Identity.Grant()`**
  — a plain transport value (its **zero value fails closed**) for packages that must not
  import `Identity` (e.g. `internal/secrets`).
- **`auth.WithIdentity(ctx, id)`** — an exported context seam so handlers invoked
  directly (e.g. in tests) get the same identity the middleware sets.

### Changed — guard reroute (Phase 2)

- **Every A5 guard now routes through the predicates** — the ~20 inline
  `len(id.AllowedScopes) > 0 && …` checks and package-local mirrors are gone:
  - `execution_mount.go` — run trigger, kill, workflow-trigger fan-out, get-run,
    get/cancel-workflow-run, and the **listRuns** SQL filter (unrestricted ⇒ all;
    restricted ⇒ GLOBAL + granted; **empty ⇒ GLOBAL only**).
  - `settings_mount.go` — secret & env-var read/write guards; `bindings_mount.go` —
    job-binding read/write, run-reference scope gate, `knownReferenceNames` filter, and
    the script-binding "unrestricted manager only" gate; `runner/log.go` — run-log IDOR.
  - `secrets/service.go` — `scopeVisible` deleted; `List` takes a `func(scope) bool`
    predicate (the API passes `id.Grant().CanRead`), keeping `secrets` free of `auth`.
- `scopes.go` doc comments rewritten: the **KNOWN LIMITATION** ("empty ⇒ unrestricted,
  indistinguishable from zero") is replaced by the documented tri-state.
- **`devIdentity()`** now holds the explicit `"*"` grant (was empty), so the dev-login
  bypass stays unrestricted under the new model.
- Acceptance gate is clean — no inline empty-set scope guard survives outside
  `scopes.go`; the transitional `[]string` shims were removed once callers migrated.

### Deferred to later phases (see the plan)

- **Phase 3** — RBAC admin surface: accept/persist the `"*"` grant (exclusive), a
  last-unrestricted-admin lockout guard, change auditing, and per-role `unrestricted`
  in the API.
- **Phase 4** — frontend "All scopes" toggle + corrected matrix copy.
- **Phase 5** — the behavior-preserving `"*"` backfill migration and the one-time
  session invalidation on deploy.

## 0.49.15 — Injection §6 end-to-end test suite

by R5 of the follow-up plan): a runner-agent end-to-end test for the full
injection + key-delivery pipeline, and a reconciliation of the §6 checkboxes with

## 0.49.14 — Runner SSH-key material delivery (R5 / D8)

**Date:** Jul 21, 2026

Group R5 of the follow-up review
(the vault-integration-followup plan): the last unshipped *functional*
item — delivering bound SSH-key material to runners at dispatch, closing the
"stored-credential-by-ID gap" (a runner could only use a key already on its disk).

### Added

- **Runner key-material delivery (D8).** A job/script that binds an SSH key
  (`AMADEUS_KEY_<name>`) now ships the resolved private-key **material** to a
  flagged, protocol-v6 runner in the manifest `Keys` block (the wire field was
  already reserved). The agent materializes each key to a **tmpfs-preferred
  (`/dev/shm`) `0600` file off the run tree**, exposes `AMADEUS_KEY_<name>=<path>`
  in the run environment, and feeds the delivered key into its key resolver so a
  bound key is used for both the SSH-connection signer and the ansible private-key
  bridge — **delivered wins, the runner's own key-dir/key-map remains the
  fallback**. Files are zeroed and removed at run end (including on early error).
  This closes the stored/vault-credential-by-ID gap: a runner no longer needs the
  key pre-provisioned on disk.

### Security

- **Lockstep redaction + audit** (the critical D8 interaction). Both runner resolve
  paths — manifest injection and per-chunk ingest redaction — no longer drop key
  bindings before resolving, so delivered key **material enters the redaction
  dictionary** and is masked in logs (a job that cats a delivered key file has its
  bytes redacted at ingest). A key-bearing run also sets the M5 `injects_secret`
  dispatch flag (fail-closed), and the delivered key is recorded in the dispatch
  audit (`change_log`, names + source, never the material). Key material is gated
  exactly like secret values — only a flagged v6 runner ever receives it.
- The in-app **SSH executor still skips** key bindings by design: it connects *from*
  Cronomicon *to* targets, so a bound key would have to land on the remote target — a
  distinct problem from runner delivery, still deferred. Because it delivers no key
  material, its redaction dictionary correctly carries none.

### Tests

- `TestManifestDeliversKeyMaterial` (material shipped to a flagged v6 runner, not
  leaked into Env/Secrets, audited, `injects_secret` armed);
  `TestIngestMasksDeliveredKeyMaterial` (a delivered key echoed in output is
  masked); `TestMaterializeKeys` / `TestMergeKeyMapDeliveredWins` (agent 0600 file
  lifecycle + delivered-wins precedence); runref key-audit `ResolvedRef` coverage.

### Residual

- memfd (vs a tmpfs file) is a future hardening; the per-log-chunk key re-resolve
  (including a Vault fetch for vault-source keys) inherits the existing per-chunk
  secret re-resolve cost.

## 0.49.13 — Injection low-severity hardening sweep (R4: L1, L3–L4, L6–L9, UI)

**Date:** Jul 21, 2026

Remediation group R4 of the follow-up review
(the vault-integration-followup plan): the low-severity hardening
items around the claim fence, fail-closed reveals, list-handler auth, the Vault
HTTP client, binding limits, and the run-detail UI.

### Security

- **L1 — the claim fence no longer admits a flagged pre-v6 runner.** The
  secret-injection fence armed on `allow_secret_injection` alone, so a flagged
  **v5** runner claimed a binding-bearing run and then 409'd `agent_too_old` on
  every manifest fetch — stranding the run on the wrong runner instead of leaving
  it queued. `claimRun` now also requires `protocol_version >= 6` to claim a
  binding-bearing run.
- **L3 — a secret deleted mid-resolve fails closed instead of injecting `""`.**
  `secrets.Reveal` returned `("", nil)` on a missing row, so a TOCTOU delete
  (between the resolver's lookup and reveal) injected an empty value, and `POST
  /env-secrets/{id}/reveal` returned `200 {"value":""}` for a just-deleted secret.
  `Reveal` now returns `ErrSecretNotFound`; the resolver maps it to a fail-closed
  missing-reference, and the reveal handler returns 404.
- **L4 — the env-secrets / env-vars LIST handlers fail closed on a missing
  identity.** Both used `id, _ := auth.IdentityFrom(...)`, and a zero Identity has
  nil `AllowedScopes` — which the scope filter reads as **unrestricted** (every
  scope's values). They now check the `ok` and 401.

### Fixed

- **L6 — the private-CA Vault transport keeps `http.DefaultTransport` defaults.**
  `caTransport` built a bare `&http.Transport{}`, dropping `ProxyFromEnvironment`,
  keep-alives, and HTTP/2 — so an egress-proxy + private-CA deployment silently
  bypassed the proxy. It now clones `http.DefaultTransport` and overrides only
  `TLSClientConfig`.
- **L7 — `capabilities.vault` reflects whether a client is actually WIRED, not
  just configured.** After a fail-loud CA error `WireVaultClient` leaves the stub,
  yet `handleCapabilities` reported `vault=true` from `ResolveVaultRuntime` alone —
  so the SPA offered a vault option whose every reveal failed "unavailable." A new
  `secrets.Service.VaultConfigured()` (real-vs-stub) is now the reported signal.
- **L9 — reference-binding PUTs are capped at 256 rows per owner.** A full-replace
  otherwise inserted every deduped row, so a `ManageEnvVars` caller could push tens
  of thousands per request; `ReplaceBindings` now rejects an oversized set with a
  422 before any DB work.
- **Run-detail "Injected references" distinguishes an error from "none."**
  `RunReferences` rendered `[]` on any fetch error, so a 403/500 looked identical to
  a run that injected nothing; it now shows a distinct error line.

### Docs

- **L8 — `vaultRetryMax` comment corrected**: it is the TOTAL attempt count (loop
  condition `attempt < vaultRetryMax`), not "first attempt plus this many retries."

### Tests

- `TestClaimRunSecretInjectionGate` extended (flagged v5 does not claim; flagged v6
  does); `TestRevealMissingFailsClosed`; `TestVaultConfigured`;
  `TestCATransportKeepsDefaults`; `TestReplaceBindingsRowCap`. Frontend dist rebuilt.

## 0.49.12 — Injection robustness: dispatch-authoritative fail-closed, audit self-heal, binding audit (M5–M7)

**Date:** Jul 21, 2026

Remediation group R3 of the follow-up review
(the vault-integration-followup plan): the robustness edges around
the runner ingest fail-closed (M5, folding in L2), the dispatch-audit slot (M6),
and binding-write auditing (M7).

### Security

- **M5 — the runner log-ingest fail-closed is now authoritative to the DISPATCH
  decision, not live bindings.** `HandleIngestLog` re-enumerated a run's bindings
  each chunk to decide whether to fail closed; a binding **deleted mid-run** (its
  job pruned, or a full-replace PUT dropping it) produced a *clean-empty*
  enumeration — not an error — so a secret-bearing run silently flipped to the
  lenient path and an already-injected **vault-source** value (absent from the
  global redaction dictionary) persisted un-redacted in remaining chunks. A new
  `runs.injects_secret` flag (migration 620), set at manifest dispatch when a
  secret VALUE ships, now drives the decision: a flagged run refuses the chunk
  (`503`) whenever its redaction dictionary can't be rebuilt (resolve failure,
  redactor build failure, or an empty resolve). Because the flag — not the live
  `SecretsInjectionEnabled` read — governs, a run dispatched while injection was ON
  stays fail-closed after the kill-switch is flipped OFF (**L2**, folded in).
- **M6 — the dispatch-audit slot can no longer wedge "audited with no row".**
  `AuditInjectionOnce` claims `runs.injection_audited` then writes the audit,
  releasing the slot on write failure. The release reused the caller's request
  context, so an agent that disconnected mid-write failed BOTH the write and the
  release on the same canceled context — leaving the slot stuck at `1` with no
  `change_log` row **permanently**, and every manifest re-fetch then shipped secret
  values with the audit gone forever. The release now runs on a cancellation-proof
  context (`context.WithoutCancel` + timeout) and is logged; a **compare-and-repair**
  trusts an already-claimed slot only when a matching audit row actually exists,
  otherwise (re)writing it — self-healing any prior wedge on the next fetch.
- **M7 — binding writes now record the resulting set in the audit.** A binding
  full-replace is last-writer-wins, so a stale editor tab could silently resurrect a
  just-revoked binding, and its `change_log` row ("Jobs"/"Scripts", "updated", empty
  details) was indistinguishable from a tag edit. Binding PUTs now write the
  resulting set (`runref.AuditBindingSet`: sorted `kind:name`, never values; `(none)`
  for a revoke), making the change visible and diffable. (The optional
  optimistic-concurrency guard — reject a stale PUT with 409 — needs a coordinated
  OpenAPI + frontend contract change and is deferred; the audit-details half, the
  plan's priority, ships now.)

### Tests

- M5: `TestIngestFailsClosedAfterBindingDeletedMidRun` (delete a secret binding
  mid-run → 503, nothing persisted); existing fail-closed/masking tests updated to
  seed a dispatched (flagged) run.
- M6: `TestAuditReleaseOnWriteFailure` (write fails → slot released) and
  `TestAuditCompareAndRepair` (wedged slot self-heals; a genuine no-op re-call adds
  no duplicate).
- M7: `TestBindingWriteAuditNamesTheSet` (audit names the set; a revoke is a
  distinct non-empty `(none)` detail).
