## 0.49.11 — Injection RBAC scope story: bindings, resolver oracle, env-vars (M1–M4)

**Date:** Jul 21, 2026

Remediation group R2 of the follow-up review
(the vault-integration-followup plan): the MEDIUM RBAC edges — one
coherent "close the scope story" pass over binding writes (M1), the resolver's
operator-facing error (M2), reference-name disclosure (M3), and env-var writes
(M4).

### Security

- **M1 — reference-binding writes are now scope-checked.** `PUT
  /job-reference-bindings/{id}` and `PUT /script-reference-bindings/{name}`
  required only `ManageEnvVars`, so a `dev`-restricted manager could add a bogus
  binding to a **prod** job (every prod dispatch then fails closed) or empty a prod
  job's binding set (prod runs execute **without** their declared secrets — the
  declaration is simply gone). Bindings are access-control writes: job bindings now
  gate on the owner job's scope (404 out-of-scope, 403 on a global job); script
  bindings — shared across scopes, no scope column — require an **unrestricted**
  manager (DEC-3).
- **M2 — the resolver's fail-closed error is no longer a cross-scope existence
  oracle.** A missing reference and one that "exists only outside run scope"
  produced distinct operator-visible strings (SSH run log, runner 409 body), so an
  actor could probe any name one run at a time — defeating P1.7's 404-not-403
  design. A new `runref.ReferenceError` keeps the precise text in the server log
  but renders a single generic "reference `X` is unavailable for this run" to the
  operator for **both** cases (`errors.Is` classification preserved).
- **M3 — out-of-scope reference NAME disclosure closed (where the scope model
  allows).** The script-scan bare-name lint (`knownReferenceNames` +
  `LintBareNames`) queried `secrets`/`env_vars` **unfiltered**, so any session could
  confirm out-of-scope secret/var names by planting tokens in a script body; those
  queries are now scope-filtered by the caller's grants. `GET
  /job-reference-bindings/{id}` is scope-guarded (403 out-of-scope) to match `GET
  /runs/{id}/references`. `ssh_credentials` labels stay unfiltered (no scope column
  — accepted §8 limitation), and job **detail** itself remains unscoped pending the
  app-wide A5 "unrestricted signal" fix.
- **M4 — env-var writes are scoped (integrity, not just a list leak).** Env-var
  create/update/delete/tag had **no** scope check at any layer. With the resolver's
  scope-exact-beats-global ordering that is an integrity hole: a `dev`-restricted
  manager POSTing `{key:"DB_HOST", scope:"prod"}` makes a prod run's
  `AMADEUS_VAR_DB_HOST` resolve the attacker's value over the global row —
  controlling that scope's deploy targets/flags. Env-var writes now apply the same
  scope model as secrets via a new `loadEnvVarWritable` helper (target-scope
  `ScopeWritable` on create; existing-row writability on update/delete/tag; 404
  out-of-scope, 403 on a global row).

### Tests

- M1: restricted manager 404/403 on out-of-scope/global job bindings, 200 in
  scope; unrestricted writes global; script bindings 403 restricted / 200
  unrestricted.
- M2: same reference name yields identical operator text across out-of-scope vs
  missing DB states, precise server-log text still differs, `errors.Is` preserved.
- M3: restricted scan omits the out-of-scope secret name; out-of-scope job-binding
  read is 403.
- M4: env-var create/update/delete/tag scope matrix (mirrors the secret-scope
  tests) with the global row proven untouched by refused writes.

## 0.49.10 — Injection RBAC + Vault client singleton (H3–H4)

**Date:** Jul 21, 2026

Continues remediation group R1 of the follow-up review
(the vault-integration-followup plan): the last two HIGH items —
the global-secret RBAC hole (H3) and the wrapped-`secret_id` multi-client bug
(H4).

### Security

- **H3 — a scope-restricted manager can no longer delete, re-scope, migrate, or
  label a GLOBAL secret.** The secret write handlers (`PUT`/`DELETE`
  `/env-secrets/{id}`, `migrate-to-vault`, `env-secret-tags`) guarded the
  **existing** row only with the read predicate (`auth.ScopeAllowed`), which is
  always true for a global (scope `""`) row — so a `dev`-restricted `ManageEnvVars`
  actor could delete a global secret (fail-closing every scope's runs that bind
  it) or `PUT scope:"dev"` to **capture** it into their own scope and deny every
  other. A new `loadSecretWritable` helper adds an existing-row
  `auth.ScopeWritable(existing.Scope)` check to all four paths: a restricted actor
  now gets **403** on a global row (global existence is not scope-secret), while a
  genuinely out-of-scope non-global row still returns 404 (no existence oracle).
  Reveal is unchanged (a read, not in scope for this fix).

### Fixed

- **H4 — a response-wrapped Vault `secret_id` no longer breaks under multiple
  per-process clients.** `settings.WireVaultClient` is called from every subsystem
  that resolves vault-source rows (API server, SSH executor, runner, SSH-key
  backfill, probe executor), and each built its **own** `httpVaultClient`. With
  `AMADEUS_VAULT_SECRET_ID_WRAPPED=true` the single-use wrapping token unwraps
  once — whichever client won consumed it, and every other client `400`'d forever
  on its own `resolveSecretID`, so the losing executor failed closed on every
  vault-source run (and even a static `secret_id` meant 5× AppRole logins). The
  underlying client is now a **process singleton** cached (mutex-guarded) by
  resolved config, so all same-config callers share one client and one unwrap;
  distinct configs still get distinct clients (no cross-test bleed).
- **SSH-key backfill wired to the shared Vault client.** `sshkeys.Backfill` was
  the last un-wired `secrets.New`, so migrating a legacy key whose material lives
  in a **vault-source** secret was skipped-with-warning; it now resolves through
  the shared client. Unconfigured Vault ⇒ the stub, unchanged behavior.

### Tests

- H3: restricted manager blocked (403) from delete/update/migrate/tag of a global
  secret with the row left intact; unrestricted admin still manages it (200/204).
- H4: two independently-wired services reveal a vault-source secret with a wrapped
  `secret_id` and observe exactly one unwrap + one AppRole login (shared client).

## 0.49.9 — Injection confidentiality highs: argv leak + output exfil (H1–H2)

**Date:** Jul 21, 2026

First remediation group (R1) of the post-merge follow-up review
(the vault-integration-followup plan): the two exploitable
injected-secret **value** paths. Both close a channel the Cronomicon log redactor
could never reach — the remote host's process table (H1) and the A12 output
capture that fed downstream steps in plaintext (H2).

### Security

- **H1 — injected secrets no longer touch the remote command line (argv).** Both
  SSH executors previously rendered injected env as a `K='value' bash -c '…'`
  prefix concatenated into the single command string, so every injected secret sat
  on the **target** host's process argv — world-readable via `/proc/<pid>/cmdline`,
  permanently recorded by auditd `execve` logging (acute on the RHEL8 fleet), and
  captured by Windows 4688 / Sysmon for PowerShell. A leak on the remote process
  table is beyond the log redactor's reach. Env is now delivered on **stdin**
  (DEC-1 hand-off): POSIX interpreters read an export prelude then the body from
  stdin (`bash -s` / `sh -s`); python3 / perl / PowerShell read a native env
  prelude + body from stdin (`python3 -` / `perl` / `powershell -Command -`).
  Values never appear in any argv; no target-side sshd configuration is needed.
  The local-exec path (ansible/terraform) already delivered env via real
  `os/exec` and is unchanged.
- **H2 — A12 output markers can no longer exfiltrate an injected secret.**
  `::amadeus-output name=TOKEN::$AMADEUS_SECRET_API` captured the secret verbatim
  into `runs.outputs_json` (raw, pre-redaction) and then into a workflow child
  step's **plaintext** `env_json` — bypassing `allow_secret_injection` and the
  "never persist an injected value" invariant through the natural output idiom.
  Near-term policy (DEC-2) is **refuse**: the runner ingest fails the run **closed**
  at the capture site (before `outputs_json` is written) when any captured output
  value carries an injected secret — reason `output_secret_leak`, nothing
  propagated, the value still masked in the stored log. Because the leaking output
  is never persisted, no plaintext reaches a child step, so the opt-in
  sensitive-output channel (DEC-2 end-state) was not needed and remains deferred.

### Changed

- **Shared remote-command renderer.** The two near-duplicate command builders
  (`sshexec/target.go`, `agent/command.go`) now delegate to a new single-source
  `internal/remotecmd` package (`Render` → `{Cmd, Stdin}`), keeping the in-app SSH
  executor and the runner agent in lockstep and hosting the POSIX-identifier key
  filter once. Both `runTarget` sites attach `session.Stdin` only when the render
  carries one, so a no-injection run is byte-for-byte the pre-H1 command with EOF
  on stdin as before. The stale `target.go` "merged into the connection env
  in-memory only" comment is corrected.
- **Run-detail output masking now covers injected values.** `execution_mount.go`
  `redactOutputs` additionally masks via the run's **per-run injected dictionary**
  (resolved on the detail path only, so a runs-list page pays no per-row Vault
  round-trip), covering vault-source values the per-scope stored-secret redactor
  does not carry — fail-closed (mask all) when a declared secret can't be resolved.

### Tests

- `internal/remotecmd`: env-on-stdin for every interpreter, secret-never-in-argv
  sweep, per-interpreter quoting (incl. quote/newline/backslash), unsafe-key drop,
  and no-env argv-form preservation.
- SSH executor loopback-sshd harness upgraded to capture stdin and assert the
  injected secret is absent from argv (`cmd: bash -s`) and present in the stdin
  export prelude; agent renderer tests adapted to the `Rendered` shape.
- H2 refuse: single-step secret→output failed closed with no `outputs_json`
  persisted and the value masked; non-leaking output still captured; run-detail
  masks an injected value and fails closed when unresolvable;
  `firstOutputLeakingSecret` unit coverage.

### Residual

- H1: a job body that consumes stdin sees EOF after its program is read (for
  `bash -s`, a `read` consumes subsequent body lines) — SSH-exec run-types do not
  read stdin by default; accepted and recorded in predecessor §8.
- H2: the opt-in sensitive-output channel (route intentional derived-secret
  outputs through the gated `Secrets` block) is the documented end-state, not yet
  built — the refuse is honest but fails a run that intentionally emitted a
  derived credential downstream.

## 0.49.8 — Vault-source SSH credentials + Phase-2 wiring/docs (P2.4–P2.5)

**Date:** Jul 21, 2026

Completes Phase 2 of the vault-integration plan: vault-source SSH
credentials resolve live, the Vault client is actually wired into **both**
executors (correcting a gap the plan assumed was "free"), and the operator docs
land.

### Fixed

- **Vault client was never wired into the executors** (correction to P2.2's
  "free by construction"). The SSH executor (`sshexec.New`) and the runner
  (`runner.New`) each built their own `secrets.Service` with the **stub** Vault
  client, so vault-source secret injection silently failed on both real dispatch
  paths — only the API server had a wired client. Centralized the wiring in a new
  `settings.WireVaultClient` (env-or-DB AppRole + the D4 hardening knobs) and call
  it from all three constructors, so vault-source rows now resolve identically
  everywhere. Unconfigured Vault ⇒ the stub, unchanged behavior.

### Added

- **Vault-source SSH credentials (P2.4 / D8 completion)**: a `source='vault'`
  `ssh_credentials` row now resolves its private-key PEM live from Vault at the
  stored `vault_ref`, through the same configured client as vault secrets. Wired
  into `internal/sshkeys/resolve.go` (`decryptCredential`) and threaded through
  `ResolveSigner` (the SSH-executor connection path) and `ResolveMaterialByName`
  (the runner key-delivery path) via `secrets.Service.Vault()`. Fails closed when
  no client is wired — a vault key is unusable rather than silently empty.
- **Operator runbook** `backend/deploy/vault-runbook.md`: AppRole creation,
  least-privilege policy scoping, `secret_id` delivery (static and
  response-wrapped) and the rotation caveat, namespace/CA config, the fail-closed
  outage model, Vault Agent sidecar retirement, and a verification checklist.

### Changed

- **Docs (P2.5)**: `deploy/env-matrix.md` and `deploy/amadeus.env.example` now
  document the D4 hardening knobs (namespace/CA/wrapped secret_id), the
  `AMADEUS_SECRETS_INJECTION_ENABLED` kill-switch, and the namespace env-vs-DB
  precedence row. Stale "stubbed"/"Phase 2" comments in `secrets/{vault,service,
  kek}.go` now describe the real wired client.

### Tests

- Vault-source SSH credential resolves as raw material (runner path) and as a
  parsed signer (SSH-executor path); fail-closed with no client wired and on an
  empty ref (`internal/sshkeys/resolve_vault_test.go`).

## 0.49.7 — Vault into the injection workflow (P2.1–P2.3)

**Date:** Jul 21, 2026

Phase 2 of the vault-integration plan: Vault becomes a *source
backend* behind the same dispatch-time injection seam Phase 1 built. Vault-source
secrets flow through the identical resolver — the redaction, audit, and
fail-closed guarantees already hold by construction — and the HTTP Vault client
gains the operator-hardening knobs (D4), each **dormant until its own config is
set**. No default behavior changes: with Vault unconfigured, everything works
exactly as before.

### Fixed

- **`caps.vault` now reflects env-**or**-DB config** (P2.1). The
  `/api/v1/capabilities` flag was computed env-only (`VaultAppRole`) while the
  client wires env-or-DB (`ResolveVaultRuntime`), so a **DB-only** Vault config
  (set via the settings page, no `AMADEUS_VAULT_*` env) hid the vault-source
  option in the SPA even though the backend could serve it. It now uses the same
  resolver the client does. The 409 on human reveal of a vault-source secret is
  **kept** (Model A — humans never see Vault values through Cronomicon; only the
  internal dispatch path reveals).

### Added

- **Vault client hardening (D4)** in `internal/secrets/vault_http.go`, via a new
  `NewVaultClientWithOptions` / `VaultOptions`. Every knob is off unless
  configured:
  - **`X-Vault-Namespace`** header — from `AMADEUS_VAULT_NAMESPACE` (env wins) or
    the DB-backed `vault_config.namespace`; sent on every request (Vault
    Enterprise / HCP namespaces).
  - **Private CA** — `AMADEUS_VAULT_CA_FILE` pins the client transport to a PEM
    bundle instead of the system roots. A missing/invalid bundle **fails loud**
    (the client is left disabled) rather than silently trusting system roots.
  - **Bounded retry/backoff** (always on, safe) — transport errors, `429`, and
    `5xx` are retried up to 3 attempts with exponential backoff; `4xx` (bad
    creds/path) is terminal and not retried.
  - **Response-wrapped `secret_id`** — `AMADEUS_VAULT_SECRET_ID_WRAPPED=true`
    treats the configured secret_id as a single-use wrapping token, unwrapped
    once via `sys/wrapping/unwrap` and cached in memory; static long-lived
    secret_id remains the default. (Token *refresh* stays the existing
    lazy-at-80%-of-lease re-login — a request-driven client needs no background
    goroutine; periodic secret_id **rotation** + operator runbook remain the
    deferred P2.5 tail.)

### Tests

- **Vault-source through injection (P2.2)** — verification is now covered by
  tests rather than only "free by construction": a mixed **stored + vault** run
  resolves both through the same path, the vault value lands in the per-run
  redaction dictionary (it is absent from the stored global dictionary), and the
  dispatch audit records the vault secret's provenance as `vault`. A
  Vault-unavailable bound secret (reachable-but-failing **and** default stub)
  **fails the resolve closed** — no partial injection, no silent skip.
- **Client hardening** — namespace header sent iff configured; retry succeeds
  after transient `5xx` and does **not** retry `4xx`; wrapped secret_id is
  unwrapped exactly once and reused across fetches; a bad CA bundle errors at
  construction.

## 0.49.6 — Run injection: UI (P1.8)

**Date:** Jul 21, 2026

The operator-facing surface for dispatch-time injection
(the vault-integration plan, P1.8): declare a job's/script's consumed
references, see which references a run received, and grant a runner the trust to
receive injected secret material. Never displays a secret value — names only.

### Added

- **Reference-binding editor** on Job and Script detail (a new reusable
  `ReferenceBindingsEditor`). Add/remove `AMADEUS_SECRET_*` / `AMADEUS_VAR_*` /
  `AMADEUS_KEY_*` bindings with a kind picker + name field (datalist of known Env
  Vars rows), a ⚠ hint for a bound name with no matching row, and full-replace
  save. Scripts additionally get **"Suggest from body"** — scans the script text to
  prefill bindings and surfaces the bare-name migration lint. Editing needs
  ManageEnvVars; without it the editor is read-only.
- **Run detail → "Injected references"**: the references a run actually injected,
  via a new `GET /api/v1/runs/{traceId}/references` (scope-guarded like the run
  detail; names + derived reference only, never values). Sourced from the P1.6
  dispatch audit — the authoritative dispatch-time snapshot, so it never overstates
  from later binding edits, SSH-skipped keys, or refused runs. Renders nothing for a
  run that injected none.
- **Per-runner "Secret injection" toggle** on the runner detail, with blast-radius
  helper text ("receives resolved secret values in its manifest — grant only to
  runners you trust…"). Warning-toned when on; gated on ConfigureApp (disabled +
  explained otherwise), calling `PUT /api/v1/runners/{id}/secret-injection`.
- OpenAPI: the `/runs/{traceId}/references` and `/runners/{id}/secret-injection`
  paths (both spec copies); frontend types regenerated. Backend test for the new
  run-references endpoint (union of job + script bindings, deduped, 404 on unknown
  run).

## 0.49.5 — Run injection: secret RBAC scope-tightening (P1.7)

**Date:** Jul 21, 2026

Makes "Cronomicon RBAC governs secret access" actually true
(the vault-integration plan, P1.7 / D3 — scope enforced on **use and
management**). Previously any authenticated session could enumerate every secret's
key/scope/vault-ref, and a scope-restricted manager could reveal, edit, or delete a
secret in any scope. Now secret metadata is gated + scope-filtered, and every
secret management operation enforces the actor's scope grants.

### Security

- **`GET /api/v1/env-secrets` + `GET /api/v1/env-vars` scope-filtered.** A
  scope-restricted session sees only their-scope + global rows; an unrestricted
  admin sees all. Secret filtering lives in `secrets.Service.List(ctx,
  allowedScopes)`. Both endpoints stay `RequireSession` (NOT `ManageEnvVars`-gated):
  non-manager Job Composer / Scripts views legitimately read secret-KEY metadata,
  so the scope-filter — not a permission wall — is the enforced control here. Values
  stay protected (reveal needs ManageEnvVars + scope). Variables carry plaintext
  values, so their cross-scope leak was a value leak, now closed.
- **Secret management is scope-enforced (D3).** Reveal, update, delete,
  migrate-to-vault, and tag-edit reject a secret outside the actor's scopes with
  **404** (no existence oracle — a restricted operator can't probe for secrets they
  can't reach), via a `loadSecretInScope` helper. Create and scope-changing update
  reject a disallowed **target** scope with **403** via `auth.ScopeWritable`, which
  (unlike the read predicate `auth.ScopeAllowed`) also forbids a restricted actor
  from writing to the **global** scope — a global secret injects into every scope.
  Both predicates are the single shared mirror of the run-log/execution IDOR guards.

### Tests

- Unit: `secrets.List` scope filtering (global always; restricted; admin sees all).
- API (trusted-header RBAC harness with scope-restricted roles): list is
  session-readable by a non-manager but scope-filtered (viewer 200, filtered);
  restricted-admin list filtered; reveal in-scope/global 200 vs out-of-scope 404;
  create out-of-scope / global 403, in-scope 201; update moving out-of-scope 403;
  delete / migrate / tag out-of-scope 404.

### Known limitation

- **Scope-model sentinel (pre-existing A5).** "Unrestricted" and "restricted to
  zero scopes" are indistinguishable — clearing a role's scope grants un-restricts
  it. This is how every existing scope guard behaves; P1.7 mirrors it rather than
  diverging. An app-wide fix (a distinct "unrestricted" signal) is tracked
  separately. Documented at `auth.ScopeAllowed`.

---

## 0.49.4 — Run injection: dispatch audit (P1.6)

**Date:** Jul 21, 2026

Records **which references a run received** at dispatch time
(the vault-integration plan, P1.6). Both executors now write a
`change_log` `Secrets`/`injected` event when they resolve a run's bindings —
reference names, kinds, and backing source (`stored`/`vault`) only, **never
values** — and **fail closed** if the audit cannot be recorded, mirroring the
existing secret-reveal handler: a run does not receive injected references without
an audit trail.

### Added

- **Dispatch-injection audit.** At resolution, the SSH executor (`execute`) and the
  runner manifest handler (`HandleGetManifest`) write one `change_log` row per run:
  `category=Secrets`, `action=injected`, `target=<trace id>`, `actor=<triggered_by>`
  (`system` when unattributed), and `details` = a deterministic JSON payload of the
  run scope + the sorted set of injected references (`{kind,name,source}`). The
  resolver now surfaces this metadata via `Resolved.Refs` (`runref.ResolvedRef`) and
  a `runref.AuditDetails` renderer — value-free by construction.
- Migration **610** adds `runs.injection_audited`. The runner manifest is
  re-fetchable (agent retries), so the audit is written **exactly once per run**,
  guarded by this flag; the SSH executor sets it too for a uniform invariant.
- Tests: audit payload determinism/no-values; resolver `Refs` population with
  source; SSH + runner audit-once (re-fetch does not duplicate); `system`
  attribution; fail-closed on a broken audit sink (500 `audit_failed` on the runner
  path; run failed on the SSH path); `injection_audited` left unset on audit failure
  so a retry re-attempts.

### Security

- **Fail-closed audit** (mirrors the reveal handler). If `WriteChangeLog` errors,
  the runner manifest is withheld (`500 audit_failed`) and the SSH run is failed —
  injected reference material is never delivered without a recorded audit trail.
  Availability tradeoff documented in the plan §8.

---

## 0.49.3 — Run injection: per-run log redaction on the runner path (P1.5)

**Date:** Jul 21, 2026

Feeds the dispatch-time resolver's redaction output into the **runner
log-ingest** sink (the vault-integration plan, P1.5), so a value the
run actually injected is masked in its stored logs even when the global
stored-secret dictionary does not contain it. The SSH executor already seeded its
log redactor from the resolver in P1.3; this brings the runner path to parity and
makes the redaction seam ready for vault-source secret values (Phase 2), which
never appear in `secrets.RedactionValues`. (Key material is still filtered out
before resolution on both executors, so D8 delivery must also relax that filter to
feed redaction.) Also closes the runner-ingest fail-open gap flagged in the P1.4
review.

### Added

- **Per-run resolver redaction at ingest.** `HandleIngestLog` now re-resolves the
  run's declared secret/variable bindings and adds the resulting sensitive values
  (secret values + key material; variable values stay log-safe, D7) to the
  redaction dictionary alongside the scope env-vars, the global stored-secret
  dictionary, and override-env values. Shared with the manifest path via a new
  `resolveInjectableReferences` helper (keys warned only on the manifest path so
  the per-chunk redaction path stays quiet).
- Tests: the redaction helper surfaces the injected secret and excludes the
  log-safe variable; an injected secret echoed in output is masked in the
  persisted log; the kill-switch renders the helper inert.

### Changed / Security

- **Fail-closed runner log ingest** (mirrors `sshexec.openLog`, P1.3). A run that
  injects a secret whose redaction dictionary cannot be completed — the per-run
  resolve failed (e.g. a Vault outage or a binding deleted mid-run leaving the
  value unmaskable) or the base redactor could not be built — now returns
  `503 redactor_unavailable` and persists **nothing** (no log bytes, no offset
  advance, no finalize) rather than write raw output that might contain the
  un-masked secret. The fail-closed decision does not silently degrade: if binding
  *enumeration* itself errors (kinds unknown), the chunk fails closed rather than
  assume the run is secret-free — the guard that protects Phase-2 vault-source
  values from a single transient `reference_bindings` error. The agent re-sends once the fault clears. A run with no
  injected secret keeps the prior lenient best-effort behavior. Availability
  tradeoff documented in the plan §8.

---

## 0.49.2 — Run injection: runner-executor path + capability gate (P1.4)

**Date:** Jul 20, 2026

Extends dispatch-time injection to the **runner executor**
(the vault-integration plan, P1.4). A runner-dispatched run now
receives the Secrets + Variables its job/script declared, resolved server-side and
shipped in a dedicated manifest block — gated so only operator-trusted runners
ever receive secret material. This deliberately relaxes the historical "the
manifest never carries secret bytes" invariant for the runner path, behind three
independent gates. Key-*material* delivery (D8) is deferred to a focused
follow-up; both executors now inject secrets/variables/run-context symmetrically.

### Added

- **Runner manifest injection** (protocol **v6**). `GET /runs/{id}/manifest`
  resolves the run's declared reference bindings and ships the resolved
  `AMADEUS_SECRET_*` / `AMADEUS_VAR_*` values in a new sensitive **`Secrets`**
  block (separate from the plaintext `Env`); `AMADEUS_RUN_*` run context merges
  into `Env`. Three gates protect it: **fail-closed** on any unresolvable binding,
  a **defense-in-depth** refusal to ship secrets to a runner not flagged for
  injection, and a **hard-fail** if the assigned agent speaks an older protocol
  (it would ignore the field and run without the declared secrets). The agent
  injects these values into the child (ansible/terraform) or remote (bash/…)
  process env.
- **Per-runner secret-injection trust flag** (migration 600,
  `runners.allow_secret_injection`). An operator grant — never agent-self-declared
  — set via `PUT /api/v1/runners/{id}/secret-injection` (ConfigureApp), surfaced
  as `allowSecretInjection` on the Runner response. Only a flagged runner may
  claim a run whose job/script declares reference bindings.
- **Claim-time capability gate.** `claimRun` now leaves a binding-bearing run
  queued unless the claiming runner is flagged for injection — a live check
  against the `reference_bindings` table (the same state the manifest resolver
  reads), mirroring the existing agency-isolation clause. The stuck-run hint
  (`EligibleOnlineRunnerForRun`) got the matching bridge.

### Changed

- The runner manifest's "the manifest never carries secret bytes" comments now
  document the P1.4 exception and its gating.
- An `AMADEUS_KEY_*` reference on a runner run is **warned and skipped** (as on
  the SSH path): runner key-*material* delivery (D8) is a follow-up. The `Keys`
  manifest field and `ManifestKey` type ship now so it needs no further protocol
  bump.

---

## 0.49.1 — Run injection: SSH-executor wiring + run context (P1.3)

**Date:** Jul 20, 2026

Wires the v0.49.0 dispatch resolver into the in-app SSH executor
(the vault-integration plan, P1.3). An SSH-executed run now resolves
the references its job (and referenced script) declared and injects the values
into the remote command at connection time — masked in logs, fail-closed, gated
by the same kill-switch. The runner executor (P1.4) is next; nothing here reaches
runner-dispatched runs.

### Added

- **SSH-executor reference injection.** Before opening the run log, the executor
  resolves the run's declared Secrets + Variables bindings (from its job and, when
  it references one, its script) and merges the derived `AMADEUS_SECRET_*` /
  `AMADEUS_VAR_*` values into the remote command env — **connection-time only,
  never written back to `env_json`**. Resolution is **fail-closed**: a missing,
  out-of-scope, or un-revealable binding fails the run instead of executing it
  without the secret it declared. Injected secret values (and any key material)
  seed the log redactor, so they can never surface un-masked.
- **`AMADEUS_RUN_*` run context.** A fixed, dispatcher-owned set is now injected
  into every SSH run: `AMADEUS_RUN_ID`, `_JOB`, `_JOB_SOURCE`, `_SCOPE`, `_TYPE`,
  `_TRIGGERED_BY`, `_EXECUTOR`. Defined once in `internal/envref`; documented in
  the namespace contract (`deploy/env-matrix.md`). Fulfils the namespace plan's
  reserved-but-uninjected `AMADEUS_RUN_*` (N-D4) for this executor.

### Changed

- **SSH executor `claim`** now also snapshots `script_ref` and `triggered_by` off
  the run (the script binding owner and the run-context actor).
- A declared `AMADEUS_KEY_*` reference on an SSH-executed run is **warned and
  skipped**, not injected: delivering a key *file* to a remote target host is a
  distinct mechanism from the runner's local memfd delivery (D8), and is deferred
  with the runner path (P1.4).

---

## 0.49.0 — Run injection: reference bindings + dispatch resolver (P1.1–P1.2)

**Date:** Jul 20, 2026

First slice of the reframed injection-first plan (Phase 1). A job or script now declares which Env Vars references it consumes, and
a dispatch-time resolver turns those declarations into injectable values —
backend-agnostic by construction (secrets route through the existing
source-transparent `Reveal`, so Vault is simply one source wired in later). This
release lands the data model, the resolver, and the authoring API; the executor
wiring that actually injects into runs (P1.3/P1.4) and RBAC tightening (P1.7)
follow. Injection is inert until those seams land, and is gated by a kill-switch
regardless.

### Added

- **Reference-binding data model** (migration `590_reference_bindings`): a
  `reference_bindings` table keying an owner triple `(kind, source, name)` —
  mirroring the `definition_schedules` owner model — to the Env Vars references it
  declares by **bare** row name and section (`secret`/`var`/`key`). The derived
  `AMADEUS_<SECTION>_<name>` reference is never stored; it is computed on read
  (D2 = 2B explicit binding).
- **`internal/runref` dispatch resolver** (`ResolveRunReferences`): resolves a
  run's declared bindings into `{Env, Keys, Redact}` — Secrets → sensitive values
  (via `secrets.Service.Reveal`, stored **or** Vault), Variables → log-safe values,
  SSH Keys → decrypted key material. Scope-enforced and **fail-closed**: a binding
  whose row lives only outside the run's scope errors (`ErrOutOfScope`), a missing
  row errors (`ErrMissingReference`), and a scope-restricted actor cannot inject
  into a scope they lack. Secret values and key material populate the redaction
  dictionary; variable values (log-safe) do not (D7).
- **Reference-binding scanner**: `ScanBody` discovers derived references
  (`AMADEUS_SECRET_X`, …) in a script body — the reserved prefix makes discovery
  precise (the namespace plan's W5 handoff) — plus a **bare-name lint** flagging
  reference sites still using a bare name that matches a known Env Vars row.
- **Reference-binding API** (`/job-reference-bindings/{jobId}`,
  `/script-reference-bindings/{name}` GET/PUT, `/script-reference-scan/{name}`
  GET). Reads are session-gated; the full-replace writes require **ManageEnvVars**
  (+ CSRF) — a binding is a least-privilege access control over secrets, so it
  sits behind the secret-management gate, not the any-user tags gate. Row names
  are validated against the derived-reference charset (secret names bar the
  reserved KEK names). Documented in both byte-identical OpenAPI copies.
- **`AMADEUS_SECRETS_INJECTION_ENABLED`** kill-switch (default **on**; D5). Spelled
  plural so it sits outside the reserved `AMADEUS_SECRET_*` reference prefix; when
  off, the resolver injects nothing.

### Changed

- **`internal/sshkeys`** gains `ResolveMaterialByName` — resolves a stored SSH
  credential's raw key material (PEM) by label, for the key-file injection the
  runner path will use (D8). Refactored to share the decrypt path with the
  existing in-process signer resolution. Vault-source key resolution stays a
  Phase-2 stub.

---

## 0.48.3 — Env-var namespace: rollout (W6)

**Date:** Jul 20, 2026

Completes the env-var namespace plan (W1–W6). This release lands the in-repo rollout artifacts; the remaining reference-
site migration is operator-owned and incremental (the server dual-reads the KEK
and resolves both bare and derived references, so there is no flag-day).

### Changed

- **`docker-compose.yml` KEK env switched to `AMADEUS_KEK*`** (from
  `AMADEUS_SECRET_KEK*`). The container now receives `AMADEUS_KEK` /
  `AMADEUS_KEK_FILE`, sourced with a fallback —
  `${AMADEUS_KEK:-${AMADEUS_SECRET_KEK:-}}` — so an un-renamed DockHand env-panel
  var keeps working. Rename the panel var at your convenience; no coordinated
  restart is needed.

### Added

- **Namespace rollout runbook** in `deploy/env-matrix.md`: the incremental,
  no-flag-day procedure for adopting the derived-reference scheme — rename the
  server KEK env, then move reference *uses* (scripts → `AMADEUS_SECRET_/VAR_…`,
  inventories → `lookup('env','AMADEUS_KEY_…')`, host `authKeyEnvVar` fields →
  `AMADEUS_KEY_<label>`) at your own pace, verifying each site independently with
  a doctor auth-chain probe or a test run. The Vault Agent sidecar rename remains
  a separate later effort (N-D5); the agent's prefixed→bare fallback lets an
  inventory migrate ahead of it.

## 0.48.2 — Env-var namespace: Env Vars UI affordances (W5)

**Date:** Jul 20, 2026

Surfaces the namespace contract in the UI. The Env Vars page now shows, per row,
the **derived reference** an operator copies into a script or inventory, so the
reference the server resolves (v0.48.1) is discoverable rather than something you
have to know to type.

### Added

- **Derived `reference` per row** on all three Env Vars tabs (Variables, Secrets,
  SSH Keys): the expanded row detail shows the `AMADEUS_VAR_<key>` /
  `AMADEUS_SECRET_<key>` / `AMADEUS_KEY_<label>` reference in monospace with a
  **copy-to-clipboard** control and a one-line value-vs-path hint. Nothing is
  renamed — the row keeps its bare name; the reference is display-only (read from
  the API's read-only `reference` field).
- **Per-tab helper banner** stating how to reference that section's values and its
  semantics — Variables/Secrets resolve to a **value**, SSH Keys to a **key-file
  path** on the executing host. Theme-aware (light + dark).

The D2 binding scanner and the bare-name-reference lint (flagging un-migrated
reference sites) remain a handoff to the vault plan's M2/M4 — the reserved prefix
is what makes that scan precise.

## 0.48.1 — Env-var namespace: derived-reference resolution + run-env guard (W3–W4)

**Date:** Jul 20, 2026

Second increment of the env-var namespace contract
(the namespace-update plan). Where v0.48.0 landed the naming rule and
docs, this release makes the reserved prefixes **operational and injector-owned**:
Cronomicon now resolves derived references, validates that new rows produce legal
references, and refuses to let operator-authored env define any `AMADEUS_*` name.
A new stdlib-only `internal/envref` package is the single source of truth for the
contract, shared by the server and the runner agent.

### Added

- **Derived-reference resolution (W3).** A reference like
  `AMADEUS_KEY_ansible_rh8_key` / `AMADEUS_SECRET_NWD_BECOME_PASS` /
  `AMADEUS_VAR_FOO` now resolves by stripping the reserved prefix verbatim and
  routing **deterministically** to one section (SSH Keys → `ssh_credentials` by
  label, Secrets → `secrets` by key, Variables → `env_vars` by key). The
  server-side SSH signer path (`sshexec.loadSigner`) and the runner agent both
  understand references; a bare name keeps today's `secrets`→`env_vars` fallback
  chain for the transition. A prefixed reference that does not resolve is a hard
  error — never a silent fall-through.
- **Agent reference bridge.** The runner strips `AMADEUS_KEY_` before its
  key-dir/key-map lookup (files keep bare names), and resolves an
  `AMADEUS_SECRET_`/`AMADEUS_VAR_` env passthrough with a **prefixed→bare
  fallback**, so an updated inventory keeps working against an un-migrated
  `secrets.env` (sidecar decoupling, N-D5).
- **Read-only `reference` field** on the EnvVar, EnvSecret, and SshCredential API
  schemas (both byte-identical OpenAPI copies; frontend types regenerated) — the
  derived reference an operator copies, surfaced beside the bare name.

### Changed

- **Row-name validation (W3)** on create/update in all three sections: names must
  be POSIX identifiers (`[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`), may not start with `AMADEUS_`,
  and (Secrets) may not be a reserved KEK name. Failures return **422**. Existing
  rows are never re-validated. **Breaking for new writes:** SSH-credential labels
  can no longer contain `-`/`.` (they broke the derived `AMADEUS_KEY_<label>`
  env-var name); rename affected labels to snake_case. The demo seed's SSH key was
  renamed to `prod_deploy_ed25519` accordingly.
- **Absolute run-env reserved guard (W4, N-D1).** Operator-authored env may no
  longer define **any** `AMADEUS_*` key — enforced at write/ingest time across the
  Job Composer (job env + inline/reusable schedule env), standalone schedule
  create/update, workflow-bound schedules, per-run overrides, and workflow step
  inputs. Inventory ingest additionally rejects a **literal** `AMADEUS_*=` var
  assignment (a `lookup('env','AMADEUS_…')` *reference* stays valid and is the
  intended pattern). A config regression test locks the invariant that no server
  config name lives under a reserved prefix (the dual-read KEK aliases excepted).

## 0.48.0 — Env-var namespace: reserved reference prefixes + KEK eviction (W1–W2)

**Date:** Jul 20, 2026

First increment of the env-var namespace contract
(the namespace-update plan, **Option B**): make every `AMADEUS_*`
name self-classifying. A small, **closed set of reserved reference prefixes** —
`AMADEUS_VAR_`, `AMADEUS_SECRET_`, `AMADEUS_KEY_`, `AMADEUS_RUN_` — names things
Cronomicon resolves and injects into runs; **everything else** under `AMADEUS_*` is
server/runner configuration. An operator reading a script, inventory, or env file
can now tell config from an injected reference at a glance. This release lands the
**contract + docs (W1)** and the **KEK eviction (W2)**; derived-reference
resolution, the run-env guard, and UI affordances (W3–W5) follow.

The one genuinely confusing config name — the stored-secret **KEK**, which read
exactly like "a store secret named KEK" — is evicted out of the reserved
`AMADEUS_SECRET_*` prefix to `AMADEUS_KEK*`. The change is **fully
backward-compatible**: the old names keep working as a dual-read deprecated alias.

### Changed

- **KEK env vars renamed to `AMADEUS_KEK*`** (the KEK is app config, not a store
  secret): `AMADEUS_KEK_FILE`, `AMADEUS_KEK`, `AMADEUS_KEK_VERSION`, and the
  rotation forms `AMADEUS_KEK_<N>` / `AMADEUS_KEK_<N>_FILE`. The deprecated
  `AMADEUS_SECRET_KEK*` names still resolve (config `Load` and the historical-KEK
  rotation lookup both dual-read, new-name-wins), so no deployment must change on
  upgrade. `config.go` collects a **single startup deprecation warning** naming
  every legacy KEK var still in use; the `no KEK configured` and
  `AMADEUS_KEK_VERSION` validation messages now name the new forms.
- **Docs:** `deploy/env-matrix.md` gains a leading **Namespace** section (the rule,
  the four reference prefixes, the derived-reference model, and the KEK rename
  table) and its KEK rows move to the new names; `backend/README.md`,
  `deploy/amadeus.env.example`, `deploy/deployment-guide.md`,
  `deploy/backup-restore.md`, and `deploy/security-review.md` follow, each noting
  the old name as a deprecated alias. The Runner **Security Guide** gains a
  "Referencing Cronomicon values" section (the four prefixes, derived-reference rule,
  value-vs-path semantics, and secret-handling hygiene:
  `: "${AMADEUS_SECRET_X:?not injected}"` fail-fast, quote every expansion, no
  echo/argv, `set +x`).
- **Vault plan cross-link** (the vault-integration plan): recorded as
  **D6**; the D5 kill-switch recommendation is respelled to
  `AMADEUS_SECRETS_INJECTION_ENABLED` (**plural** — outside the reserved prefix).

## 0.47.29 — Runners: Vault Agent sidecar for runner-local secrets (opt-in)

**Date:** Jul 15, 2026

A first, reversible step toward "Cronomicon/Vault is the source of truth for a
runner's credentials" (the stopgap ahead of the control-plane secret delivery in
the vault-integration plan, Decision 1C). Lets an operator make
**HashiCorp Vault the source of truth** for NAME-referenced runner secrets — an
Ansible `become`/sudo password, WinRM passwords, anything a play resolves via
`{{ lookup('env','NAME') }}` — instead of hand-editing `secrets.env`. Cronomicon
stays **names-only (D1)**: the value is rendered beside the runner by a Vault
Agent under its own AppRole and never crosses the control-plane → runner channel.
Deploy artifacts + wiring only; no server, protocol, or agent-binary change.

### Added

- **`deploy/vault-agent/`** — an opt-in Vault Agent sidecar: `vault-agent.hcl`
  (AppRole auto-auth, no token sink — the runner never gets a Vault token),
  `secrets.env.ctmpl` (binds KV-v2 fields to env-var NAMEs), and a hardened
  `amadeus-vault-agent.service` (renders `/etc/amadeus-runner/secrets.env` as
  `0640 root:amadeus-runner`, ordered `Before=amadeus-runner.service`). `README.md`
  covers the model, threat notes, response-wrapped `secret_id`, rotation, and a
  worked `ansible_become_password` example.

### Changed

- **`amadeus-runner.service`** (and the unit `runner-install.sh` generates) now
  source an **optional** `EnvironmentFile=-/etc/amadeus-runner/secrets.env`. The
  `-` prefix makes it a no-op when no sidecar/secrets file is present, so the
  line is non-breaking for existing runners and also documents the standard place
  for a hand-managed secrets file.
- **`amadeus-runner.env.example`** documents the runner-local secrets file and
  the sidecar as the way to source `become`/WinRM passwords by NAME.

### Notes

- This is a **pilot stopgap**, not the end state: it gives no per-job secret
  binding, no control-plane visibility, and no UI. Those arrive with the 1C
  manifest `Secrets` block + `secret-injection` capability work still tracked in
  the vault-integration plan. Nothing here blocks that path.

**Date:** Jul 15, 2026

Phase 5 (final) of the runner-auth unification
(the runner-update plan). Documents the Phase 1–4 simplifications so
operators have one place that explains the whole auth chain. Docs only.

### Changed

- **Security guide** (`runner-security.html`) gains a "How a runner
  authenticates, end to end" subsection under §2: the three execution paths as a

## 0.47.27 — Runners: declared key names in the Runner detail

**Date:** Jul 15, 2026

Phase 4 of the runner-auth unification.
Credential coverage becomes visible *before* a run fails: each runner now
declares the credential names it can resolve, shown as chips in the expanded
Runner detail. Display-only this release (no server-side red/green
cross-reference yet). No server or protocol change — the field rides the existing
`additionalProperties: true` toolchains blob, stored verbatim by the server.

### Added

- **`keyNames` in the declared toolchains blob** — the agent reports the
  credential NAMES it can resolve to a local key (key-map keys + key-dir
  basenames, `.pub` siblings ignored). Names only — never paths or key material.
  A pre-Phase-4 agent omits it; the field re-declares automatically on the first
  poll after a binary upgrade (the version bump changes the drift digest).
- **"Key names" row in the Runner detail** — a row of mono chips next to
  Toolchains, with a tooltip explaining these are the local credential names the
  runner can resolve (a host's `authKeyEnvVar` must match one). Shows `—` for a
  runner that hasn't re-declared yet.
- Demo seed: two runners now carry a realistic `toolchains` blob (ansible-core,
  collections, checkout/vault/sandboxed, `keyNames`) so the detail previews the
  feature; the rest stay `—` to show the empty state.

### Changed

- OpenAPI `toolchains` schema description (both spec copies) notes the `keyNames`
  field; codegen regenerated. No shape change — it remains
  `additionalProperties: true`.

## 0.47.26 — Runners: auto `--private-key` for single-key ansible runs

**Date:** Jul 15, 2026

Phase 3 of the runner-auth unification.
Closes the last onboarding seam: the server already knows each target's key
name, so when a run's hosts all share one key the agent now hands it to ansible
directly — a new scope needs neither an inventory `ansible_ssh_private_key_file`
nor an env lookup. Agent-only; no server or protocol change.

### Added

- **Auto `--private-key` for single-key ansible runs.** When every resolved
  target shares exactly one `authKeyEnvVar` that resolves to a local key file,
  the agent appends `--private-key <path>` to `ansible-playbook` (before `-i`, so
  the existing flag order is unchanged). Purely additive — an inventory
  `ansible_ssh_private_key_file` host/group var still overrides per host — and it
  applies to body-only and checkout runs alike. A run whose hosts use **multiple**
  key names is left to the inventory / env bridge and emits one provenance line
  naming the keys it did not wire; a run with no key names, or `-no-auth-bridge`,
  wires nothing. The decision is logged (`amadeus: auth: --private-key NAME →
  <path>`), so each run shows what authenticated it.

### Changed

- New scopes assigned to a single-key runner need **no** inventory key wiring and
  **no** `{{ lookup('env', NAME) }}` — the Phase 1 env bridge still fires, so
  existing inventories that use the lookup keep working unchanged.

## 0.47.25 — Runners: installer key defaults + doctor auth-chain probe

**Date:** Jul 15, 2026

Phase 2 of the runner-auth unification.
The installer now owns the key convention up front, can mint a key on the spot,
and `doctor` can prove the whole auth chain end-to-end — turning the RHEL 8
onboarding's multi-step "why won't this key work" loop into one command.
Installer + agent-doctor only; no server or protocol change.

### Added

- **`runner-install.sh --generate-key <NAME>`** — mint a passphrase-less
  `ed25519` key at `/var/lib/amadeus-runner/keys/<NAME>` (owned by
  `amadeus-runner`) and print its public key to add to each target's
  `authorized_keys`. The private key never leaves the host; refuses to overwrite
  an existing key. `NAME` must be a plain filename (same rule as `--key-map`).
- **`amadeus-runner doctor --auth NAME [user@host]`** — resolve a credential
  NAME exactly as a run would (key-map → env-PEM → key-dir), reporting source +
  path; given a target, dial it with the agent's own SSH stack (same known_hosts
  - strict callback) and classify the result as auth OK / host-key-unknown
  (points at Scan & approve) / permission-denied / connect-failed.
- **Doctor `key-names` + `known-hosts` checks** (full, non-`--quick` runs) — the
  `key-names` check enumerates resolvable key names (key-map + key-dir) and
  parses each, WARNing on a passphrase-protected or unreadable key before a run
  needs it; the `known-hosts` check reports the trust-store path and host-key
  count. Names, paths, and parse status only — never key material.

### Changed

- **The installer always provisions the key directory.** `runner-install.sh` now
  creates `/var/lib/amadeus-runner/keys` (`0700`) and writes
  `AMADEUS_RUNNER_KEY_DIR` on every install, with or without `--key-dir` — so a
  key dropped in later (or generated) works with no `runner.env` edit. The
  post-install "before the first SSH run" guidance now reflects the default
  (only the key files may still be missing).

## 0.47.24 — Runners: one key + one trust store for bash and ansible

**Date:** Jul 15, 2026

First phase of the runner-auth unification.
A runner's SSH credential and host-key trust are now **one fact, provisioned
once**: the key file that already serves bash/Go-SSH runs is bridged to ansible
automatically, and ansible verifies hosts against the same known_hosts store that
Scan & approve seeds — closing the dual-provisioning and split-brain seams a real
RHEL 8 onboarding hit. Agent-only; existing runners get the behavior on a binary
upgrade (no server or protocol change).

### Added

- **Auth bridge (key NAME → local key FILE for ansible).** When a run's
  `authKeyEnvVar` NAME has no env value but resolves to a key-map entry or a
  key-dir file, the agent now injects `NAME=<path>` into the ansible child env so
  one provisioned key serves bash AND ansible — no second provisioning of the
  same name as an env-var-holding-a-path. Env-held PEMs are deliberately not
  bridged (a PEM is bytes, not a path); use key-map/key-dir for ansible-shared
  names. `resolveKeyPath` is the single resolver now shared by the Go-SSH signer
  path and the bridge.
- **Trust-store unification.** Ansible runs get
  `ANSIBLE_SSH_COMMON_ARGS="-o UserKnownHostsFile=<known_hosts> -o StrictHostKeyChecking=yes"`
  injected, pointing OpenSSH at the agent's known_hosts. Scan & approve now covers
  ansible; the field `~/.ssh/known_hosts` symlink workaround is no longer needed
  (and stays harmless).
- **Per-run auth/trust provenance.** Each run log emits `amadeus: auth: key
  "NAME" → <path> (key-map|key-dir)` per bridged key and `amadeus: trust:
  known_hosts → <path>`, so what authenticated a run is visible in the log, not a
  post-mortem.
- **`AMADEUS_RUNNER_ANSIBLE_SSH_COMMON_ARGS`** (`-ansible-ssh-common-args`) — an
  operator override injected INSTEAD of the synthesized args for ProxyJump/
  cipher-restricted estates that must own the whole arg string (still
  fail-closed).
- **`AMADEUS_RUNNER_NO_AUTH_BRIDGE`** (`-no-auth-bridge`) — escape hatch that
  disables the bridge and the known_hosts injection for estates managing their
  own ansible SSH/key config; runs then behave as pre-Phase-1.

### Changed

- **Missing-key errors now name every place checked and the fix.** The Go-SSH
  "no local key" error distinguishes *no key-dir configured* from *file not found
  in key-dir*; the ansible env-passthrough error points at key-map/key-dir
  bridging and drops the stale `secrets.env` example (the installer never creates
  one). An explicitly-set env var still wins over the bridge, and an
  operator-supplied `ANSIBLE_SSH_COMMON_ARGS` is never overridden.

## 0.47.17 — Runner preflight doctor + installer sandbox self-probe

**Date:** Jul 14, 2026

A follow-up to 0.47.16 that turns "installed and running, but never registers"
into a **diagnosable, self-healing** install. It adds an environment preflight
and makes the installer detect and route around a systemd sandbox that stalls
filesystem access — the failure mode that took a multi-day investigation on a
RHEL 8 host (the unit's `ProtectSystem`/namespace/seccomp hardening hung
`exec.LookPath`/`stat` at startup, so the agent detected no toolchains and
crash-looped).

### Added

- **`amadeus-runner doctor` preflight.** A subcommand that resolves the same
  config the agent uses and runs **bounded** checks: server URL scheme;
  `/healthz` reachability (distinguishing an **SSO-proxy HTML login page** from a
  real response); every `$PATH` directory responsive (catching a hung mount — or
  a systemd sandbox stalling filesystem access when run in-sandbox);
  identity-file writable; registration-token / resumed-identity readiness; and
  (full mode) toolchain detection + tier-2 sandbox. It prints a labeled
  PASS/WARN/FAIL report and exits non-zero on any FAIL. `--quick` skips the two
  slow probes. Wired as a **non-fatal `ExecStartPre`** (logs the report to the
  journal before every start) and run once at **install time** before the
  installer declares success.
- **Installer sandbox self-probe.** `runner-install.sh` reproduces the hardened
  sandbox in a bounded transient unit and stats a file; if it stalls or fails,
  the generated unit falls back to **reduced hardening** (basic privilege drop
  kept; mount-namespace/seccomp dropped) so the runner can start, with a loud
  warning to fix the host's systemd. Force with
  `AMADEUS_INSTALL_MINIMAL_HARDENING=1`.

### Fixed

- **`probeSandbox` could still hang startup after the 0.47.16 fix.** That fix
  moved the `systemd-run` lookup inside the abandonable deadline but left a
  **duplicate, unprotected `exec.LookPath("systemd-run")` before it**, so on a
  host with a stalled `$PATH` the sandbox probe still wedged (goroutine 1 parked
  at the leftover line). Removed the duplicate; the only remaining lookup runs
  inside the 3s deadline.

## 0.47.16 — Runner startup & registration hardening

**Date:** Jul 12, 2026

A runner that installed cleanly and ran as a healthy service could still never
appear in the Runners view — it was wedging or failing during startup, before
registration, on hosts with awkward environments (a bare server URL, a stale
NFS/autofs mount in `$PATH`, or a server whose runner-token store had been
reset). These fixes make the agent register reliably in those conditions, and —
just as important — make the failure modes **diagnosable** instead of silent.

### Fixed

- **Schemeless server URL.** A bare `AMADEUS_RUNNER_SERVER` (e.g.
  `amadeus.example.com`, no scheme) made the agent die at register with
  `unsupported protocol scheme ""`. The agent now normalizes a schemeless value
  to `https://` and validates the scheme with a clear error; the installer's
  auto-prepend guard was rewritten in POSIX `case` so it still fires when the
  script is piped to `sh`/dash rather than bash.
- **Startup probes could block registration forever.** The tier-2 sandbox probe
  (`systemd-run`) and the toolchain-capability probes (`ansible --version`,
  `ansible-galaxy collection list`) ran unbounded. On an Ansible control node a
  slow `ansible-galaxy`, or a `systemd-run` that can't reach a manager as a
  non-login system user, left the agent silent until systemd `SIGKILL`ed it
  after the stop timeout. Each probe now runs under a hard deadline with a
  process-group kill and `WaitDelay` backstop; a timeout degrades to "not
  detected" and registration continues.
- **A `$PATH` directory on a hung mount wedged startup — the root cause.**
  `exec.LookPath` stats every `$PATH` entry; a directory on a stale NFS/autofs
  mount blocked that stat uninterruptibly, *before* any probe timeout could
  apply. All startup lookups (sandbox, toolchain detection) now run inside the
  bounded/abandonable section, so a hung mount degrades a probe instead of
  hanging the runner.
- **Runner stranded on a rejected token.** A poll that returned **401** (the
  runner was deleted, or the server's token store was reset/rebuilt) was retried
  forever on a dead token — the runner never reappeared and needed manual
  `identity.json` surgery. A 401 now triggers the same discard-identity +
  re-register recovery as a 404, so the runner self-heals once a valid
  registration token is in place.

### Added

- **Installer PATH sanitization.** `runner-install.sh` probes each candidate
  `$PATH` directory with a bounded `stat` and, if any hang, pins `runner.env`'s
  `PATH` to the responsive directories only — so a fresh install on a
  hung-mount host comes up cleanly instead of silently hanging. It warns which
  directories it excluded and that the mount must be repaired for runs. Opt out
  with `AMADEUS_INSTALL_SKIP_PATH_CHECK=1`.
- **Startup progress logging.** The agent logs each startup phase *before* it
  runs it (`runner agent starting` → `probing tier-2 sandbox availability` →
  `detecting host capabilities` → `registering with server`), so when a phase
  wedges the last journal line names it — no goroutine dump required.
- **Troubleshooting section in the runner Config Guide**
  (`runner-manage.html`): the healthy startup-log sequence, a last-line →
  cause → fix table (schemeless URL, SSO-proxy HTML intercept, 401 tokens,
  x509 CA, register hang), a host reachability check, and the silent-startup-
  hang playbook (SIGQUIT goroutine dump, per-`$PATH`-dir `stat` probe, and the
  repair / clean-PATH / `NO_SANDBOX` mitigations).

## 0.47.15 — Runner endpoints behind an SSO proxy

**Date:** Jul 10, 2026

### Fixed

- **Runner endpoints behind an SSO proxy.** Documented (and fixed in the
  reference config) that the runner-provisioning paths must bypass a
  browser-SSO forward-auth. When Cronomicon sits behind Authelia/Traefik with
  `default_policy: deny`, an unauthenticated `curl …/install/<token>` (and the
  runner's own `poll`/`register`) was redirected to the login page and returned
  HTML — the install failed with `bash: syntax error near unexpected token
  '<!doctype html>'`. The reference `deploy/authelia/configuration.yml` and
  `deploy/deployment-guide.md` now carry an auth-bypass allowlist for the
  runner surface (`/install/*`, `/agents/*`, `/runner-install.sh`, and the
  runner bearer-authed `/api/v1/runners/{register,{id}/poll,{id}/redeclare,
  {id}/hostkeys}` + `/api/v1/runs/{id}/{manifest,log}`); the app still enforces
  the runner bearer on the `/api` paths, so the bypass skips only the SSO. No
  binary change — a deployment-config + docs correction.

## 0.47.13 — Runner provisioning round 2, Phase 5: host-key scan & approve

**Date:** Jul 10, 2026

Phase 5 of the second runner-provisioning plan
(the runner-install-update-2 plan, D4: 4A; protocol **v5**):
human-approved TOFU for target host keys. Instead of hand-assembling a
`known_hosts` before a runner's first SSH run, you trust a key at the moment
it's known — scan, compare the fingerprint out-of-band, approve — with an audit
trail.

### Added

- **Protocol v5:** the `keyscan` and `trust-hosts` poll control ops (gated on
  `protocol_version >= 5`). A run that fails host verification now surfaces a
  `host_key_unverified` reason naming the host (via the trailing envelope →
  the run's status reason).
- **Scan → approve → trust flow:** a **Scan keys** action per runner queues a
  scan; the agent captures each host's presented key natively (no
  `ssh-keyscan` binary — `x/crypto/ssh`) and uploads it. A **Pending host-key
  approvals** section on the Runners view shows the full SHA256 fingerprint for
  out-of-band comparison; **Approve** appends the key to the runner's
  `known_hosts` on its next poll, **Reject** never trusts it. Migration `570`
  adds `pending_host_keys` + a `keyscan_requested` queue column.
- **Endpoints:** `POST /runners/{id}/keyscan` (operator), `POST
  /runners/{id}/hostkeys` (runner-key upload), `GET
  /runners/host-keys/pending`, `POST /runners/host-keys/{keyId}/resolve` —
  scan/approve/reject all audited.

### Changed

- **`known_hosts` is now optional pre-seeding.** A fresh runner defaults its
  known_hosts path (beside the identity file) and creates it empty, so an
  unknown host is refused (a soft `host_key_unverified` failure) until scanned
  and approved — rather than requiring `--known-hosts` up front. Strict
  verification and the no-fall-open stance are unchanged.
- **OpenAPI** (both copies + gen); security guide (§8 human-approved TOFU),
  install guide (`--known-hosts` demoted to optional), `runner-manage.html`
  (§4.6 the flow), and `security-review.md` (never auto-trusts; secrets stay
  runner-local).

## 0.47.12 — Runner provisioning round 2, Phase 4: server-managed runner settings

**Date:** Jul 10, 2026

Phase 4 of the second runner-provisioning plan
(the runner-install-update-2 plan, D3/D5): operational knobs a
runner used to bake in at install (and re-install to change) are now edited on
the runner's row and delivered over the poll channel — **no SSH, no restart, no
env edit**. This is the deepest change of the plan (a new server→runner
authority direction); it lands additively within protocol v4.

### Added

- **Server-managed settings:** a new `⚙ Settings` drawer per runner row edits
  `maxConcurrent`, the three sandbox caps, the checkout policy (`allowCheckout`
  - `checkoutRepos` allowlist), and a subtract-only **capability mask**. Each
  field is tri-state (override, or blank = keep the runner's local value).
  Changes take effect on the runner's next poll and apply in-memory.
- **Poll-channel delivery + ack:** the poll response gains an optional
  `settings` object; the agent echoes the version it has applied as a
  `settingsVersion` query param. The server delivers settings only to an
  ack-capable agent and only until it acks — so the row shows a pending dot
  until the change round-trips, and **a pre-Phase-4 agent is untouched** (it
  never sends the param, so it never receives settings).
- **`PATCH /api/v1/runners/{id}/settings`** (ConfigureApp + CSRF,
  activity-audited): replaces a runner's managed set and bumps its version.
  Migration `560` adds `runners.managed_settings` + `settings_version` +
  `settings_acked_version`.
- **Capability mask enforcement:** masked run-types are subtracted from the
  runner's effective claim set server-side (never assigned) and honored
  agent-side for symmetry.

### Changed

- **Agent concurrency limiter** moved from a fixed-size channel to a
  mutex-guarded counter so `maxConcurrent` can be raised/lowered live.
  Server-managed sandbox/checkout overrides layer onto a per-run config
  snapshot (race-free); managed overrides never touch the config digest, so
  they can't trigger a drift re-registration.
- **Provision helper reshaped:** max jobs, sandbox caps, and checkout policy
  inputs are gone (set them on the runner's row now); only the install-time
  secret-file inputs remain. `provisionNeedsEnvFollowUp` and its
  "merge the env" apology note are **deleted** — the one-liner is complete.
- **OpenAPI:** the `Runner` schema gains `managedSettings` /
  `settingsVersion` / `settingsAckedVersion`, `PollResponse` gains `settings`,
  the poll op gains the `settingsVersion` param, and the PATCH path + a
  `ManagedRunnerSettings` schema are added (both spec copies + regenerated
  types).
- **Docs:** `runner-manage.html` gains a "Managed settings" section, the
  security guide's protocol-history note and `security-review.md` cover the
  server-authority extension (D3 — secrets stay runner-local).

## 0.47.11 — Runner provisioning round 2, Phase 3: secret ceremonies

**Date:** Jul 10, 2026

Phase 3 of the second runner-provisioning plan
(the runner-install-update-2 plan): a checkout+vault Ansible runner
now installs in **one** `runner-install.sh` invocation — no post-install file
placement, no env merge.

### Added

- **Installer checkout/vault flags:** `--allow-checkout`, `--checkout-repos
  <csv>`, `--checkout-token-file <path>`, and `--vault-pass-file <path>` place
  the opt-in, the repo allowlist, and the two secret files. Secrets can also be
  typed at a hidden stdin prompt (`--checkout-token -` / `--vault-pass -`, echo
  off). The installed secret files get `0640 root:amadeus-runner` (same custody
  as `runner.env`) and the bytes never transit the server.
- **No secrets as flag values:** passing a token/password as a flag *value* is
  refused (it would leak via `ps` and shell history); a stdin prompt requires a
  real terminal, so a piped `curl … | sudo bash` install is told to use the
  file form. New `runner-install-check.sh` cases cover all of this.
- **Missing-toolchain hint:** when checkout/vault flags are given but
  `ansible-playbook` isn't on PATH, the installer prints a distro-matched
  `apt/dnf install ansible-core` hint (prints, never installs — package
  management belongs to config management).

### Changed

- **Provision helper:** the one-liner now emits the checkout/vault flags, so
  `provisionNeedsEnvFollowUp` no longer fires for them — only the sandbox caps
  and a non-default max-jobs remain env-only (Phase 4 moves those to the
  runner's row). The checkout/vault fields are now labeled as source paths the
  installer copies into place.
- **Docs:** Install Guide flag table + a "secrets are never a flag value" note;
  Security Guide checkout/vault sections; env-example cross-refs; a
  `security-review.md` entry on the secrets-placement posture.

---

## 0.47.10 — Runner provisioning round 2, Phase 2: one-click Add Runner

**Date:** Jul 10, 2026

Phase 2 of the second runner-provisioning plan
(the runner-install-update-2 plan, D2: 2A): registering a runner
collapses from "mint a token, build a command, copy it" to **click Add Runner,
paste one line on the host**.

### Added

- **`GET /install/{token}` endpoint:** serves `runner-install.sh` with this
  server's URL, the registration token, and binary-download-on baked in, so the
  whole install is one flagless pipe —
  `curl -fsSL <server>/install/<token> | sudo bash`. A dumb substitution
  endpoint: it does not read the DB (no token-validity oracle), only
  syntax-checks the token (`amt_reg_` + 64 hex, which also blocks shell-meta
  injection into the baked assignment). Registration remains the sole
  enforcement point. Unauthenticated at root by design, same posture as
  `/agents/` and `/runner-install.sh`; `Cache-Control: no-store`. Capabilities
  are not baked — the agent auto-detects (Phase 1).
- **Add Runner button + modal:** a primary **+ Add Runner** action on the
  Runners view mints a token (optional label) and shows the personalized
  one-liner with a copy button, an "expires in 24h · single-use" caption, and a
  collapsed download-inspect-run variant. The registry empty state links to it.
  New `personalizedInstall*` command builders back the modal.

### Changed

- **Register New Runner card demoted:** it keeps the token audit trail and the
  manual command builder, but Add Runner is now the headline path (the card's
  intro says so).
- **OpenAPI:** `/install/{token}` added to both spec copies (`security: []`);
  frontend client types regenerated.
- **Docs:** Install Guide §1 leads with the one-click story; both manuals'
  runner-registration sections updated; `security-review.md` gains a
  token-in-URL access-log hygiene note (single-use + 24h expiry bound the
  exposure).

## 0.47.9 — Runner provisioning round 2, Phase 1: detect, don't ask

**Date:** Jul 10, 2026

Phase 1 of the second runner-provisioning plan
(the runner-install-update-2 plan, D1: 1B): run-type capabilities
are now **auto-detected by the agent** when left unset, so an install needs no
capability decision from the operator — the explicit setting remains as a
narrowing override.

### Added

- **Agent run-type auto-detection:** with `AMADEUS_RUNNER_CAPABILITIES` /
  `-capabilities` unset, the agent probes the host's PATH at startup (`bash`,
  `perl`, `pwsh`, `python3`/`python`, `ansible-playbook`, `terraform`) and
  claims the matching run-types. Zero findings is a startup error; explicit
  capabilities behave exactly as before. Detection re-runs on Resync and feeds
  the declared-config digest, so installing a toolchain and restarting the
  agent propagates the new capability to the registry via the existing drift
  resync.

### Changed

- **Installer (`runner-install.sh`):** the blind `bash,ansible` capability
  default is gone. Without `-c` the generated `runner.env` omits
  `AMADEUS_RUNNER_CAPABILITIES` entirely (agent auto-detects) and the
  post-install summary says so; `-c` writes the explicit override.
  `runner-install-check.sh` guards the new behavior.
- **Provision helper:** the capability chips moved behind an
  **auto-detect on the host ★ / override** toggle (auto-detect is the default).
  In detect mode the one-liner and `docker run` artifacts omit the capability
  flag/env and the generated `runner.env` keeps the var present but commented;
  the Register card's install command likewise drops `-c`.
- **Env example:** `amadeus-runner.env.example` documents unset-means-probe and
  ships the capabilities line commented out.
- **Docs:** Install Guide (flag table, §8 detection story, container section),
  both manuals' runner capability sections, and a `security-review.md` note on
  the auto-broadening trade-off (detection widens by default; the explicit
  override is the narrowing lever until the Phase-4 server-side capability
  mask lands).

## 0.47.6 — Runner provisioning Phase 6: the "Provision a Runner" helper

**Date:** Jul 10, 2026

Phase 6 — the last phase — of the runner-provisioning plan
(the runner-install-update plan): a pure-frontend helper on the
Runners view that turns one set of choices into three copy-paste artifacts, so
authoring a runner's config no longer means hand-editing an env file against
the reference table.

### Added

- **"Provision a Runner" panel** (Runners view, collapsible): capability chips
  (dashed borders mark the fat-image local toolchains), inventory mode (+
  local inventory path), SSH custody (known_hosts, key-dir or key-map, private
  CA), checkout opt-in (repo allowlist + deploy-token file), vault password
  file, per-run sandbox caps, and max jobs. A freshly minted registration
  token feeds straight in; otherwise a quoted `<TOKEN>` placeholder.
- **Three artifacts, per-artifact copy buttons:**
  - a complete annotated **`runner.env`** — the verbatim
    `amadeus-runner.env.example` with the choices patched in, so every
    annotation survives and the emitted env **cannot drift from the single
    source** (the plan's D-alternative "make the example the skeleton": the
    example is now published by the manuals plugin at
    `/amadeus-runner.env.example` and fetched by the helper);
  - the matching **install one-liner** with the Phase-1 flags
    (`--known-hosts`, `--key-dir`/`--key-map`, `--ca-cert`,
    `--inventory local --local-inventory`) and `--download`; a note flags the
    env-only options (checkout/vault/sandbox/max jobs are not installer
    flags — merge the generated env after install);
  - the **`docker run` variant**, slim vs fat image derived from the
    capability pick, identity on the named volume, file-backed options
    pathed to the volume.
- **Generators live in `runner-install`-style pure functions**
  (`runner-provision.ts`) with 12 unit tests, including a **drift guard**:
  the tests patch the real `backend/deploy/amadeus-runner.env.example` from
  disk, and the generator throws loudly if the template loses a var it
  patches (a rename in the example or `config.go` fails the suite instead of
  drifting silently). Key-map values are rewritten to the installer's
  `keys/<NAME>` destinations, matching what `runner-install.sh` actually
  does.

### Documentation

- `runner-install.html` §4 opens with the helper as the fast path for env
  authoring (the table remains the hand-authoring reference); user manual
  gains §13.4 describing the panel (existing section numbers untouched).

### Notes

- Bumps the version constant in `backend/cmd/amadeus/main.go` to `0.47.6`.
- Verified visually in the running app (both themes): panel expand, capability
  toggles, local-inventory/checkout conditionals, and all three artifacts
  render and update live.
- No backend or API change (pure frontend + one manuals-plugin publish
  entry). This completes the provisioning plan — all phases (1–7) shipped.

## 0.47.5 — Runner provisioning Phase 5: automatic config-drift detection

**Date:** Jul 10, 2026

Phase 5 of the runner-provisioning plan (decision D2 stage 2): declared-config changes now **propagate on the next poll
after a restart** — no operator action at all. The agent sends a canonical
digest of its declared config with every poll; on mismatch with the digest
stored at (re-)registration, the server delivers the Phase-4 `re-register` op
and the agent re-declares in place. The Resync button demotes to a force-lever.

### Added

- **`runnerproto.ConfigDigest`** — the shared canonical SHA-256 over the
  declared set (name, os, capability tokens, maxConcurrent, inventory,
  version, protocolVersion). Canonicalization is baked in so agent and server
  agree by construction: capabilities sorted (detection order is unstable),
  the register handler's defaults normalized (`maxConcurrent <= 0` → 5,
  `inventory ""` → amadeus), newline-framed fields. Unit-tested for
  order-insensitivity, normalization equivalence, per-field sensitivity, and
  framing.
- **Migration `550`** adds `runners.config_digest`, computed and stored by
  register **and** redeclare from the same normalized values they persist. A
  pre-550 row (NULL digest) counts as drift and self-heals via one redeclare.
- **Poll drift check:** the poll request's new optional `configDigest` query
  param is compared against the stored digest (protocol v4+ rows only; absent
  digest = pre-Phase-5 agent, no check). Mismatch delivers `re-register` on
  that same poll — **flap-guarded** to at most one op per 5 minutes per
  runner (in-memory, per-runner), with a loud log on suppressed repeats, so a
  disagreeing agent can never re-register-loop. A manual Resync click always
  delivers (bypasses the cooldown) but arms it.
- **Agent:** computes its digest at startup — including on **resume**, which
  is the whole point (config edited or binary upgraded + restart → the first
  poll carries the new digest) — refreshes it on redeclare, and sends it with
  every poll.

### Changed

- **Docs headline flip:** "config changes propagate on the next poll after a
  restart" is now the documented behavior; the Resync button is the
  don't-wait force-lever. `runner-manage.html` (declared-vs-local blockquote,
  no-hot-reload, upgrade blockquote, §4 intro + Cases B/D), the v4 entry and
  gate list in `runner-security.html` §4 (the digest is a hash of what the
  agent already declares — never a channel for new config), administrator
  manual §7.6/§7.8, user manual §13.1, both glossaries, the Resync
  button/dialog copy, and `deploy/security-review.md`.
- No protocol bump: the digest is additive within v4 — a digest-less poll
  simply skips the check, and the op still only goes to v4+ rows.

### Tests

- Server: matching digest quiet; mismatch delivers the op immediately;
  immediate repeat suppressed by the flap guard; fires again after the
  cooldown; convergence after redeclare. Gates: no digest → no check;
  protocol < 4 row → no op; NULL stored digest → self-heal op. Migration 550
  up/down round-trip with data present.
- Agent: every poll carries the digest, and after a re-register round-trip it
  equals `ConfigDigest` over exactly the declared set the redeclare body
  carried (shared canonicalization proven end-to-end).

### Notes

- Bumps the version constant in `backend/cmd/amadeus/main.go` to `0.47.5`.
- OpenAPI: the poll path gains the `configDigest` query parameter (both
  byte-identical spec copies; frontend types regenerated).
- This completes D2's staged plan (2A manual lever v0.47.3 → 2B automatic
  detection here). Remaining from the provisioning plan: Phase 6 (the
  "Provision a runner" helper UI).
