## 0.47.4 — Runner provisioning Phase 7: single-use registration tokens

**Date:** Jul 10, 2026

Phase 7 of the runner-provisioning plan (decision D6): the shared 24h registration token is replaced by **single-use,
per-install tokens with an audit trail** — mint one per host (optionally
labeled), each dies on its first successful registration and records which
runner consumed it. Registration tokens are now strictly first-contact
credentials: resync (Phase 4) runs on the runner's own key, so a dead install
token never blocks anything; only a reaped/deregistered runner needs a fresh
one.

### Added

- **Migration `540`** extends `registration_tokens` for multiple active rows:
  `label`, `used_at`, `used_by_runner_id`. Existing shared-token rows
  grandfather as unlabeled single-use rows until their 24h expiry.
- **`POST /api/v1/runners/registration-tokens`** mints a token (optional
  label, plaintext returned once, hash-at-rest) — unlike the retired rotate,
  minting does NOT revoke other tokens, so several installs can be in flight.
  **`GET`** lists label/created/expires/status and the used-by audit trail
  (never plaintext; the consuming runner's name resolved at list time).
  **`DELETE /{id}`** revokes an unused token (409 for a used one — its row is
  the audit record; revoking the runner it registered is Deregister's job).
  Mint/revoke write activity audit entries.
- **Atomic consumption:** registration consumes the token row inside the
  registration transaction (`UPDATE … WHERE used_at IS NULL`, rows-affected
  guard) — two hosts cannot register from one token; the race loser's
  registration rolls back whole. Distinct rejection errors: `token_used`
  (naming the consuming runner) vs `token_expired` vs plain `unauthorized`.
- **`AMADEUS_RUNNER_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN` unchanged** — env-configured, multi-use,
  no row, no provenance (documented as the out-of-band alternative).

### Changed

- **The shared-token endpoints are gone:** `GET/POST
  /runners/registration-token` (placeholder-serving GET, rotate-to-replace
  POST) are removed from routes, spec, and UI. "Regenerate" no longer exists
  as a concept — revoke-unused replaces it.
- **Runners view — Register New Runner card** becomes a token manager: a
  **Mint token** form (optional label, e.g. the intended runner name) feeding
  the freshly-returned plaintext straight into the Phase-2 token-agnostic
  install-command builders, plus a token list (label, created, expires,
  status incl. "used by <runner>", per-row Revoke). The "Regenerate is not a
  kill-switch" callout becomes "token hygiene is not a kill-switch".

### Tests

- Mint/list/revoke round-trip (list never leaks plaintext; labels survive;
  mint leaves sibling tokens active; revoke-unused kills registration;
  revoke-used 409s; unknown id 404s).
- Single-use semantics: consumption records the audit trail on both sides
  (`runners.registration_token_id` ↔ `used_by_runner_id`), double-use is
  rejected naming the consumer, expiry is a distinct error.
- Concurrency: 8 simultaneous registrations with one token — exactly one 201,
  exactly one runner row.
- Bootstrap token: still multi-use, still provenance-free. Migration 540
  up/down round-trip with data present.

### Documentation

- **OpenAPI:** the registration-token paths replaced by the
  `/runners/registration-tokens` collection (+ `DELETE /{tokenId}`);
  `RegistrationToken` schema replaced by `RegistrationTokenInfo` (status enum,
  used-by fields); register endpoint re-described (single-use, atomic
  consumption, distinct errors). Both byte-identical copies; frontend types
  regenerated.
- **Guides & manuals:** `runner-install.html` §1 rewritten as the
  mint-per-install flow; `runner-manage.html` §2 "Regenerate is not a
  kill-switch" → token hygiene, §4 Case A (a reaped runner needs a *fresh*
  token — its key was revoked with the row); admin manual §7.3 two-token
  model + FAQ; user manual §13.2 panel, §13 SVG caption ("shared, used once"
  → "single-use per install"), §15.5 onboarding, FAQ; both glossaries;
  `amadeus-runner.env.example` + `env-matrix.md` reworded.
- **Security review:** single-use consumption closes the two-hosts-one-token
  race, adds the which-token-registered-which-runner audit trail, and bounds
  a leaked token's value (`deploy/security-review.md`).

### Notes

- Bumps the version constant in `backend/cmd/amadeus/main.go` to `0.47.4`.
- Acceptance (plan): two hosts cannot register from one token; the Runners
  view shows which runner consumed which token; resync works on a runner
  whose install token is long dead.

## 0.47.3 — Runner provisioning Phase 4: the Resync button (protocol v4)

**Date:** Jul 10, 2026

Phase 4 of the runner-provisioning plan (decision D2 stage 1): the deregister-and-let-it-404 "Resync dance" is replaced by
a per-runner **Resync** button. The runner wire protocol bumps to **v4**, adding a
`re-register` poll control op and an id-preserving redeclare endpoint: the agent
re-declares its current local config **in place** — same id, same API key, same
agency membership, no orphan row, active runs unaffected.

### Added

- **`POST /api/v1/runners/{id}/resync`** (operator, ConfigureApp + CSRF; new
  `internal/runner/resync.go`) sets a `resync_requested` flag (migration `530`)
  and writes a Change-Log-style activity entry. **409 `agent_too_old`** when the
  runner's recorded protocol is < 4 — mirroring the v2 inventory / v3 checkout
  gate philosophy: never send an op an old agent would silently ignore.
- **Poll delivery of `re-register`** (protocol v4): the flag is consumed
  atomically (deliver-once, like kill/drain) and the op is delivered
  immediately — including mid-long-poll, via the same cheap per-iteration
  re-check that catches a mid-poll drain, so a Resync click lands within one
  poll interval, not after the 30s timeout.
- **`POST /api/v1/runners/{id}/redeclare`** (runner bearer): the id-preserving
  re-declaration. Authenticated with the runner's **existing `amt_run_*` key,
  never a registration token** (D6: registration tokens are first-contact-only
  — a reaped runner still needs a fresh token via the unchanged 404 path).
  Ownership-guarded like poll (404, no existence leak); validates like
  register (shared `normalizeAndValidate`); requires a declared protocol >= 4
  (426 otherwise); updates name/os/capabilities/maxConcurrent/version/
  inventory/toolchains/protocolVersion in place and leaves status, load,
  agencies, tokens, and registration provenance untouched.
- **Agent `re-register` op handling** (`internal/agent`): re-detects toolchain
  capability tokens (a newly installed collection propagates without a
  restart), POSTs the redeclare with the existing key, keeps its identity, and
  resumes polling — nothing drains. A 404 (reaped meanwhile) defers to the
  existing discard-identity + fresh-register path.
- **Runners view:** per-runner **Resync** button (online runners) with a
  confirm dialog consistent with Drain/Deregister; disabled with an
  "upgrade the runner binary" tooltip while the server records protocol < 4.
  The runner list (and OpenAPI `Runner` schema) now exposes
  **`protocolVersion`** to drive the gate.

### Tests

- Server: resync endpoint version gate (404/409/202 + flag semantics); poll
  delivers the op once and clears the flag (and never sends it to a < v4 row);
  redeclare updates in place (one row, same id, agencies kept, token
  unrevoked, pending flag cleared) with ownership + 426 guards; migration 530
  up/down round-trip with data present.
- Agent: integration round-trip — on `re-register` the agent redeclares with
  the **runner key** (exactly one token-based registration ever happens),
  ships the full declared set at protocol 4, and keeps polling with the same
  identity.

### Documentation

- **OpenAPI:** `/runners/{runnerId}/resync` + `/runners/{runnerId}/redeclare`,
  `Runner.protocolVersion`, and the `re-register` control-op enum added to
  both byte-identical spec copies; frontend types regenerated (`npm run gen`).
- **The payoff rewrite:** `runner-manage.html` §4's Cases B/D collapse to
  "restart, then click Resync" on a v4+ agent (older agents keep the
  deregister path; the one v3 → v4 boundary crossing is called out — the
  button can't enable itself). Declared-vs-local callouts in both runner
  guides, `runner-security.html` §4's version history (v4 entry + gate
  bullet), administrator manual §7.6/§7.8, user manual §13.1 row actions, and
  both glossaries (new **Resync** entries) updated.
- **Security review:** resync cannot reconfigure a runner from the server
  side — the op carries no config; the agent re-reads its own local files and
  authenticates with its own key (`deploy/security-review.md`).

### Notes

- Bumps the version constant in `backend/cmd/amadeus/main.go` to `0.47.3`.
- `MinProtocolVersion` stays 1 — older agents keep working; only the Resync
  button requires v4.
- Automatic drift detection (D2 stage 2, config digests) is Phase 5; this
  release ships the manual lever first per the staged decision.

## 0.47.2 — Runner provisioning Phase 3: the server distributes the agent binary

**Date:** Jul 9, 2026

Phase 3 of the runner-provisioning plan (decision D1): the server image bakes cross-compiled `amadeus-runner` binaries in
and serves them itself, and `runner-install.sh --download` fetches + verifies one
— so a host with only curl, sudo, and reachability to the Cronomicon server goes
from nothing to a registered, online runner with the panel's one-liner. No
GitLab reachability, no Go toolchain on the target.

### Added

- **`GET /agents/{filename}`** (new `internal/api/agents.go`) serves the runner
  agent binaries and their checksums from `AMADEUS_AGENT_DIR` (default
  `/usr/share/amadeus/agents`; added to `env-matrix.md`). Allowlisted filenames
  only — `amadeus-runner-linux-{amd64,arm64}` + `SHA256SUMS` (D5: no Windows
  publish until a Windows install story exists) — no directory listing or
  traversal surface. Unauthenticated **by design**: the binary is not a secret
  and the install flow runs before any credential exists on the host; rationale
  recorded in `deploy/security-review.md`. Deployments without the files
  (bare-metal `go build`) get a clean 404 with a distinct `agents_not_bundled`
  code and a build-it-yourself hint. Handler unit tests cover the allowlist,
  both content types, and the unbundled case.
- **Server Dockerfile `agents` stage** cross-compiles the agent for linux
  amd64 + arm64 (`CGO_ENABLED=0`, same `-trimpath`/ldflags recipe as
  `Dockerfile.runner`, stamped with the image's `VERSION`/`COMMIT`), writes
  `SHA256SUMS`, and the runtime stage copies the set into
  `/usr/share/amadeus/agents/`.
- **`runner-install.sh --download`** detects the host architecture
  (`x86_64|amd64` / `aarch64|arm64`), fetches the binary + `SHA256SUMS` from
  `--server`'s `/agents/` endpoint (honoring `--ca-cert` for the fetch), and
  **verifies the SHA-256 before installing** — a mismatch aborts loudly and
  never falls back; an unavailable endpoint (404/unreachable) falls back to the
  existing `-b`/auto-search with a warning. Requires curl; exercised end-to-end
  against a local HTTP server (happy path, tampered-checksum abort, 404
  fallback). The check harness gains a `--download` help assertion (21 checks).
- **The panel's install command gains `--download`** (both the one-liner and
  the two-step variant — `runner-install-cmd.ts`, tests updated), and its
  helper note now explains the fetched-and-verified binary with the local
  fallback.

### Documentation

- **OpenAPI:** `/agents/{filename}` added to both byte-identical spec copies
  (root-served like the health endpoints; mirror + route-conformance tests
  pass) and the frontend types regenerated (`npm run gen`).
- **Install guide:** §0 prerequisite loosens to "pre-built **or**
  `--download`"; §2 becomes "download **or** build" with the `/agents/`
  endpoint documented; §3's example uses `--download` and the flag table gains
  its row (checksum-mismatch-never-falls-back semantics spelled out).
  Administrator manual §7.2 and user manual §13.2 drop "needs a pre-built
  binary alongside" for the downloaded-and-verified flow. `deploy/README.md`
  documents the bundled-agents stage.

### Notes

- Bumps the version constant in `backend/cmd/amadeus/main.go` to `0.47.2`.
- Acceptance (plan): a host with only curl + the one-liner (and sudo) reaches a
  registered, online runner — on a container-deployed server. Bare-metal
  servers keep the build-it-yourself path with the same one-liner (the script
  falls back and says so).

## 0.47.1 — Runner provisioning Phase 2: the app serves the installer & a real install command

**Date:** Jul 9, 2026

Phase 2 of the runner-provisioning plan (decisions D3/D4): the install script is served by the app itself and the Runners
panel's install command becomes a real, copy-pasteable invocation of it — the
target host no longer needs GitLab reachability, and the `amadeus-agent register …`
placeholder (and its apology callouts in three docs) is gone. Frontend, build
plugin, and documentation only — no backend, schema, or API changes.

### Added

- **The app serves `runner-install.sh`.** `frontend/vite-manuals-plugin.js` gains
  a third published class, `FILES` (verbatim repo files): it copies
  `backend/deploy/runner-install.sh` into the embedded dist on build and serves
  it in `vite dev`, so `spa.go` delivers it at `/runner-install.sh` with no
  backend change — the same single-source pattern as the manuals/guides, with the
  same caveat (`npm run build` is the sync step after editing the script). The
  server `Dockerfile`'s frontend stage now copies `backend/deploy/runner-install.sh`
  in so the container build bundles it too, and a missing `FILES` source **fails
  the build** rather than silently shipping an app whose install command would
  curl-pipe the SPA fallback into bash (caught in review — the manuals' silent
  best-effort skip pattern would have masked exactly that in the Docker build).
- **A real install command, in two forms (D4).** The Register New Runner card now
  renders a curl-pipe one-liner — `curl -fsSL <origin>/runner-install.sh | sudo
  bash -s -- -s <origin> -t <token> -n $(hostname) -c bash,perl,powershell,python`
  — plus a collapsed *download-inspect-run* variant for orgs that don't pipe curl
  into sudo, each with its own copy button and a note about the pre-built binary
  and `-c` tuning. Token gating is unchanged (LB8): the plaintext is substituted
  only while the mint-time value is revealed, `<TOKEN>` otherwise, copy disabled
  without a usable plaintext. The builders live in a new token-agnostic module
  (`frontend/src/views/runner-install-cmd.ts` — takes "a usable plaintext token",
  per D6, so single-use tokens in Phase 7 won't rebuild the command UI), unit
  tested in `runner-install-cmd.test.ts` (script path, origin, arg passthrough,
  placeholder rendering).

### Changed

- **The Download button downloads from the app.** It now points at the app-served
  `/runner-install.sh` (with the `download` attribute); the hardcoded GitLab raw
  URL (`RUNNER_AGENT_URL`, an internal hostname baked into the frontend bundle)
  is deleted — a runner host reaches the Cronomicon server by definition, GitLab
  maybe not (D3).

### Documentation

- **The three "illustrative command" apology callouts are retired**, replaced by
  descriptions of the real command: user manual §13.2 (warn → note), administrator
  manual §7.2's "Binary & command name" note, and the install guide §1
  parenthetical. User manual §13.3 and install guide §3 now say the Download
  button / install command fetch the script from the app itself. Embedded dist
  republished.

### Notes

- Bumps the version constant in `backend/cmd/amadeus/main.go` to `0.47.1`.
- The one-liner still expects a pre-built `amadeus-runner` binary on the target
  host (`-b` / auto-search); binary distribution from the server is Phase 3.

## 0.47.0 — Runner provisioning Phase 1: the install script completes the install

**Date:** Jul 9, 2026

First phase of the runner-provisioning simplification plan
(the runner-install-update plan): `deploy/runner-install.sh` can now
finish the job in one pass — known_hosts, key custody, CA trust, and local
inventory no longer require the post-install hand-edit of
`/etc/amadeus-runner/runner.env` + restart that every SSH-capable runner needed
before. Install script and documentation only — no backend, schema, API, or
protocol changes.

### Added

- **`runner-install.sh` custody & trust flags.** New optional flags complete
  the install in one invocation, each installing its file into the standard
  layout and wiring the matching var into the generated `runner.env`:
  - `--known-hosts <file>` → `/var/lib/amadeus-runner/known_hosts` (`0640`,
    owner `amadeus-runner`) + `AMADEUS_RUNNER_KNOWN_HOSTS` — without it the
    agent refuses SSH runs (strict host-key verification, no fall-open);
  - `--key-dir <dir>` → copies the directory's key files into
    `/var/lib/amadeus-runner/keys` (`0700` dir, `0600` files, owner
    `amadeus-runner`) + `AMADEUS_RUNNER_KEY_DIR`;
  - `--key-map NAME=path,…` → copies each key to
    `/var/lib/amadeus-runner/keys/<NAME>` and writes the rewritten map to
    `AMADEUS_RUNNER_KEY_MAP` (mutually exclusive with `--key-dir`);
  - `--ca-cert <pem>` → `/etc/amadeus-runner/ca.pem` (`0640`) +
    `AMADEUS_RUNNER_CA_CERT` for private/internal-CA server TLS;
  - `--inventory amadeus|local` + `--local-inventory <file>` →
    `/etc/amadeus-runner/inventory.json` (`0640`) +
    `AMADEUS_RUNNER_INVENTORY`/`AMADEUS_RUNNER_LOCAL_INVENTORY`, so a
    network-isolated (T-b) runner is also a one-shot install.
  Flag combinations are validated up front (`--key-dir`/`--key-map` mutual
  exclusion, `--inventory local` ⇄ `--local-inventory` pairing, key-map
  syntax incl. duplicate or path-like `NAME`s, value-less flags), and all
  source files are existence-checked **before** the script mutates anything.
- **Post-install "before the first SSH run" summary.** When no custody flags
  were given, the script now ends with a loud, explicit block spelling out the
  exact `runner.env` edits + restart needed before the first SSH run (this
  guidance previously lived only in the install guide); when only key custody
  is missing, a shorter note is printed. The success summary also reports the
  inventory mode and every installed path.
- **`deploy/runner-install-check.sh`** — a CI-less smoke harness for the
  installer (the repo has no shell-test framework): `bash -n`, `--help`
  content, required-arg and flag-combination rejection, and the root gate —
  20 checks, all runnable unprivileged because validation now precedes the
  root check.

### Fixed

- `runner-install.sh`'s header comment named the script by its retired name
  (`install-runner.sh`); `--help` now exits `0` instead of `1`.
- The generated `runner.env` — which carries the registration token — was
  briefly world-readable (created with umask perms, `chmod`ed after the
  write); it is now created `0640 root:amadeus-runner` before any content is
  written. A flag given without a value now fails loudly ("requires a value")
  instead of dying silently on the argument shift.

### Documentation

- **Install guide** (`documentation/runner-install.html`): §3's example and

- **`deploy/amadeus-runner.env.example`**: cross-references the installer
  flags that can write the file's vars automatically, and fixes a stale
  pointer to the retired `deploy/install-runner.md` (now
  `documentation/runner-install.html`).

## 0.46.6 — Security Hardening & Workflow Resilience

**Date:** Jul 8, 2026

Remediation suite addressing IDOR, auth loop prevention, and workflow orphan reclamation.

### Security

- **IDOR Protection (`FR-H2`).** Added strict `AllowedScopes` authorization checks on executions, logs, and cancellation endpoints (`GET /api/v1/runs/{traceId}`, `GET /api/v1/runs/{traceId}/log`, `GET /api/v1/workflow-runs/{traceId}`, and `POST /api/v1/workflows/runs/{traceId}/cancel`). Restricted users attempting to access or mutate out-of-scope resources receive a `403 Forbidden` response.
- **Authentication Loop Prevention (`FR-H3`).** Added middleware in `frontend/src/api/client.ts` to intercept `401 Unauthorized` responses and redirect the browser to the login screen, ignoring `/me` requests to avoid infinite redirect loops at startup.
- **Integration Testing.** Hardened the `TestIDORScopeGates` test suite to cover all four scope-gated endpoints, and updated the test request dispatcher to inject matching double-submit CSRF cookies and headers for state-changing operations.

### Reliability

- **Workflow Orphan Reaper (`FR-R1`, `FR-R2`).** Implemented a startup sweep and a periodic background reaper (running every 10 minutes) in the workflow `Engine` to transition orphaned running workflows and their child runs (queued or running) to `failure` with reason `orchestrator_lost` if the process restarts or if runs exceed a 24-hour stale limit.
- **Unit Testing.** Added `TestEngineOrphanReaper` to verify database transitions and activity emission for reclaimed workflow runs and child jobs.

## 0.46.4 — Ansible runner hardening Phase 5: Tier 2 sandbox & always-on scoped env

**Date:** Jul 7, 2026

Fifth tranche of the runner-checkout program (**Phase 5 — Tier 2 sandbox**). Local-toolchain runs now execute inside a per-run
`systemd-run` scope for resource isolation, with availability detected and
reported (never silently assumed); scoped child env graduates from opt-in to
always-on. Backend + runner agent + the systemd unit template; no schema
changes.

### Security

- **Per-run Tier 2 sandbox (RX.10/§6.3).** Each ansible/terraform run (checkout
  AND body-only) is wrapped in a `systemd-run --scope` transient cgroup carrying
  the operator's resource caps (`-sandbox-memory-max` / `-sandbox-cpu-quota` /
  `-sandbox-tasks-max`). The filesystem/namespace/syscall hardening
  (`ProtectSystem=strict`, `PrivateTmp`, `NoNewPrivileges`, the syscall filter)
  is inherited by the child from the agent's own service unit — the per-run
  scope adds the resource bound the unit can't apply per run. `-no-sandbox`
  opts out.
- **Availability is detected, reported, never assumed.** A startup probe
  actually creates + collects a trivial scope (a host can ship `systemd-run`
  yet have no reachable manager); the result gates wrapping. When
  `-allow-checkout` is set but no sandbox is available, the agent logs a loud
  startup warning and every such run emits an `UNSANDBOXED` provenance line —
  an operator can never falsely assume a checkout run was sandboxed. The probe
  is bounded (3s) so a stuck `systemd-run` never hangs agent startup.
- **`sandboxed` capability token (§6.3).** A sandbox-available runner advertises
  `sandboxed`; a job may declare `requires: [sandboxed]` to never land on an
  unsandboxed host — reusing the Phase 4 claim-gating machinery. Sandbox status
  also rides the `toolchains` registration detail and shows on the Runners page
  (`checkout · sandboxed`).
- **Scoped child env is now always-on (completes RX.9).** The env-scoping that
  shipped opt-in in Phase 1 is now the only mode: a local-toolchain child sees
  the base safe-list + manifest env + galaxy dep-paths + the passthrough
  allowlist, never the agent's full environment — even when the manifest omits
  the `envPassthrough` field (an old server), which is now treated as an empty
  allowlist rather than a full-env fallback.

### Added

- **Egress-allowlist section in the runner systemd unit template**
  (`deploy/amadeus-runner.service`) — a commented, opt-in `IPAddressDeny=any` +
  `IPAddressAllow=…` block (P5), plus documentation of the inherited-sandbox +
  per-run-scope model. Enforcement stays commented until agency-zone address
  maps are stable.

---

## 0.46.3 — Ansible runner hardening Phase 4: capability advertisement & claim gating

**Date:** Jul 7, 2026

Fourth tranche of the runner-checkout program (**Phase 4 — capability advertisement + claim gating**). Runs can now declare
requirement tokens (e.g. `vault`, `collection:<fqcn>`) that route them only to
runners which actually satisfy them; runners advertise a widened capability set
plus a detected-toolchain detail for the Runners page. This completes the vault
claim-gating half deferred from Phase 3. Backend + runner agent + a Runners-page
display; migration **520** (`runners.toolchains` — the `requires_json` columns
shipped in Phase 3's migration 512).

### Added

- **Requirement-token claim gating (§5).** `claimRun` now matches a run's
  `requires` set against the runner's capability tokens entirely in SQL
  (`json_each` subset shape): a run is claimed only if `run_type ∈ capabilities`
  AND `requires ⊆ capabilities` AND the agency gate passes. A run with no
  requires (NULL/`[]`) matches any type-capable runner (back-compat). The claim
  statement is now a static parameter list — the old Go-built `IN (?,…)` clause
  was migrated to the same `json_each` form.
- **Widened capability advertisement (RX.7).** The agent detects its toolchain at
  registration and advertises flat tokens beyond the run-types: `ansible`,
  `checkout` (with `-allow-checkout`), `vault` (with `-vault-password-file`), and
  `collection:<fqcn>` per installed collection. Detected versions (ansible-core,
  collections) ride a new `toolchains` display detail.
- **Runners page toolchains display.** Each runner shows a compact
  `ansible-core 2.16.3 · N collections · checkout · vault` line; the noisy
  `collection:*` tokens are summarized rather than badged individually.
- **Requirements-aware stuck-run hint (§5).** A queued run with no eligible
  runner now explains *why* — "no online runner satisfies this run's requirements
  [vault]" (vs the coarser "no online runner in agency X") — via a pure-SQL
  `json_each` probe that mirrors the claim gates.
- **`requires` on the job API.** Cronomicon jobs can declare requirement tokens
  through the composer (`JobComposeInput.requires`); the job detail returns
  `requires` for git and amadeus jobs alike. OpenAPI updated in both spec copies;
  the runner `capabilities` schema widened from the `RunType` enum to free-form
  tokens.

### Notes

- The composer's requirement-token *editor UI* and a live-app visual check of the
  toolchains display are deferred to a focused follow-up — the claim-gate,
  advertisement, and stuck-run hint (the functional core) are complete and
  covered by tests; git jobs already declare `requires` via `spec.requires` in
  YAML. Agent-side capability *refresh on re-poll* is also deferred: detection
  runs at registration/restart.

---

## 0.46.2 — Ansible runner hardening Phase 3: requirements, galaxy & vault

**Date:** Jul 7, 2026

Third tranche of the runner-checkout program (**Phase 3 — requirements / galaxy / vault**). Checkout projects can now declare
`requirements.yml` dependencies (installed per run into the ephemeral workdir),
opt into Ansible Vault, and are lint-gated for pin reproducibility and inline
plaintext secrets. Backend + runner agent only; no frontend changes. The
capability/claim-gating half of vault (routing a `vault` job only to runners that
have a password file) lands with Phase 4.

### Added

- **Per-run `requirements.yml` install (RX.4/RX.12).** When a checkout project
  contains `<project_root>/requirements.yml`, the agent installs its collections
  and roles into an ephemeral `<workdir>/.deps` and points
  `ANSIBLE_COLLECTIONS_PATH`/`ANSIBLE_ROLES_PATH` there (workdir first, so project
  deps win). The verified SHA, `ansible-core` version, and every install line are
  emitted as run provenance.
- **Skip-if-satisfied (§4).** A collection already present in the runner's
  provisioned base at the **exact** pinned version is not re-downloaded — a
  pre-provisioned runner installs nothing and runs offline; repeat runs don't
  hammer the galaxy source. Roles (git-SHA pins) are always installed per run. An
  unsatisfied pin whose download fails **fails the run loudly** — there is no
  silent fallback to a differently-versioned local copy.
- **Galaxy source config (P6).** Defaults to the public `galaxy.ansible.com`;
  `-galaxy-server` (config `galaxyServer`, env `AMADEUS_RUNNER_GALAXY_SERVER`)
  points installs at a private mirror/hub.
- **Ansible Vault opt-in (RX.13).** A job declares `spec.requires: [vault]`
  (synced to `jobs.requires_json`, snapshotted onto the run). The manifest then
  sets `Checkout.UsesVault`, and the agent passes `--vault-password-file` from its
  **own** runner-local config (`-vault-password-file`) — the password never
  travels (D1). If a vault run reaches an agent with no password file configured,
  it is **refused loudly**. Migration **512** (`jobs.requires_json`,
  `runs.requires_json`).
- **Pinning lint (RX.5).** `amadeus validate` fails CI when a `requirements.yml`
  collection lacks an exact version or a git role isn't pinned to a full commit
  SHA; git sync surfaces the identical findings as never-blocking warnings.
- **Project tree secret-scan (§6.2).** `amadeus validate` (error) and sync
  (warning) scan a project's YAML/INI/template files for inline plaintext secrets
  the value-based log redactor could never mask — catching the YAML-form
  (`key: value`) secrets the INI-only inventory guard never saw. Vault-encrypted
  (`$ANSIBLE_VAULT`) files and `lookup('env', …)` indirection are exempt.

### Security

- **Vault-decrypted values bypass redaction — documented loudly.** The runner
  security guide now states that a value a playbook decrypts from vault at run
  time is not one Cronomicon can mask, so `no_log: true` is mandatory on any task
  that could print one; operators should register the vault password itself as an
  Cronomicon stored secret (the redactor then masks that value) and prefer env-var
  indirection where possible.

---

## 0.46.1 — Ansible runner hardening Phase 2: checkout-mode core (pinned project checkout)

**Date:** Jul 7, 2026

Second tranche of the runner-checkout program (**Phase 2 — checkout-mode core**). Runners can now execute full Ansible playbook
**projects** (roles, `vars_files`, `.j2` templates) by checking out the playbooks
repo at a **server-pinned commit SHA**, instead of only single self-contained
playbook bodies. Checkout is opt-in per job (a project wrapper) **and** per runner
(`-allow-checkout` + a repo allowlist); body-only runs are unchanged. This bumps
the runner wire protocol to **v3**. Backend + runner agent only; no frontend
changes. Dependency installs, capability/claim gating, and the systemd sandbox
remain later phases (3–5).

### Added

- **Runner-side pinned checkout (protocol v3, RX.1/RX.2/RX.3).** A new
  `ManifestCheckout` (`{repo, sha, entry}`) tells the agent to fetch the repo into
  a persistent bare mirror using its **own** read-only deploy credential (never
  shipped — D1), verify the pinned commit exists, `git archive` that commit into a
  fresh per-run working tree (no `.git`, torn down on every exit path), and run the
  entry playbook from the tree. A full commit SHA is required — a branch/tag never
  travels.
- **Project grouping in the Script catalog (§7).** A `kind: Script` wrapper may
  declare `spec.project_root` (a repo-relative directory) + `spec.entry` (the
  entry playbook). The whole directory becomes **one** catalog script; its member
  files (`roles/`, templates, included vars) are no longer mis-synthesized into
  bogus standalone "playbook" entries. Discovery is **two-pass** so grouping is
  correct regardless of file visit order — a project member listed before its
  wrapper still groups.
- **Enqueue-time SHA pin (RX.2).** A checkout run snapshots the sync clone's
  current commit (`git_sync_state.last_sha`) and entry onto the run at enqueue, so
  a mid-run re-sync cannot retarget an in-flight run. Migration **511**
  (`scripts.project_root`, `jobs.project_root`, `runs.checkout_sha`,
  `runs.checkout_entry`).
- **New runner agent config for checkout.** `-allow-checkout` (opt-in),
  `-checkout-repos` (clone-URL allowlist), `-mirror-dir`, and
  `-checkout-token` / `-checkout-token-file` (the read-only deploy credential),
  each also settable via config file and `AMADEUS_RUNNER_*` env.
- **`amadeus validate` project checks (§7).** A project wrapper is validated: the
  `project_root` must stay inside the repo, `entry` must be declared and live under
  the root and exist on disk, and overlapping/nested roots warn (first wins).

### Security

- **Checkout is refused unless explicitly enabled (RX.6).** An agent without
  `-allow-checkout`, or handed a repo outside its `-checkout-repos` allowlist,
  refuses the run loudly — a compromised server cannot point a runner at an
  arbitrary repo. The SHA is re-validated as a full commit hash agent-side, and the
  extracted archive is written through a path-traversal guard.
- **v3 gate.** A checkout run assigned to a pre-v3 agent hard-fails
  `agent_too_old` rather than silently falling back to the display body (mirrors
  the v2 inventory gate).

---

## 0.46.0 — Ansible runner hardening Phase 1: scoped env, per-run workdir, real timeouts

**Date:** Jul 7, 2026

First tranche of the ratified runner-checkout program (**Phase 1 — universal hardening**): the runner agent stops handing its entire
environment to local-toolchain processes, every ansible/terraform run gets a fresh
per-run working directory, and `timeout_seconds` is finally enforced at the process
level. These wins apply with or without the upcoming checkout mode (Phases 2–6, not
yet implemented). Backend + runner agent only; no frontend or API-surface changes.

### Security

- **Playbooks no longer see the runner's full environment (RX.9).** Previously any
  ansible/terraform body could read every value in the runner's environment —
  including everything sourced from `secrets.env`. The manifest now carries an
  `envPassthrough` allowlist of env-var NAMES (never values — D1) computed
  server-side as the union of: the shipped inventory's `{{ lookup('env', NAME) }}`
  references, each resolved target's `authKeyEnvVar`, and the job's new
  `env_passthrough` spec list. A current agent seeing the field builds the child
  env from an explicit base safe-list (`PATH, HOME, USER, LOGNAME, SHELL, TERM,
  TMPDIR, TZ, LANG, LC_*`, `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`) + the manifest env snapshot + the
  allowlisted names — nothing else. An allowlisted name unset on the runner fails
  the run loudly instead of surfacing as a silently-empty lookup.
- **New agent config for scoped-env control.** `-env-base-extra` (config
  `envBaseExtra`, env `AMADEUS_RUNNER_ENV_BASE_EXTRA`) adds operator-declared names
  to the base safe-list — visible in config, never silently inherited.
  `-exclude-ssh-auth-sock` drops `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` for runners that use per-host key
  files (it is default-in because ansible needs it for agent-based SSH auth, but it
  grants signing access to every key the runner's ssh-agent holds).
- **Back-compat is explicit, not accidental.** The field is additive on protocol
  v2: an older agent ignores it (legacy behavior); a new agent against an older
  server (field absent) keeps the legacy full-env inheritance. Presence of the
  field — even as an empty list — is what engages scoping, so it is shipped
  non-null for every local-toolchain manifest. Local-mode runners' own inventories
  are invisible to the server; names they need beyond the computed list are the
  operator's `-env-base-extra`.

### Added

- **Per-run working directory for all local-toolchain runs (§6.1).** Every
  ansible/terraform run now executes in a fresh `0700` directory under the agent's
  state dir; the materialized inventory temp file lives inside it, and the whole
  directory is removed on every exit path — success, failure, and kill. Previously
  only the inventory temp file was cleaned, and runs executed in the agent
  process's cwd.
- **Job spec `env_passthrough` (migration 510).** Git jobs may declare the env-var
  NAMES their runner-executed playbook needs (`spec.env_passthrough`), synced to a
  new `jobs.env_passthrough` column (the `prompts_json` pattern) and folded into
  the manifest allowlist. Cronomicon-composed jobs default to none (composer field
  lands with the Phase 4 capability work).

### Fixed

- **`timeout_seconds` is now enforced for runner runs.** The value rode the
  manifest but the agent never honored it; a hung playbook ran forever. The agent
  now enforces it at the process level for both local-toolchain and SSH-fan-out
  runs (mirroring the in-app SSH executor's A12 fix), emits a
  `run timed out after Ns; process killed` log line, and reports a non-zero exit.
- **Kill/timeout now terminates the whole toolchain process tree (Linux).** The
  agent previously killed only the direct child; grandchildren (ansible module
  subprocesses, ssh muxes) survived holding the output pipes open, so a killed or
  timed-out run didn't actually end until every orphan exited. Local-toolchain
  children now run in their own process group, ctx-cancel SIGKILLs the group, and
  a 10s `WaitDelay` force-closes the pipes as a backstop.

### Changed

- **Terraform runs execute in the per-run workdir, not the agent's cwd.** A
  terraform job that relied on `.tf` files in the agent process's working
  directory must pass `-chdir=<path>` in its body (or use env-driven config); the
  old implicit-cwd behavior was fragile and leaked state between runs.

## 0.45.7 — Code cleanup Phases 6 & 7: frontend performance + repo/toolchain hygiene

**Date:** Jul 4, 2026

The final tranche of the pre-production cleanup pass (**CC.23–CC.27**) — frontend performance and repository/toolchain hygiene. `tsc`, the
147 Vitest tests, `make verify`, and `vite build` are green.

### Fixed

- **Dashboard stat counts are now exact, not truncated (CC.23).** "Running Now" and
  "Failed (24h)" were derived by client-filtering a single default `/runs` page, so
  the counts silently capped at ~one page (≈50 runs). They now come from targeted,
  live server-filtered requests (`status=running` / `status=danger` + `from` +
  `kind=job` to exclude ssh-test probes); the page envelope's `totalItems` is the true
  count, and the requests poll via `useLiveGet` so the tiles refresh while the
  dashboard is open. The failed-run banner and "Currently Running" list read from the
  same feeds. (The jobs-derived "Total Jobs"/"Active Schedules" tiles are page-based
  and out of CC.23's scope.)

### Changed

- **Runner guides lazy-loaded (CC.24).** The Install/Config/Security guide pages embed
  ~51 KB of raw HTML (`backend/deploy/runner-*.html`); they were eagerly imported into
  the main bundle. They now `React.lazy`-load into their own chunk (like the Workflow
  Editor route), fetched only on first visit — the main JS chunk drops by ~55 KB.
- **`make generate` retired (CC.26 / CC-D5).** `oapi-codegen@v2.4.1` can't parse the
  OpenAPI 3.1 spec (upstream #373) — the target produced no usable output
  (`internal/apigen` never existed) yet a `generate-check` CI job advertised a drift
  guard that couldn't run. Removed the `generate`/`generate-check` Make targets, the
  `oapi-codegen.yaml` config, and the CI job. Backend spec-drift is guarded by the
  existing OpenAPI conformance tests + the two-copy byte-identity check (both run under
  `make verify`) plus the frontend `npm run gen`.
- **docker-compose production posture (CC.27 / CC-D6).** Enabled `restart:
  unless-stopped` and parameterized the timezone (`TZ: ${TZ:-America/Los_Angeles}`) in
  the root `docker-compose.yml`, and fixed the stale `backend/Dockerfile` comment that
  pointed at a compose file in `backend/deploy/` (it lives at the repo root). Operators
  should confirm these values for their deployment.

### Removed

- **Trimmed the oversized icon master (CC.25).** `assets/amadeus_icon.png` was a 4.7 MB,
  2048×2048 master that nothing in the app references (the served favicon,
  `frontend/public/amadeus-icon.png`, is a separate 58 KB file and is untouched).
  Resized to a 512×512, 232 KB master — a 95% reduction; the original remains in git
  history if a larger source is ever needed.

## 0.45.6 — Fix: theme toggle no longer resets in-page state

**Date:** Jul 4, 2026

### Fixed

- **Light/dark toggle preserves the active tab (and search, pagination, expanded
  rows).** The theme toggle repainted views by putting `key={mode}` on the router
  `<Outlet>`, which **remounted** the whole route subtree on every toggle and reset
  each view's local state (e.g. Env Vars / Scopes / Settings tabs snapping back to
  the default). `App` now subscribes to the theme context so a toggle **re-renders**
  the route tree — recreating the route elements, which repaints every view from the
  mutable `c` tokens — instead of remounting it. Verified safe because no component
  is `React.memo`'d and no `useMemo`/`useCallback` caches a theme-derived style, so a
  plain re-render repaints everything while preserving state.

## 0.45.3 — Code cleanup Phase 4: backend consolidation

**Date:** Jul 3, 2026

Phase 4 of the pre-production cleanup pass (**CC.12–CC.15**) —
backend consolidation refactors under the existing test suites. **No API behaviour
change** beyond the audit NULL-semantics normalization noted below. All list-endpoint
JSON, tag-handler responses, and permission gates are unchanged; the full backend test
suite, `go vet`, and `deadcode -test` are green, and a dev-seeded instance was
smoke-checked (tag writes, change-log/activity feeds, audit export).

### Changed

- **One tag-update skeleton for all seven tagged entities (CC.12).** The copy-pasted
  decode→normalize→UPDATE→404 prefix of `updateScriptTags`, `updateJobTags`,
  `updateWorkflowTags`, `updateScheduleTags`, and the env-var/secret/credential tag
  handlers is now a single `writeTagsUpdate(table, whereSQL, notFound, whereArgs…)`
  helper. Each handler keeps its own — deliberately divergent — re-fetch, audit, and
  permission tail (the differences documented in `settings_tags_mount.go`'s header are
  preserved exactly: session+CSRF vs `requirePerm`, `workflow` vs `settings` audit
  writers, the composite `(source,name)` schedule key, and the audit-before-refetch
  ordering). All five tag test suites — including the permission-gate and slash-name
  cases — pass unchanged.
- **Single change_log / activity writer (CC.13, CC-D2).** `settings.WriteChangeLog` /
  `writeActivity` and `workflow.InsertChangeLog` / `EmitActivity` now delegate to one
  new leaf `internal/auditlog` package, so there is exactly one INSERT statement per
  table behind those four writers (`workflow.ActivityParams` is now a type alias of
  `auditlog.ActivityParams`, so every call site is unchanged). Per **CC-D2**, the
  change_log optional columns (`target`, `details`) are standardized on **empty strings**
  — `workflow.InsertChangeLog` previously stored NULLs there — and **migration 500**
  normalizes the older NULL rows. Activity optional columns keep NULL-when-empty
  semantics (the `outcome` CHECK constraint forbids `''` and the numeric columns have no
  empty form). Every reader already coerces NULL→`""`, so no read or filter changes. The
  run-execution lifecycle activity emitters in `runner`/`sshexec`/`gitlab` are distinct
  events (not the duplicated writers CC.13 targeted) and remain their own inserts.
- **Single filter slice on the five list endpoints (CC.14).** `listRuns`, `listActivity`,
  `listChangeLog`, `listWorkflowRuns`, and `listWorkflows` dropped the parallel
  `args`/`cArgs` double-append (two slices that had to be kept in lockstep — a documented
  footgun): the COUNT now reuses the one filter slice before `LIMIT/OFFSET` is appended
  for the page query. The repeated `totalPages`/JSON envelope tail across eight list
  handlers collapsed into one `pageEnvelope` helper.
- **Shared tag helpers extracted (CC.15).** The duplicated `parseTags` (api + settings)
  and `normalizeTags` + caps moved into one leaf `internal/tagutil` package
  (`tagutil.Parse` / `tagutil.Normalize`), removing the copies. A `mustActor` helper
  collapses the `IdentityFrom`-then-401 boilerplate; it is adopted in the tag handlers
  touched here, with the broader ~70-site rollout left to happen per-file as those files
  are next touched (per the plan's incremental guidance).

## 0.45.2 — Code cleanup Phase 3: backend query efficiency

**Date:** Jul 3, 2026

Phase 3 of the pre-production cleanup pass (**CC.8–CC.11**) —
backend query-efficiency work. The list endpoints now derive their per-row data in SQL
instead of issuing a follow-up query per row, the audit export streams instead of
buffering whole tables, and the Scripts list stops shipping script bodies. The only wire
changes are additive/agreed: a new `sourceKind` field on `Script`, the Scripts **list**
no longer carrying the `command`/`script` blobs (still on the detail response), and the
audit export's empty result serializing as `[]` rather than `null` (a downloaded file the
UI never parses).

### Changed

- **Jobs list folds its per-row queries into the page query (CC.8).** `listJobs`
  previously ran two follow-up queries per row on top of the CC.2 status derivation —
  the latest-run lookup and the `definition_schedules` "+N" badge COUNT (~4 queries ×
  up to 200 rows a page). The latest run is now joined once by its rowid (status,
  timestamp and duration all come from the same row) and the schedule count is a
  correlated subquery, so a page costs a fixed number of queries regardless of size. A
  new white-box test (via a query-counting driver) asserts the count does not grow with
  page size and that the derived fields match the latest run.
- **Workflows + schedules lists batched the same way (CC.9).** `listWorkflows` dropped
  its three per-row lookups (`isWorkflowDisabled`, `workflowLastRun`, `loadSchedules`):
  paused state and the latest run are derived in the page query, and Next Run is computed
  from a single batched schedules query per page. The unpaginated schedule inventory
  (`listSchedules` / `listUpcomingSchedules`) — which the Inventory, Upcoming and
  Dashboard views read whole and page client-side, so it deliberately stays unpaginated —
  replaced its three-per-entry lookups (enabled, paused, last-run) with a fixed set of
  preload queries; a `COALESCE(schedule_name,'default')` grouped query reproduces the rule
  that the `default` entry also absorbs legacy NULL-schedule runs.
- **Audit export streams row-by-row (CC.10).** `settings.ExportAudit` no longer buffers
  the entire `change_log` / `activity` / `runs` / `schedule_pushes` tables into memory
  before marshaling — it streams each table's rows straight to the response as JSON or
  CSV, so a full-table export (no date range) stays flat on memory. The four copy-pasted
  scan functions collapsed into one generic helper. Golden-file tests pin byte-for-byte
  parity with the previous non-empty output; the empty JSON export now serializes as `[]`.

### Removed

- **Script bodies out of the Scripts list response (CC.11).** `GET /scripts` no longer
  ships the (potentially large) `command`/`script` blob columns per row. A server-derived
  `sourceKind` field (`command` | `script` | `file`) badges each row, and the body is
  fetched on demand from `/script-content/{name}` when a row is expanded — that endpoint
  already resolves all three body kinds. `GET /scripts/{name}` still returns the full body
  (and now also `sourceKind`). Touches both `openapi.yaml` copies and the regenerated
  TypeScript client.

## 0.45.0 — Code cleanup Phase 1: list-endpoint correctness

**Date:** Jul 3, 2026

Phase 1 of the pre-production cleanup pass (**CC.1–CC.4**) —
correctness bug fixes only, no feature or API-shape changes.

### Fixed

- **Jobs list `status=` filter vs pagination (CC.2).** The display status
  (paused → latest-run state → idle) is now derived **in SQL** (correlated
  `paused_jobs`/latest-run subqueries feeding a `CASE`), so a `status=` filter
  applies **before** `COUNT(*)` and `LIMIT/OFFSET`. Previously the filter ran
  per row after pagination: filtered requests returned short pages (e.g. 35 of
  50) with the unfiltered `totalItems`/`totalPages`. Regression test proven to
  fail against the pre-fix code. A failed count now fails the request (500)
  instead of silently answering `totalItems: 0` beside a full page.
- **Jobs toast auto-dismiss race (CC.4).** `fireToast` in the Jobs view now
  cancels the prior dismiss timer and clears it on unmount (the ref+cleanup
  pattern the Workflows view already used), so a second toast fired within
  3.5s no longer disappears early.

### Changed

- **One redactor per scope per request on the runs list (CC.3).** Rendering a
  runs page no longer rebuilds the secrets redactor for every row — each build
  envelope-decrypts **every stored secret**, so a 200-row page cost 200 full
  secret sweeps. Redactors are now built lazily, at most once per distinct
  scope per request (fail-closed semantics unchanged), and the per-row
  `jobs`-rowid reverse lookup is one batched query per page (now under the
  request context). New white-box test asserts the ≤ 1-build-per-scope bound.

### Removed

- **Dead, silently-failing COUNT in `listJobs` (CC.1).** The stale
  `TrimPrefix`-based count built invalid SQL, swallowed the error, and its
  result was discarded; the surviving count is folded into the CC.2 derived
  query.

## 0.44.2 — Python run-type

**Date:** Jul 2, 2026

Python joins Bash, Ansible, Terraform, PowerShell and Perl as a first-class
**run-type**, handled the same way as the existing shell-family types.

### Added

- **Detection & validation** (`internal/gitlab`): `.py` files sync as `python`
  scripts; `python` is an allowed `run_type` in the pragma/YAML validator; the
  `no_shebang` linter accepts `#!/usr/bin/env python3` (and bare `python`).
- **Variable scanning**: a new `python` extractor detects `os.environ['X']`,
  `os.environ.get('X', default)` and `os.getenv('X', default)` references (a
  fallback argument marks the variable optional), so the Scripts detail, Run
  dialog and Job Composer show referenced variables for Python scripts too.
- **Execution**: `python` is a **shell-family / SSH-capable** type (like
  bash/perl/powershell) — it is added to `SSHRunTypes`, resolves to interpreter
  `python3 -c`, and is claimed by the in-app SSH executor and slim runner agents
  (`bash,perl,powershell,python`). It is **not** runner-only (unlike
  ansible/terraform).
- **Schema**: migration **490** (schema v490) widens the `run_type` CHECK on
  `jobs`/`runs`/`scripts` to include `python` (a 12-step table rebuild per the
  migration-170 precedent; data-preserving, with a round-trip test).
- **API**: the `RunType` enum gains `python` (both OpenAPI copies + regenerated
  TS client).
- **UI**: a Python badge icon (`python.webp`) with a distinct blue tone; `python`
  added to the Scope supported-types picker, the History type filter, the Publish
  run-type selector, and runner capability chips.
- **Docs**: README, AGENTS.md, the user/administrator manuals, and the runner
  install guide updated to list Python.

## 0.44.0 — Visual workflow canvas

**Date:** Jul 1, 2026

The **interactive workflow canvas** (Option C — the workflow-update-2b plan; closes backlog item **V2-17** and the **W1** watch-out) graduates in-app workflow authoring from a one-level linear form to a **structured, nestable graph canvas** (React Flow / `@xyflow/react`). This is the umbrella release for the program that landed incrementally as **v0.43.0 → v0.43.8**; it makes the README's long-standing "visual graph composition" claim literally true. The engine, the compose API, and capability semantics are **unchanged** — authoring stays Admin-only (`compose`) and amadeus-source only (A9).

### Added — the canvas (WC-P0 … WC-P7)

- **Structured block canvas (WC1).** Job steps are nodes; sequence, `parallel` blocks, and `branch` conditions are structured containers with side-by-side Pass/Fail arms. Constraints are enforced **at drag time** (can't drop a container into a parallel; pickers offer only legal upstream producers), so the canvas **cannot emit an invalid `steps[]`** — serialization is deterministic, no post-hoc inference.
- **Nested authoring (WC5) — the headline capability.** Branch-in-branch and parallel-in-branch arms now author natively, **retiring the read-only "complex graph" fallback**; the linear editor could never represent these.
- **Full per-node inspector (WC6).** Every job node (including parallel members and branch-arm jobs) exposes `label`, `jobSource`, `retries`/`backoffSeconds`/`continueOnError`, and A12 inputs — closing the old `JobLeaf` drop-gap where these were silently lost on round-trip.
- **On-canvas A12 data edges (WC14).** Drag a producer job's handle to a downstream consumer to wire `inputs[KEY] = {fromStep, fromOutput}`; `isValidConnection` rejects illegal wires (downstream→upstream, parallel siblings, cross-arm) at drag time, mirroring the engine.
- **Simple ｜ Advanced toggle + full CRUD.** Create, edit, and delete workflows in the canvas; a lossless round-trip toggle keeps the linear list editor for flat chains. You can now author a **new nested workflow entirely in-app** — previously only possible via Git YAML.
- **Persisted layout (WC-P7).** Hand-arranged node positions survive reload — advisory-only migration **480** `workflows.layout_json` (nullable; `NULL` ⇒ dagre auto-layout), never part of the definition or `steps_hash`, with a **Reset layout** escape hatch. `Workflow.layout` + `WorkflowComposeInput.layout` added to both OpenAPI copies.
- **Chrome & a11y (WC-P2/P5).** Theme-reactive custom nodes, `<Controls>`/`<Background>`/`fitView`, a minimap above a node-count threshold, a metadata panel (name/description/enabled/schedules), empty/loading/error/git-read-only states, an unsaved-changes guard, and keyboard equivalents for every gesture.

### Changed

- **First code-split (WC-P0/WC4).** The editor route is now `React.lazy` + `<Suspense>` — the app's first code-split — keeping React Flow and its CSS out of the eager bundle. The main chunk stays ~614 KB; the canvas ships in a separate ~274 KB lazy chunk.
- **Correctness spine (WC-P1).** A pure, unit-tested round-trip model (`canvasModel.ts`: `toCanvasTree`/`toSteps`), a scope-aware upstream walk mirroring the engine, and a local `ValidateSteps` mirror for precise per-node errors. The server dry-run `POST /workflows/validate` remains the backstop.

### Notes

- **No backend change for authoring** — the compose endpoints already accepted the full nested `steps[]`. The only backend touch is the advisory `layout_json` column (480).
- Reconciles the README ("visual graph composition" now accurate — `README.md`) and the honest v20 follow-on note; supersedes the read-only Option B DAG (the workflow-update-2 plan), whose edge-derivation model this reuses.
- Decisions ratified as the **`WC` series** in the architecture notes §12.

## 0.43.8 — Workflow canvas: persisted layout (WC-P7)

**Date:** Jul 1, 2026

WC-P7 of the Visual Workflow Canvas program — the optional persisted-layout follow-on. Node positions hand-arranged in the graph editor now **survive a reload** instead of always being re-derived by dagre. The layout is **advisory only**: it is stored in its own column, is never part of the workflow definition, and **cannot affect execution order or `steps_hash`**.

### Added

- **Drag-to-arrange, persisted.** In the graph editor's canvas, nodes are now **draggable**; the arrangement is saved with the workflow (`POST`/`PUT /workflows`, new optional `layout` field) and restored over dagre on the next load. A **Reset layout** button discards the hand-arrangement and returns to dagre auto-layout. Positions are keyed by the deterministic flow-node id, so they re-associate across reloads; newly added nodes still auto-layout.
- **`workflows.layout_json` column (migration 480).** Additive, nullable, advisory-only — `NULL` ⇒ auto-layout. Omitted from every definition/sync upsert (like `tags`), so a Git re-sync never touches it; a layout-less save (e.g. from the linear editor) **preserves** any existing layout via `COALESCE`. `migrate_test.go` head bumped 470 → 480 with a DROP-COLUMN round-trip test.
- **OpenAPI `Workflow.layout` + `WorkflowComposeInput.layout`.** A `{nodeId: {x, y}}` map on both the read and write schemas (both byte-identical spec copies; `npm run gen` regenerated).

### Internal

- New tests: `parseLayout` tolerance (frontend Vitest — null/malformed/non-finite entries dropped), the migration 480 data round-trip, and a compose-API layout round-trip asserting create-echo, layout-less-edit **preserve**, new-layout **replace**, and that the layout never leaks into `steps`.
- **Verified:** `make -C backend verify` green (migration round-trip + full suite + build); `npm run gen` clean; `tsc -b && vite build` green with the main bundle unchanged at ~614 KB (React Flow drag wiring stays in the lazy editor chunk); **147 Vitest tests** pass.
- The workflow-update-2b plan — phase **WC-P7** of 9 (only the **WC-P8** release ritual remains).

## 0.43.7 — Workflow canvas: Simple ｜ Advanced editing + create/delete (WC-P6)

**Date:** Jul 1, 2026

WC-P6 of the Visual Workflow Canvas program — the last core phase. The canvas graduates from "nested-workflows-only" to a **first-class, opt-in editing surface** for any amadeus workflow, with a safe rollout toggle back to the linear editor and full create / edit / delete.

### Added

- **Simple ｜ Advanced toggle.** The linear editor gains a "Graph editor (Advanced) →" button; the canvas editor gains a "Simple editor" button — enabled only when the graph is **one level deep** (a nested graph can't round-trip to the linear editor, so the button is disabled with a note). State converts losslessly through the round-trip serializer (`emitStep`/`toSteps` ⇄ `toCanvasTree`/`toEditorStep`), so you can move a workflow between the two editors freely.
- **Create + delete in the canvas.** The canvas metadata panel now includes the workflow **Name** (editable when creating, immutable on edit); `submitCanvas` **POSTs a new** workflow or **PUTs an existing** one with full-state resend (`enabled` + schedules — RT-3), and a two-click **Delete** flow matches the linear editor. You can now author a **new nested workflow entirely in-app** — previously only possible via Git YAML.

### Notes — already in place from earlier phases

- The `POST /workflows/validate` → POST/PUT save path, `compose` capability gating (Admin-only), git-source read-only (409), and per-node validation-error placement (the client `validateTree` mirror) landed with WC-P1/P3; this phase makes the canvas reachable for every amadeus workflow, not just nested ones.

### Internal

Full suite **144 Vitest tests** pass; `tsc -b && vite build` green; main bundle unchanged at ~614 KB.

## 0.43.5 — Workflow canvas: A12 connect seeds a default key (WC-P4 fix)

**Date:** Jul 1, 2026

Fixes a UX gap in WC-P4 found during a browser pass. Drawing an A12 wire on the canvas added an env input with a **blank key**, which drew **no edge** (the renderer needs a non-blank key) and was silently **dropped on save** (the serializer filters blank-key inputs) — so a successful drag looked like it did nothing until you opened the consumer's inspector and named the key. The connect now seeds a **valid, unique default key** derived from the producer's job name (UPPER_SNAKE — e.g. `alpha-job-01` → `ALPHA_JOB_01`), so the wire is **immediately visible** (its dashed data edge draws) and **survives save**; the user refines the key and `fromOutput` in the step's inspector.

### Fixed

- `WorkflowCanvasEditor`'s on-connect handler uses the new `defaultInputKey(producerName, existingKeys)` (in `canvasEdit.ts`) instead of an empty key; the canvas hint text is updated to match.

### Internal (tests)

- `canvasEdit.test.ts` — 3 tests for `defaultInputKey` (UPPER_SNAKE derivation, never-blank guarantee, uniqueness suffixing). Full suite **142 Vitest tests** pass; `tsc -b && vite build` green; main bundle unchanged at ~614 KB.
- A WC-P4 refinement of the Visual Workflow Canvas program.

## 0.43.4 — Workflow canvas: on-canvas A12 data edges (WC-P4)

**Date:** Jun 30, 2026

WC-P4 of the Visual Workflow Canvas program — inter-job env passing (A12) becomes a **first-class canvas gesture**: drag from one job to a downstream job to wire an env input, instead of only filling it in a form. This turns the canvas from a picture into a place you connect things.

### Added

- **On-canvas A12 wiring.** `WorkflowCanvas` gains an optional connect mode (`connectable` + `onConnectEdge` + `isValidEdge`); in edit mode job nodes expose grab handles. `WorkflowCanvasEditor` wires drag-to-connect: dropping producer → consumer adds an env input on the consumer (its key is named in the step's inspector). **`isValidConnection` enforces the engine's rules at drag time** — both endpoints must be jobs and the producer must be **upstream** of the consumer (via the scoped-upstream walk), so a downstream→upstream / parallel-sibling / cross-arm wire is refused mid-drag (WC14).

- `WorkflowCanvasEditor.test.tsx` — a **jsdom render smoke** for the interactive editor: React Flow mounts (with `ResizeObserver` / `DOMMatrixReadOnly` shims), a controlled `+ Job` edit fires `onChange`, and validation issues surface. Closes the earlier "visual smoke pending" gap for the WC-P3/P4 UI at the mount-without-throwing level.
- Full suite **139 Vitest tests** pass. Code-split holds: editor chunk ~268 → ~269 KB; **main bundle unchanged at ~614 KB**. `tsc -b && vite build` green.
- The workflow-update-2b plan — phase **WC-P4** of 9.

## 0.43.3 — Workflow canvas: structural editing (WC-P3)

**Date:** Jun 30, 2026

WC-P3 of the Visual Workflow Canvas program — the canvas becomes **interactive**. A new structured, **nestable** editor authors the full step graph, and **nested workflows** (previously a read-only "complex graph" dead-end) now load into it for editing in the Workflow Editor. This closes the two related gaps the linear editor left open: nested branch/parallel authoring (**RT-2** — the read-only fallback is retired) and full per-node fidelity (**RT-1** — every node gets an inspector for the fields the one-level model silently dropped).

- `frontend/src/views/workflows/canvasEdit.ts` — the pure editing core: immutable tree mutations (`insertNode` / `appendNode` / `removeNode` (cascade) / `updateNode` / `moveNode`), stable-id node factories, and `withFreshIds`. Every edit returns a new tree.
- `frontend/src/views/workflows/WorkflowCanvasEditor.tsx` — a controlled, recursive nested-tree editor: add **Job / Parallel / Branch** per lane, insert / reorder / delete, a **per-node inspector** (label, `jobSource`, `retries` / `backoffSeconds` / `continueOnError`, and A12 inputs driven by the engine-faithful **scoped-upstream** picker — **RT-1**), a branch **condition editor** (enum dropdowns), live `validateTree` error markers on the offending nodes, and a live read-only `WorkflowCanvas` preview.
- Nested (deeper-than-one-level) amadeus workflows now open in the canvas editor instead of the read-only screen (**RT-2**); saves go through the existing compose path with **full-state resend** (`enabled` + preserved inline schedules + `scheduleRefs` — **RT-3**).

### Internal (build/tests)

- `canvasEdit.test.ts` — 16 tests (insert / remove-cascade / update / move / `withFreshIds` / immutability). Full suite **136 Vitest tests** pass.
- Code-split holds: the editor chunk grew ~252 KB → ~268 KB; the **main bundle is unchanged at ~614 KB**. `tsc -b && vite build` green.
- The common one-level linear editor is untouched; the canvas editor is scoped to the nested-workflow path. The workflow-update-2b plan — phase **WC-P3** of 9.

## 0.43.1 — Workflow canvas: round-trip model + validation (WC-P1)

**Date:** Jun 30, 2026

WC-P1 of the Visual Workflow Canvas program — the **correctness spine**: a pure, framework-free `canvasModel.ts` that the React Flow canvas (WC-P2+) will render and edit. It carries the editable **ordered nested authoring tree** (the source of truth — array order lives in the model, never in node positions), the **round-trip serializer** between that tree and the compose `steps[]` wire shape (generalizing the editor's one-level `emitStep`/`toEditorStep` to arbitrary nesting, so nested branches/parallels are finally representable), a **scoped-upstream walk** mirroring the engine's `validateStepSeq` visibility (parallel-sibling invisibility, branch-arm scoping) for the A12 `fromStep` / branch `jobRef` pickers, and a path/tree-aware **`ValidateSteps` mirror** (incl. the same-path duplicate-name guard) that places each error on the right node. No UI yet — purely the model + its tests.

### Added

- `frontend/src/views/workflows/canvasModel.ts` — `toCanvasTree` / `toSteps` (round-trip serializer), `upstreamProducers` (scoped-upstream walk), `validateTree` (engine-faithful validation oracle), plus `conditionLabel` / `findNode` helpers and the definition-shaped `DefStep` / `CanvasNode` types.

### Internal (tests)

- `canvasModel.test.ts` — **43 tests**: round-trip identity across every step shape (flat / parallel / both-arm branch / `output_match` / nested branch-in-branch / parallel-in-branch / advanced job with inputs + retries + `jobSource`); validation parity with the engine (leaf-only parallels, required `jobRef`, A12 upstream-only refs, negative retries, same-path duplicate names — and *allowing* a name once per mutually-exclusive arm); and scoped-upstream visibility (incl. the engine's pass-merged-before-fail quirk).
- **No bundle change:** `canvasModel.ts` is not yet imported by a component (the canvas UI lands in WC-P2), so it tree-shakes out of the build. Frontend `tsc -b && vite build` green; **113 Vitest tests** pass.
- The workflow-update-2b plan — phase **WC-P1** of 9.

## 0.42.10 — Tags on Env Vars, Secrets & SSH Keys

**Date:** Jun 30, 2026

Operator-authored tags now extend to the three amadeus-owned Env Vars entities — **Variables**, **Secrets**, and **SSH key credentials** — bringing them to parity with the Scripts/Jobs/Schedules/Workflows catalogs. Each tab gains an inline tag column, a click-to-edit tag editor in the expanded row, and a "Tag" filter. Tags are free-form, SQLite-only metadata (schema **470**); for secrets and SSH credentials they are plaintext labels stored in their own column, entirely outside the AES-256-GCM envelope, so the encryption/reveal/rotate paths are untouched. Unlike the read-only Git catalogs (whose tag endpoints are open to any logged-in user), these writes carry the entity's own permission — `ManageEnvVars` for variables + secrets, `ConfigureApp` for credentials.

### Added

- Migration **470**: `tags TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'` on `env_vars`, `secrets`, and `ssh_credentials` (amadeus-owned, no Git-sync preservation needed).
- `tags` (writable, normalized) on the `EnvVar`, `EnvSecret`, and `SshCredential` API schemas; surfaced on the list/detail reads.
- Full-replace tag write endpoints `PUT /api/v1/env-var-tags/{envVarId}`, `/api/v1/env-secret-tags/{secretId}` (ManageEnvVars), and `/api/v1/ssh-credential-tags/{credentialId}` (ConfigureApp). Tags are normalized server-side (trim, drop blanks, case-insensitive de-dupe, ≤30 tags / ≤64 chars) — a violation is 422; a missing `tags` field is 422 (not a silent clear).
- Inline `InlineTags` column, expanded-row `TagEditor`, and `TagFilterSelect` on the Variables, Secrets, and SSH Keys tabs, with optimistic save (shared `useInlineTags` hook).
- Tests: migration 470 data round-trip (`TestMigrate470ConfigTagsRoundTrip`), and the three tag endpoints (`TestUpdateConfigTags`, `TestUpdateConfigTagsPermGate`).

**Date:** Jun 30, 2026

Scope creation/update now supports Ansible-formatted inventories directly during scope authoring in the UI and API (in addition to flat hosts lists). This includes inline validation for secret leakage, dynamic capability parsing, and automatic database projection table generation (groups, hosts, children, and variables) within an atomic database transaction.

### Added

- Support for `rawInventory` payload field on Scope creation and update APIs (`POST /api/v1/scopes`, `PUT /api/v1/scopes/{id}`).
- Segmented input mode control in `ScopeFormModal` (`Hosts List` vs `Ansible INI Inventory`).
- Inline error highlighting for raw inventory validation errors (e.g. secret leakage detection rejecting inline credentials).
- Automatic lazy loading of existing inventory content during scope editing.
- Automated integration/unit test suite `TestCreateScopeWithInventory` validating inventory creation, update, secret rejection, and flat hosts reversion.

### Fixed

- Resolved a SQLite `NOT NULL constraint failed: scopes.projection_status` regression during standard flat-host scope creation by ensuring `projection_status` defaults to `"ok"`.
- Gracefully handled inventory reversion where modifying an inventory-based scope back to flat hosts successfully clears all associated database projection tables.

  (`dangerouslySetInnerHTML`) under a scoped `guideCss()` stylesheet built from the

## 0.42.7 — SSH credentials: the name path is permanent (SK.17 reframe)

**Date:** Jun 30, 2026

The final SSH-credential milestone (SK.17 of the ssh-keys-update plan), resolved
as a **reframe, not a removal**. SK.17 originally proposed dropping the legacy
`auth_key_env_var` name path once the migration was proven — but that path is
**load-bearing and permanent**: runner-executed hosts resolve keys by NAME
*locally* (and never receive credential material), and inventory/git-imported hosts
name keys in their Ansible vars (re-imported on every sync). So nothing is dropped;
instead the misleading "legacy / deprecation" language is retired so a future
maintainer isn't lured into removing a required path.

### Changed

- The host/bastion **key picker** option is renamed from "Legacy: key by name…" to
  **"Key by name (runner / inventory)"** with accurate help text — it is a coequal
  mechanism, not a deprecated one.
- Reframed the "legacy / deprecation-window" wording in `loadSigner` (`conn.go`),
  `execspec.Target.AuthKeyEnvVar`, and the `460` migration comment to state that the
  two resolution mechanisms are **permanent** (credential for app-managed hosts;
  name for runner/inventory hosts). The plan-doc decisions (SK-D2/SK-D7), the SK.17
  milestone, and the ssh-update plan cross-reference were updated to match; the
  unbuilt "managed as SSH key" badge (SK-D7) is formally dropped.

No behavior, schema, or API change. **With this, the SSH key credentials feature
(SK.1–SK.17) is complete.**

## 0.42.4 — SSH credentials: log redaction of key material

**Date:** Jun 30, 2026

Closes a security gap in the SSH credential work (SK.14 of
the ssh-keys-update plan). A private key created **directly** as a credential
has no backing secret row, so before this it would never enter the log-redaction
dictionary — its material could echo into run logs (a script error, a misbehaving
command). This makes credential material masked exactly like a stored secret.

### Security

- **`secrets.RedactionValues` now also decrypts stored `ssh_credentials` material**
  into the redaction dictionary, reusing the same KEK cache and envelope path
  (best-effort: a missing table or undecryptable row is skipped, never failing
  redaction of the secrets above it). Both log-ingest paths inherit this for free —
  the in-app SSH executor and the runner both build their redactor through
  `runner.NewRedactor` → `secrets.RedactionValues`, and the redactor already splits
  multi-line PEM keys per line (PP-B4a), so a pasted key is masked line by line.

### Internal

- Test `TestRedactionValuesIncludesSshCredentials` guards the regression (a stored
  credential with no backing secret must appear in the dictionary).

## 0.42.2 — SSH credentials: API, OpenAPI contract & startup backfill

**Date:** Jun 30, 2026

Makes first-class SSH key credentials reachable over HTTP (SK.7–SK.9 of
the ssh-keys-update plan). The Env Vars UI for them is still pending
(SK.10–SK.11), but the full REST surface, the frozen-spec contract, and a one-time
migration off the legacy key-name references now exist.

### Added

- **REST API for SSH key credentials** (`ConfigureApp`-gated writes):
  `GET`/`POST /api/v1/ssh/credentials`, `GET`/`PUT`/`DELETE
  /api/v1/ssh/credentials/{credentialId}`, and `GET …/{credentialId}/usage`.
  Create/update **validate on save** and return derived metadata (key type, SHA256
  fingerprint, authorized_keys public line) but **never the private material**;
  `DELETE` returns **409 with the referencing hosts/bastions** unless `?force=true`
  (which clears the references first). `ssh_hosts`/`bastions` create + update now
  accept `authCredentialId`.
- **Startup backfill** (idempotent): migrates every host/bastion that still
  references a key by `auth_key_env_var` NAME to a first-class credential —
  resolving the material from the stored secret (or plaintext env var), sealing it,
  and repointing the row by FK. Original secrets are left in place as the dual-read
  fallback (SK-D7); names with no resolvable/parseable material stay on the name
  path and are counted. Non-fatal at startup.

### Changed

- **OpenAPI (both byte-identical copies):** new `SshCredential` /
  `SshCredentialInput` / `SshCredentialUsage` schemas, the six credential paths, a
  `credentialId` parameter, and `authCredentialId` on
  `SshHostInput`/`SshBastionInput`. Frontend TS client regenerated.

### Internal

- `sshkeys` validation sentinels (`ErrInvalidKey`, `ErrLabelRequired`,
  `ErrVaultRefRequired`, `ErrMaterialRequired`) + `IsValidationError`, so the API
  maps operator-input errors to 422 and internal failures to 500.
- Tests: backfill (migrate + idempotency + skip-unresolvable), credential API
  (create / 422 / material-not-returned / 409-guard / force delete).

## 0.42.1 — SSH credentials: service, validation & executor dual-read

**Date:** Jun 29, 2026

Builds on 0.42.0 with the credential service and executor wiring (SK.3–SK.6 of
the ssh-keys-update plan). Still no operator UI; what changes is that the SSH
executor now resolves a first-class credential when a host or bastion references
one, and the host/bastion CRUD round-trips the new reference.

### Added

- **`sshkeys` package — CRUD service for `ssh_credentials`.** `Create` /
  `List` / `Get` / `Update` (including in-place **key rotation** that preserves the
  id, so every host/bastion FK reference follows) / `Delete` (guarded — returns
  `ErrCredentialInUse` unless forced, and force orphans the referencing rows
  before deleting) / `Usage` (the reverse lookup the name-string model could not
  do). Stored keys are **validated on save**: `Parse` derives the key type, SHA256
  fingerprint, and authorized_keys public line, and **rejects passphrase-protected
  keys** with a clear error (the v1 boundary, SK-D8). Private material is sealed via
  the `secrets.Sealer` (0.42.0) and never returned.
- **Executor dual-read (`loadSigner`).** A host or bastion that references a
  credential by id resolves it first — fatal on failure, no silent fallthrough
  (PP-M7) — otherwise the legacy `auth_key_env_var` name path is used unchanged.
  `auth_credential_id` is threaded through `execspec.Target` and every resolver
  that feeds the executor (`HostByName`, the probe's `hostByID`/`bastionByID`, and
  `bastionAddr`), so both job execution and the **Test-connection** probe exercise
  the new path.
- **`ssh_hosts` / `bastions` CRUD** (`settings`) now read and write
  `auth_credential_id` alongside the retained `auth_key_env_var`.

### Internal

- `sshkeys.ResolveSigner` (free function, for the executor's `loadSigner`) and
  `Service.Resolve` (for callers holding a Service). Vault-source credential
  resolution returns a clear "Phase 2" error.
- Tests: key parsing (ed25519/rsa/ecdsa, garbage rejection, passphrase rejection),
  a stored round-trip (create → resolve → usage → guarded/force delete), and
  rotation-preserves-id.

## 0.42.0 — SSH credentials: schema & crypto foundation

**Date:** Jun 29, 2026

Groundwork for **first-class system SSH key credentials** — the typed entity that
replaces "an SSH key is an opaque secret referenced by name." This release lands
the schema and crypto foundation only (SK.1–SK.2 of the ssh-keys-update plan);
there is no API or UI yet, and existing key resolution is unchanged.

### Added

- **`ssh_credentials` table (migration `460`, schema → v460).** A typed home for
  the private keys Cronomicon uses for automated SSH: key material is envelope-
  encrypted with the **same** scheme as the `secrets` table
  (`ciphertext`/`nonce`/`wrapped_dek`/`kek_version`, so KEK rotation applies
  uniformly), with `key_type`/`fingerprint`/`public_key` columns reserved for
  derive-on-save validation and a `source` (`stored`|`vault`) mirroring the
  secrets model. New nullable `auth_credential_id` FK columns on `ssh_hosts` and
  `bastions` reference it by id — the basis for reverse lookup and rotation-by-
  reference — and coexist with the legacy `auth_key_env_var` name string for a
  later dual-read deprecation window. v1 reserves **no** passphrase/certificate
  columns (those are additive migrations if/when needed).

### Internal

- **`secrets.Sealer` — one column-based envelope-crypto implementation.** The
  KEK + AES-256-GCM scheme behind the `secrets` table is now a small exported
  helper (`Seal`/`Open` over the `ciphertext`/`nonce`/`wrapped_dek`/`kek_version`
  column layout). `createStored`, `Update`, and `Reveal` are routed through it,
  so there is a single code path the upcoming `ssh_credentials` store reuses
  rather than a second copy of the crypto. Behaviour and stored format are
  unchanged; the per-row `EncryptString`/`DecryptString` config-token path is
  untouched. Round-trip migration test `TestMigrate460RoundTrip`.
