## 0.41.4 — Timezone: the setting now governs scheduling AND display

**Date:** Jun 28, 2026

### Changed

- **The Timezone setting is real now — one application zone governs BOTH cron
  scheduling and UI display.** Previously Settings → General → **Timezone** was an
  inert stored string: cron actually fired in the container's OS zone (`time.Local`)
  and the SPA rendered every timestamp in each viewer's *browser* zone. Now a single
  effective app zone — the stored setting if set and loadable, else the host `TZ` —
  is the source of truth the scheduler evaluates cron in **and** the UI displays
  every timestamp in, so "2 a.m." means the same thing in the schedule editor, the
  Upcoming list, run History, and reality (the timezone-update plan). **No
  migration** — stored instants stay UTC RFC3339; only the evaluation/display zones
  change.
  - **Scheduling (M1).** One resolver `settings.ResolveEffectiveTimezone` computes
    the zone; the cron engine is constructed with `cron.WithLocation` and
    `cronutil.Next/NextN` take an explicit location, so next-run/upcoming compute in
    the **same** zone the engine fires in (no drift — principle "scheduling and
    display must agree"). **Editing the zone re-times every schedule**: the cron
    engine is rebuilt in the new zone (`RebuildWithLocation`), since robfig/cron fixes
    its location at construction. An invalid zone is rejected on save with **422**; an
    unloadable stored value degrades to the host zone with a logged warning and never
    wedges the scheduler (a failed reschedule still adopts the zone and self-heals via
    the backstop reload).
  - **Display (M2).** A shared `fmtInAppZone` formatter — sourced from the app zone
    fetched once at startup and refreshed on save — routes ~24 previously
    browser-local timestamp sites across the Dashboard, Jobs, Workflows, Schedules,
    Scripts, History, env-vars, runners, and settings views. The live cron preview is
    computed and rendered in the app zone (labelled "app zone"); relative formatters
    ("5m ago") stay zone-agnostic. The Settings banner is now informational ("times
    are shown in **{appTimezone}**") rather than a server-zone-mismatch warning.
  - **Self-contained binary.** `time/tzdata` is embedded so `America/…`-style zones
    resolve in slim containers lacking `/usr/share/zoneinfo` — no image `tzdata`
    package required. The resolved effective zone is logged once at startup.
  - `GET /settings/general` now returns a read-only `appTimezone` (the resolved,
    validated zone the SPA formats in). OpenAPI updated in both byte-identical copies;
    frontend types regenerated; embedded `backend/web/dist` rebuilt.
    `backend/deploy/env-matrix.md` documents the new `TZ`-as-fallback behavior.
    `make verify` (`go test ./...`) + `vitest` green.

## 0.41.3 — Agency-Based Runner Isolation — M4: Stuck-Run Visibility & Coverage

**Date:** Jun 27, 2026

### Added

- **Agency-based runner isolation — M4: stuck-run visibility + agency coverage.**
  The operational safety net for M3's hard isolation: now that dispatch is gated, a job bound
  to an agency with no online runner waits **silently** — M4 makes that visible. No migration
  (schema stays **v450**); **warn-only** (a stranded run keeps waiting rather than auto-failing,
  per OD-A8).
  - **One resolver** `execspec.AgencyHasOnlineRunner` mirrors the disjoint claim matrix: a named
    agency needs an online member; the general pool needs an online untagged runner. It backs
    both surfaces below.
  - **Per-agency coverage**: `GET /agencies` now reports `onlineRunnerCount`, and the Agencies
    tab shows an **Online runners** column that flags `0 → jobs will wait`.
  - **Read-time stuck-run signal**: a queued runner run whose agency has no eligible online
    runner surfaces a `statusReason` ("Waiting: no online runner in agency 'X'") on the run
    list / detail API — computed at read time, so it always reflects current fleet state (no
    stale enqueue-time write, no background sweep).
  - **Enqueue advisory**: the scheduler logs a warning when a scheduled run targets an agency
    with no online runner (the automated path where no operator is watching).
  - OpenAPI updated in both byte-identical copies (`Agency.onlineRunnerCount`); frontend types
    regenerated; embedded `backend/web/dist` rebuilt. `go test ./...` / `make verify` + `vitest`
    green.

## 0.41.2 — Agency-Based Runner Isolation — M3: Hard-Isolation Dispatch (Live)

**Date:** Jun 27, 2026

### Changed

- **Agency-based runner isolation — M3: hard-isolation dispatch is LIVE.**
  The keystone of the agency-support plan: a job now dispatches **only to a runner that can
  reach its network**. The effective scope's agency is snapshotted onto the run at enqueue and
  matched against runner membership when a runner claims work. Schema **v450**.
  - **Migration `450_runs_agency`** adds `runs.agency` — a denormalized agency-**NAME** snapshot
    (no FK), mirroring `runs.scope` and the per-run reproducibility-snapshot discipline; frozen
    at enqueue, immutable. Down is data-present round-trip tested.
  - **One resolver** (`execspec.ScopeAgency`) maps a scope to its agency name; the snapshot is
    written across **all three enqueue paths** — the scheduler, manual runs, and workflow child
    runs.
  - **The `claimRun` filter** (the single dispatch choke point) now enforces the **disjoint
    matrix** (OD-A1): a tagged run is claimed only by a runner in that agency; an **untagged run
    only by a runner with no agencies** (the general pool). **Backward-compatible** — with no
    agencies defined every run is untagged and dispatch is unchanged (existing claim tests pass
    verbatim).
  - Runs surface their `agency` on the run list / detail API for observability.
  - The behavior change is **gated by configuration**: isolation activates only once an operator
    binds a scope (M1) and assigns runners (M2). `go test ./...` + `make verify` green.

### Notes

- Stuck-run visibility (a run tagged for an agency with no online runner) is the next milestone
  (M4). Until then such a run waits in `queued`, exactly as it would for an unsatisfied capability.

## 0.41.0 — Agency-Based Runner Isolation — M1: Agency Catalog + Scope Binding

**Date:** Jun 27, 2026

### Added

- **Agency-based runner isolation — M1: agency catalog + scope binding (foundation).**
  First slice of the agency-support plan. Introduces **agencies** — operator-managed
  network-isolation zones — as a first-class catalog, and lets a scope be bound to the one
  agency its hosts live in. **Additive and inert: no dispatch behavior changes yet** (runner
  membership lands in M2; hard-isolation dispatch in M3).
  - **Schema v430.** Migration `420_agencies` adds the `agencies` catalog table (operator
    registry, `name` UNIQUE). Migration `430_scopes_agency` adds `scopes.agency_id` (declarative
    FK) — **operator-owned and never synced**: GitLab `upsertScopes` does not write it, so an
    operator's binding survives re-sync (the operator-owned model used for tags). Both downs are
    data-present round-trip tested (`TestMigrate430RoundTrip`).
  - **Catalog CRUD** (`/agencies`, ConfigureApp-gated): create / rename / delete, with a
    duplicate-name 409 and an `agency_in_use` 409 that blocks deleting an agency a scope still
    references. Agencies are **operator-governed, never self-declared by a runner**.
  - **Scope binding** via `PUT /scopes/{scopeId}/agency` — an operator overlay valid for both
    git- and amadeus-source scopes (`unknown_agency` 422 on an unknown id). The `Scope`
    serializer surfaces the bound `agency` (`{id,name}`).
  - **UI:** a new **Agencies** tab on the Env Vars page (catalog management) and a per-scope
    **Agency** selector in the Scopes tab's expanded row. Demo seed adds two agencies with two
    scopes bound.
  - OpenAPI updated in both byte-identical copies (`Agency`/`AgencyInput`, the agency paths,
    `Scope.agency`); frontend types regenerated; embedded `backend/web/dist` rebuilt.
    `go test ./...`, `tsc -b && vite build`, and `vitest` green.

## 0.40.0 — Ansible Inventory Support (M1–M5): Honor, Project, Target, Import & Author

**Date:** Jun 26, 2026

Delivers **Ansible inventory support end-to-end** across five milestones (M1–M5),
implementing the plan in the ansible-inventory plan. An `inventory/*.ini` — whether
**git-synced** or **authored in-app** — is now: honored at execution
(`ansible-playbook -i`, M1); parsed into an **advisory** group / host-vars projection
surfaced read-only in the UI (M2); targetable by **group** and a raw `--limit`
passthrough (M3); **imported into `ssh_hosts`** so the in-app SSH executor dials
inventory hosts with zero operator action, with amadeus-overlay precedence (M4); and
**authorable in-app** without git, including operator-initiated host import (M5). Inline
secret **values** are rejected fail-closed at ingest throughout (env-var-NAME indirection
is the supported remediation); the raw inventory always ships to `ansible` unchanged, and
the projection is never authoritative for execution. Runner manifest **protocol v1 → v2**;
schema **v340 → v410** (migrations 350 / 360 / 370 / 390 / 400 / 410).

### Added

- **Ansible inventory support — M5: in-app inventory authoring (feature now end-to-end).**
  Operators can author/upload an inventory for an **amadeus-source** scope without git.
  - `PUT /scopes/{id}/inventory` validates + parses through the SAME pipeline git
    sync uses (`inventory.ValidateSecrets` / `ParseProjection` / `WriteProjectionTables`
    / `InferTypes`, now shared so authored and synced inventories behave identically):
    secret-bearing vars are rejected (422 `inventory_secret_rejected`, line-numbered;
    the scope is left unchanged), the advisory projection + `scope_hosts` membership
    are replaced, and run-type capability is inferred (unioned into `supportedTypes`).
    Git scopes are read-only here (409); only `ini` is supported.
  - `POST /scopes/{id}/inventory/import-hosts` (the cap-C completion deferred from M4)
    materializes the parsed hosts into `ssh_hosts` (`source=amadeus`, `scope_id`) for
    the in-app SSH executor — keyed by `(scope_id, hostname)` with an `overwrite` flag,
    returning created/updated/skipped.
  - **UI:** the Env Vars › Scopes expanded row gains an inventory editor + file upload
    - “Import hosts → SSH” for amadeus scopes, surfacing line-numbered secret rejections.
    Scope creation no longer requires a host (an inventory scope can start empty).
  - **Precedence/safety (review fixes):** `HostByName` now scope-qualifies imported
    rows so a job in scope A can't dial scope B's same-named host (a global operator
    overlay still wins); a partial unique index (migration `410`) enforces the import
    key. Git sync now **refuses to clobber** an operator-authored (amadeus) scope of
    the same name (OD-1, both directions). A degraded authored inventory keeps its
    full host membership (no truncation). Schema **v410**.
- **Ansible inventory support — M4: import inventory hosts → `ssh_hosts` + precedence.**
  Git inventory hosts are imported into `ssh_hosts` on sync (`source='git'`,
  migration `400_ssh_hosts_source`), so the **in-app SSH executor dials inventory
  hosts with zero operator action**. `ansible_host`/`ansible_port`/`ansible_user` map
  to `address`/`port`/`username`; the auth-key NAME comes from a per-host
  `amadeus_auth_key_env_var` (host/group var) or a per-scope sidecar
  `spec.authKeyEnvVar` — NAMES only, never secret values (D1).
  - **Precedence (D4):** when a hostname has both an imported (git) row and an
    operator (amadeus) overlay, the **amadeus row wins**, resolved in one place
    (`execspec.HostByName`, amadeus-first). The TOFU host-key capture is now
    **id-qualified** to the exact resolved row (was an unbounded `WHERE hostname`),
    and the sync upsert leaves `host_key`/`status` untouched so a captured key
    survives re-sync.
  - Imported rows are **read-only** in Settings → SSH Targets (a `git` badge);
    operator edits/deletes are rejected (author an Cronomicon host to override). Stale
    imported rows are pruned by owner on sync; operator rows are never touched.
  - **Trust note (decision ratified):** import lets a git inventory choose a host's
    dial address AND the NAME of the key Cronomicon authenticates with (no secret value
    crosses, D1). That is an expansion of the GitOps repo's trust scope. Decision:
    **allow global key NAMEs, with visibility** — bindings are surfaced (a sync log
    line + the read-only SSH Targets rows) for operator review. Tighter controls
    (restricting git rows to scope-bound keys, or an operator allowlist of bindable
    NAMEs) are available to revisit if the threat model tightens.
  - `SshHost.source` added to the API. Schema **v400**. (The operator-initiated
    `import-hosts` endpoint + UI is deferred to M5, where it serves in-app-authored
    inventories — git scopes import automatically here.)
- **Ansible inventory support — M3: group / `--limit` targeting.**
  A run can now target inventory **groups** (not just individual hosts). One
  resolver — `execspec.ResolveRun(scope, hosts, groups)` — expands group members
  for the SSH executor AND passes the group NAMES to the runner as
  `ansible --limit`, so both executors target the identical set (no drift). Group
  and host names are charset-validated (`AnsibleLimit` refuses any name with an
  ansible `--limit` metacharacter). New trigger fields on `POST /jobs/{id}/run`:
  - `targetGroups[]` — validated at the boundary (422 `group_membership` for an
    unknown group or a `scope==""`; **all** group targeting is rejected when the
    scope's projection is `unavailable`, since SSH can't enumerate members of an
    unparsed inventory); unions with `targetHosts`.
  - `ansibleLimit` — a raw `--limit` passthrough for patterns the projection can't
    model; **ansible/runner only** (422 `invalid_executor` on the SSH executor).
  `Scope.groups` (NAME + member count, session-level — names aren't sensitive)
  feeds the run dialog's new group selector + advanced `--limit` field. OpenAPI
  both copies; types regenerated; dist rebuilt.
- **Ansible inventory support — M2: advisory parsed projection + inventory view.**
  Builds on M1. A synced `inventory/*.ini` is now parsed into an **advisory**
  projection — groups, `[group:children]`, `[group:vars]`, and inline host_vars —
  persisted in new normalized tables (migrations `360_scope_groups`,
  `370_scope_host_group_vars`). The parser (`internal/inventory.ParseProjection`)
  supports a documented static-INI subset and **degrades loudly**: on the first
  out-of-subset construct (host ranges, unterminated quotes, bare flags, unknown
  section suffixes, or a name with an `ansible --limit` metacharacter) it stops,
  records `projection_status='unavailable'` + reason/line, and discards the
  half-parsed tree — the raw inventory still ships to ansible unchanged. The
  projection is never authoritative for execution.
  - **New `GET /scopes/{id}/inventory`** (ConfigureApp-gated) returns the inventory
    document (advisory projection, parse status/reason/line; raw for amadeus-source
    scopes only). `Scope` gained `hasInventory`/`inventoryFormat`/`projectionStatus`.
  - **UI:** the Env Vars › Scopes expanded row now shows the parsed group tree and
    host_vars with an "advisory — not authoritative" badge and a loud "preview
    unavailable — raw still ships to `ansible -i`" state.
  - `internal/inventory.Hosts` is now the single host-membership implementation
    (gitlab's `parseInventoryHosts` delegates to it). OpenAPI updated in both
    copies; frontend types regenerated.
- **Ansible inventory support — M1: honor inventory at execution (`ansible-playbook -i`).**
  First slice of the plan in the ansible-inventory plan. A git-synced
  `inventory/*.ini` is now persisted byte-exact (migration `350_scope_inventory_raw`,
  `scopes.raw_inventory`) and shipped to an **amadeus-mode** runner on the manifest
  (`ManifestResponse.inventory`, protocol **v2**), which writes it to a `0600` temp
  file and runs `ansible-playbook -i`. Previously an ansible runner manifest errored
  in `execspec.ResolveCommand` (ansible/terraform now resolve, shipping the body with
  no server-side interpreter).
  - **Path A secret rejection (D1, fail-closed).** New `internal/inventory.ValidateSecrets`
    rejects inventory carrying inline secret VALUES (a narrow explicit reject-set:
    `ansible_ssh_pass`/`*_become_pass`/`*_sudo_pass`/`*_su_pass`/… + inline-vault markers)
    at INGEST — the scope is skipped, so no secret value is ever persisted or shipped.
    The allowed remediation is env-var-NAME indirection (`{{ lookup('env','NAME') }}`)
    the runner resolves locally; the manifest path never carries a decrypted secret.
  - **Back-compat + no-leak gates.** Each runner's `protocol_version` is persisted
    (migration `390_runners_protocol_version`); an amadeus ansible run that needs a
    managed inventory **hard-fails** (409) on a `< 2` agent or on a scope with no
    inventory rather than running unscoped. **Local-mode** runners are never shipped
    an inventory (no-leak), enforced server-side and again agent-side.
  - OpenAPI updated in both spec copies (`ManifestResponse.inventory`/`limit`,
    `ManifestInventory`); frontend types regenerated. Schema **v390**.

## 0.39.2 — Secrets: description field now persists

**Date:** Jun 26, 2026

Fixes a bug where a Secret's **Description** entered in the Env Vars › Secrets "New
Secret" / "Edit Secret" form was silently dropped — it never saved and always read
back blank ("—"). The OpenAPI `EnvSecret`/`EnvSecretInput` schemas and the SPA form
both carried `description`, and the API handler passed it into `secrets.CreateInput`,
but the `secrets` table had no `description` column and `secrets.Service` never wrote
or read one (the column was discarded with `_ = desc`). This is the identical defect
migration `100` fixed for **env_vars** — Secrets were missed. Backend-only; the
frontend already sent and rendered the field correctly. Full backend suite green.

### Fixed

- **`secrets.description` now round-trips (migration `340_secrets_description`, schema
  v340).** Adds the missing `description TEXT` column to the `secrets` table and threads
  it through `secrets.Service` — `List`/`Get` now `SELECT` and scan it, and
  `createStored`/`createVault`/`Update` now persist it. Removed the stale
  `_ = desc // description column not in base table` discard. Demo seed now gives each
  seeded secret a description for parity with seeded env vars. New
  `TestSecretDescriptionRoundTrips` covers create → read-back → list → update.

## 0.39.0 — Job Composer Update 3: searchable Script/Scope pickers, unified Schedule section

**Date:** Jun 25, 2026

Implements the jobs-composer-update-3 plan (decisions **JC17–JC25**): the Job
Composer's Script and Scope fields become searchable, keyboard-navigable comboboxes on a
shared base, and the two schedule sections merge into one. **Frontend-only — no backend /

build` and `vitest run` (52 tests) green.

- **`SearchSelect` — a shared, accessible combobox base (JC24/JC25).** Type-to-filter;

  `aria-activedescendant`; click-outside to close; optional folder grouping and a

- **Searchable Script picker (JC17–JC19).** Replaces the flat `<select>` with a

- **Dangling-script soft warning.** A job whose referenced script was deleted shows a

### Fixed

## 0.38.0 — User-Defined Run Variables (Ad-Hoc Prompts)

**Date:** Jun 25, 2026

Implements the user-defined-vars plan: a Job can **declare prompt variables**
(name, label, required, default, options) that surface as **fillable fields in the
ad-hoc Run dialog**. Answers ride the existing per-run **env override** path (UDV2) —
merged into `runs.env_json` via `internal/envmerge` — so the run lifecycle is
unchanged. Decisions **UDV1–UDV8** (see the plan).

- **Schema v330** — migration `330_job_prompts` adds `jobs.prompts_json TEXT NOT NULL
  DEFAULT '[]'` (mirrors `env_json`/`scripts.variables`). Dual-source (A9): read-only
  for git jobs (parsed from `spec.prompts` at sync), writable for amadeus jobs (the
  Composer). Additive; advisory — a malformed/empty list never blocks a sync.
- **Declared, not inferred (UDV1/UDV5)** — the heuristic script-variable highlighter is
  **demoted, not deleted**: removed from the run path (its false-positives / misses /

  422); the unfilled name is recorded in the run's `override_json` under `promptWarnings`

  pre-filled and auto-submitted, UDV8); the inferred panel is gone from the run path.

## 0.37.1 — Paged Catalogs (Jobs · Scripts · Upcoming) + Upcoming Column Table

**Date:** Jun 23, 2026

Implements the pagination plan: a **paged view** (default **25** rows; a
**25 / 50 / 100** selector) on **Jobs**, **Scripts**, and **Schedules › Upcoming**,
plus a redesign of **Upcoming** from a grouped row list into a defined-column
**table** matching the Jobs/Scripts/Inventory catalogs. Wiring pagination also
**fixes a latent Jobs truncation bug** — the list fetched `/jobs` with no page
params and rendered only the server-default first **50** jobs by name, leaving the
rest unreachable. Frontend-only; embedded `backend/web/dist` rebuilt.
`tsc -b && vite build` and `vitest run` green.

### Added

- **`useClientPager(items)` + a pure pager core (`utils/pager.ts`).** A client-side
  analogue of the server `paged()` path: it owns a `usePager()`, re-clamps the stored
  page against the current length each render (a shrinking set never strands the user
  on an empty trailing page), and slices the window. The pure math — `clampPage`,
  `sliceForPage`, `pagerLabel` — lives in `utils/pager.ts` with `utils/pager.test.ts`
  coverage (no DOM needed), mirroring the `utils/tree.ts` house style.
- **Pagination on three catalogs** (flat/search mode), each over the already-resident,
  already-filtered set so status tabs, type/tag filters, search, and the folder tree
  keep operating on the full set: **Jobs** (`Jobs.tsx`), **Scripts** (`Scripts.tsx`),
  and **Schedules › Upcoming** (`UpcomingTab.tsx`). Browse-mode folder trees stay
  un-paged (one folder level at a time). An honest "first N" banner/caption appears
  when a catalog exceeds its resident cap (Jobs 200, Upcoming 500).
- **Schedules › Upcoming column table.** A flat, soonest-first `<table>` (When · Type ·
  Owner · Schedule · Cron) with resizable columns (`useColumnWidths("schedule-upcoming")`),
  mirroring `InventoryTab`; the day-header grouping is dropped (the When column carries
  the full date+time). All colour tokens are applied inline at render (theme-toggle safe).

### Changed

- **Pager relocated to the canonical UI kit.** `usePager` / `Pager` / `clampPage` /
  `PagerState` moved from `views/history/shared.tsx` into `components/ui.tsx` (the
  page-size control gained `role="group"` / `aria-label` / `aria-pressed`);
  `shared.tsx` re-exports them as a back-compat shim, so the five existing consumers
  (the History and Workflow-runs tables) compile unchanged.
- **Jobs fetches the full small catalog** (`pageSize=200`, the server max) instead of
  the default 50, then pages it client-side.
- **Version of record** (`backend/cmd/amadeus/main.go`) bumped to `0.37.1`.

### Fixed

- **Jobs no longer silently truncates at 50.** Jobs past the first server page were
  unreachable (no Next control); the list now loads the whole catalog and pages it.

### Notes

- **Client-side, not server-side, by design.** Although `/jobs` and `/scripts` already
  paginate server-side, the backend derives a job's **status after `LIMIT/OFFSET`** (it
  is not a SQL column), so server-paging the status-tab list would return sparse,
  miscounted pages. Paging the resident set client-side keeps the status tabs, filters,
  and folder tree correct; the catalogs are small (sync-derived), so the resident caps
  are effectively the whole catalog. The optional backend Upcoming paging (plan T10) was
  not taken.

## 0.37.0 — Go-Live Stabilization: Production-Review Medium & Low Findings

**Date:** Jun 23, 2026

Closes the remaining 🟡 Medium (PP-M1, M3–M5, M7–M9) and ⚪ Low/Hardening
(PP-L2–L5, L7, L8, L10, L12, L14, L16) findings from the go-live production
audit (the 2026-06-23 production review) — the Blocker (PP-B*) and High
(PP-H*) batches having already shipped in 0.23.1 / 0.24.0. A DoS-hardening,
security, reliability, and operations pass with no new product surface. Schema
**290 → 320** (three reversible migrations). Backend-only except the PP-M9
settings/job-composer cleanup; OpenAPI + TS client regenerated and embedded
`backend/web/dist` rebuilt.

### Security

- **PP-M1 — Request bodies are capped at 2 MiB.** Write routes decoded bodies with
  no size limit (~145 `json.NewDecoder` sites), so a multi-gigabyte `POST` could
  OOM the single-process backend. A new `limitBody` middleware (innermost in
  `withBaseMiddleware`) wraps `r.Body` in `http.MaxBytesReader` at 2 MiB for
  `POST`/`PUT`/`PATCH`; the chunked runner log-ingest route is exempt
  (`isStreamingIngest`) and long-poll is a body-less GET. The
  `ReadHeaderTimeout`/`IdleTimeout` half was already in place.
  (`backend/internal/api/middleware.go`; `TestRequestBodySizeLimit`)
- **PP-L2 — Kill-run enforces scope access.** `killJob` gained the `AllowedScopes`
  guard already on `runJob`/workflow-trigger, so run / kill / workflow-trigger all
  reject (403) a caller whose scopes don't cover the target.
  (`backend/internal/api/execution_mount.go`)
- **PP-L3 — Integration credentials are redacted in runner logs.** `RedactionValues`
  now also decrypts `gitlab_config.pat_enc`, `notification_config.smtp_password_enc`,
  and `vault_config.secret_id_enc` into the redaction dictionary (best-effort).
  (`backend/internal/secrets/service.go`)
- **PP-L7 / PP-L10 — Constant-time secret comparison.** The runner bootstrap token
  (`runner/token.go`) and GitLab webhook secret (`gitlab/sync.go`) now use
  `subtle.ConstantTimeCompare`, closing timing side-channels.
- **PP-L14 — 500 responses no longer leak DB internals.** A shared `httpx.Fail500`
  logs the real error server-side and returns a generic envelope; raw SQLite/driver
  strings no longer reach clients. (`backend/internal/httpx/respond.go`)
- **PP-L16 — SMTP refuses cleartext fallback.** The STARTTLS notify client requires
  the server to advertise STARTTLS and hard-errors rather than authenticating over
  plaintext. (`backend/internal/notify/smtp.go`)
- **PP-L4 — Unreadable KEK file is fatal.** A configured-but-unreadable KEK file is
  now a hard startup error instead of silently falling through to the env KEK (which
  would wrap new secrets under a different key). (`backend/internal/secrets/kek.go`)

### Fixed

- **PP-M8 — Log-stream resume no longer corrupts on reconnect.** The agent tracked
  raw transmitted bytes while the server validated `X-Resume-Offset` against the
  *redacted* file size; any redacted secret diverged the two, causing spurious 409s
  and truncated/duplicated logs. The server now tracks a raw (pre-redaction) byte
  count (`runs.log_raw_offset`, migration 310), persisted only on clean EOF, and
  opens the log with `TRUNC` when the offset is 0. No agent change.
  (`backend/internal/runner/log.go`)
- **PP-L8 — `Forbid` concurrency no longer double-runs under a race.** The
  read-then-insert check had no DB constraint. Migration 300 adds a partial unique
  index `uq_runs_active_concurrency` on `runs(concurrency_key)` for queued/running
  rows; only Forbid runs set the key, and both `scheduler.fire()` and `runJob` map
  the violation to a graceful 409. (`backend/internal/scheduler/scheduler.go`)
- **PP-M7 — SSH key-load errors are no longer swallowed.** `loadSigner` treats a
  `Reveal` error on a *matching* stored-secret row as fatal instead of falling
  through to the env-var path and masking it as "no key material found".
  (`backend/internal/sshexec/conn.go`)
- **PP-M3 — Readiness probe verifies DB writability.** `ReadyCheck` runs a write
  probe (`INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` on a `settings` sentinel) and fails with
  "db not writable", so a full/read-only/locked volume no longer reports `ready`.
  (`backend/internal/db/migrate.go`)

### Added

- **PP-M4 — S3 backup uploads retry and alert.** The uploader retries with
  exponential backoff and dispatches a `notify` alert on persistent failure instead
  of silently logging one failed `FPutObject`. (`backend/internal/backup/s3.go`)
- **PP-M5 / PP-L12 — Retention sweep prunes local backups and the action queue.**
  The daily sweep removes `amadeus-YYYYMMDD.db` snapshots older than 7 days
  (previously unbounded on the live volume) and prunes consumed `action_queue` rows
  older than 7 days. (`backend/internal/db/retention.go`)
- **PP-L5 — Seamless KEK rotation (`AMADEUS_SECRET_KEK_VERSION`).** The active KEK
  version (default 1) is written into each secret's `kek_version` (was hardcoded),
  and reads decrypt each row with its matching key via `loadKEKForVersion` (historical
  keys from `AMADEUS_SECRET_KEK_<N>` / `_FILE`). Config-blob tokens gained a
  self-describing `v2:<version>:…` format (legacy `v1:` ⇒ version 1). Zero-downtime
  rotation procedure documented in `backend/deploy/env-matrix.md`.
- **Operator deployment guide** (`backend/deploy/deployment-guide.md`) — end-to-end
  go-live runbook landed alongside the hardening pass.

### Changed

- **Internal API error logging standardized on `httpx.Fail500`** across the access,
  execution, compose (job/schedule/workflow), scripts, and settings mounts — one
  log-server-side / return-generic path instead of ad-hoc 500s (PP-L14).

### Removed

- **PP-M9 — The dead `sensitiveLogging` toggle is gone.** Redaction in
  `runner/redact.go` was always unconditional and the agent never read the
  manifest's `SensitiveLogging`, so the global settings toggle and per-job field
  changed nothing. Removed end-to-end across settings, job compose/detail, runner
  proto+manifest, GitLab sync/YAML, seed, and the frontend; OpenAPI regenerated
  (both byte-identical copies) and the TS client + embedded SPA rebuilt. Migration
  320 drops `jobs.sensitive_logging` (reversible; data-roundtrip tested). The lenient
  GitLab YAML parser silently ignores a leftover `sensitive_logging:` key rather than
  erroring; `redact.go` now documents redaction as unconditional.

### Database

- Migration **300** (`300_runs_forbid_unique`) — partial unique index for the
  `Forbid` concurrency guard (PP-L8).

## 0.36.2 — Operator-Owned Tags, Phase 2: Serializers & Write Endpoints

**Date:** Jun 20, 2026

Second phase of the tags-support plan: the read serializers now surface the
new `tags` columns, and three new write endpoints let any logged-in user author

### Added

- **`PUT /api/v1/job-tags/{jobId}`** (`updateJobTags`) — full-replace a job's tag
  set, addressed by integer rowid (source-agnostic). 404 if the row is gone; 422

  for workflows, keyed by rowid. (`execution_mount.go`)
- **`PUT /api/v1/schedule-tags/{name}`** (`updateScheduleTags`) — keyed by
  `(source, name)` with `?source` defaulting to `git` (a git and an amadeus
  schedule can share a name); returns the updated schedule with its `usedBy`

  schedule-defs catalog, so it adds the session + CSRF chain there.

## 0.35.0 — Workflow Builder Phase 4: Engine Power In-App

**Date:** Jun 19, 2026

The Workflow Editor now authors the engine's full step model, and the engine gains retry, soft-cancel, and a stable run→definition link (the workflow-builder-update plan Phase 4; decisions D2/D3/D4). Schema **270**.

- **Branch & parallel authoring (WB-E2, one level — D2):** editor step rows gain a Job / Parallel group / Branch selector. Parallel is a multi-job list; Branch is a condition form (job to check, `job_status` / `output_match` with operator + value) plus pass/fail arm lists. The assembled graph renders live in the same `StepChain` the list and run views use; graphs nested deeper than one level stay read-only (the recursive editor is V2).
- **Per-step inputs & retry authoring (WB-E3 / WB-R1):** a job step's Advanced expander declares A12 inputs (`ENV_KEY ← {upstream step, output}`, the upstream step picked from a dropdown), an optional label, and per-step retry / backoff / continue-on-error overrides.
- **Retry + continue-on-error (WB-R1 — D3):** on a failed step the engine re-dispatches a fresh child run up to N times with a cancellable backoff (each attempt its own timeline row), then continue-on-error skips-and-proceeds instead of halting. Config resolves as **step value ?? job default**; migration **250** adds `jobs.backoff_seconds` + `continue_on_error` (job-level retries already existed), surfaced in the Job Composer and the compose/read API. (Honoring retry on standalone, non-workflow runs is deferred — a deeper run-lifecycle change.)
- **Soft-cancel (WB-S2 — D4):** a new `POST /workflows/runs/{traceId}/cancel` stops further dispatch, marks not-started children `skipped`, lets in-flight children finish, and ends the run `cancelled`; a Cancel button appears on running runs. Migration **260** records cancellation as an additive flag (the run-status CHECK can't gain a value without rebuilding `workflow_runs` under the live `runs` FK), surfaced as a display-only `cancelled` status; the walk also honors the persisted flag so cancel works for scheduler-driven runs.
- **Stable run linkage (WB-D2):** migration **270** indexes `workflow_runs(workflow_source, workflow_name)`; "runs for workflow X" now filters by that stable identity instead of the reusable rowid, so renames/recreates no longer strand or mis-attribute runs.
- **Contract:** additive `WorkflowStep.retries/backoffSeconds/continueOnError`, `Job`/`JobComposeInput.backoffSeconds/continueOnError`, `WorkflowRun.cancelled`, a `cancelled` `RunStatus`, the cancel route, and `workflowName`/`workflowSource` run-list filters on both byte-identical `openapi.yaml` copies.

Tests: engine retry-succeeds, continue-on-error, and cancel-stops-dispatch (exercising the `ctx.Done()` path); the cancel HTTP endpoint; migrations up/down (schema **240→270**). `go test ./...` green; `tsc -b && vite build` green; embedded `backend/web/dist` rebuilt.

## 0.34.0 — Workflow Builder Phase 3: Run Observability

**Date:** Jun 19, 2026

Workflow runs become debuggable: every run captures the graph it ran, the run detail reconstructs that graph with live status, and each step drills into its redacted context and log (the workflow-builder-update plan Phase 3; decision D5). Schema **240**.

- **Per-run step-graph snapshot (WB-D1):** migration **240** adds `workflow_runs.steps_snapshot` + `steps_hash`; the engine captures the step graph (with its minted node ids) and a sha256 at trigger time, mirroring the per-run `script_ref`/`content_hash` reproducibility pattern — so History can render a past run's structure even after the definition is edited.
- **Real step types + run graph (WB-O3):** the run-detail serializer reconstructs the executed graph from the snapshot, merging each node's live status/duration by node id (parallel groups, branch arms, untaken arms shown skipped), rendered with the shared `StepChain`. Flat-timeline rows now carry their real `stepType` (job / parallel / branch), and "steps starting" reads distinctly from "no steps".
- **Per-step logs + redacted context (WB-O1 / WB-O4 — D5):** each step exposes a resolved-context snapshot (resolved env + captured A12 outputs, run through the existing redactor) and an inline job-run log — the step's id *is* its child-run trace id, so the log reuses `GET /runs/{id}/log` with no new endpoint. The log viewer is extracted into a shared `RunLog` component (also adopted by the Executions drill-in) to avoid drift.
- **Unified run surfaces (WB-O5):** a shared `WorkflowRunsTable` + `WorkflowRunDetail` back both the Workflows page and the History tab; both now page server-side **and** offer step-level drill-down — one component, no drift.
- **Contract:** additive read-only `WorkflowRunDetail.graph`, a `WorkflowRunGraphStep` schema, and a widened `WorkflowRunStep.stepType` enum on both byte-identical `openapi.yaml` copies.

Tests: engine snapshot capture; run-detail graph / real-stepType / redacted-context; migration **240** up/down (schema **230→240**). `go test ./...` green; `tsc -b && vite build` green; embedded `backend/web/dist` rebuilt.

## 0.33.0 — Workflow Builder Phase 2: Editor Parity

**Date:** Jun 19, 2026

The Workflow Editor becomes the third complete in-app authoring surface alongside the Job Composer and Schedule Builder — editable, deletable, validated, and previewed (the workflow-builder-update plan Phase 2). No migration (schema stays **230**).

- **Edit + delete (WB-E1):** the editor reads `?id=` to load an existing amadeus workflow, re-saves via PUT (full-replace, preserving per-step labels, A12 inputs, and inline schedules), and deletes behind a confirm with a redirect toast — mirroring the Job Composer pattern. A row-level Edit action appears on amadeus workflows; git-source workflows (and, later, deeply-nested graphs) show a read-only notice rather than silently flattening.

## 0.32.0 — Workflow Builder Phase 1: Correctness & Live Runs

**Date:** Jun 19, 2026

Correctness, security, and live-run quick wins that de-risk the workflow engine ahead of the editor and observability work (the workflow-builder-update plan Phase 1; decision D1). No migration (schema stays **230**).

- **Trigger authorization (WB-S1 — D1):** the workflow trigger now enforces scope-access and the global concurrency cap over **every** constituent job (via a new `Engine.JobScopes`), mirroring the per-job `runJob` guards — closing a hole where any authenticated user could trigger any non-disabled workflow regardless of its jobs' scopes.
- **Bounded parallel fan-out (WB-S4):** a parallel step's goroutines are gated by a semaphore sized to the global concurrency cap (`settings.maxConcurrent`), replacing the unbounded goroutine-per-job.
- **Real run durations (WB-S3):** the persisted `workflow_runs.duration_ms` is now serialized in the run-list and run-detail responses (was hardcoded null), so Duration columns populate.
- **Live run polling (WB-O2):** a new `useLiveGet` hook silently re-polls the workflow list, runs panel, run-step timeline, and History runs tab while any run is running/queued, stopping once everything is terminal.

Tests: a `TestWorkflowTriggerScopeGuard` regression for the trigger authz. `go test ./...` green; embedded `backend/web/dist` rebuilt.

## 0.31.0 — Script Variable Scanning

**Date:** Jun 19, 2026

Scripts are now scanned at sync time for the **environment variables they reference**, so an operator can see **what to define** before a run — closing the gap where the Run dialog and Job Composer asked for env vars with no hint of which ones a script actually needs (the scope's Env Vars are not auto-injected — Q-JC13). Mirrors the v0.26.x body-lint precedent: the same single read of each body at sync, persisted as advisory metadata, surfaced read-only on the Script API.

- **Sync-time extraction:** migration **230** adds `scripts.variables`; the sync engine extracts each body's referenced env vars (`ExtractScriptVariables`) alongside the existing content-hash + lint scan, from the same bytes. Advisory only — extraction never blocks a sync, drops a script, or enters `content_hash` (Decision 8).
- **Shell-family aware, extensible:** a per-run-type extractor registry handles **bash/sh** (`$VAR`, `${VAR:-default}`), **perl** (`$ENV{VAR}`), and **powershell** (`$env:VAR`). It subtracts variables the script assigns itself (`NAME=`, `export`, `local`, `read`, `for`), shell special/positional params (`$1`, `$?`, …) and ambient vars (`$HOME`, `$PATH`, `LC_*`, `BASH_*`), and reads `${VAR:-x}` / `${VAR:=x}` defaults (⇒ optional). **Ansible/Terraform** are recognized but not yet analyzed (return none, shown as such) — they slot into the registry later.
- **Three surfaces, one parser:** a shared `ScriptVariablesPanel` renders the variables as status chips — **✓ already provided**, **● required & missing**, **○ optional (with its default)** — in the **Scripts** detail (cross-referenced against defined Env Vars/Secrets), the **Run** dialog (vs. existing override rows + scope env vars; one-click *add as override*), and the **Job Composer** (vs. the injected job/schedule/scope env; one-click *add to job env*).
- **Git submodule sync:** the sync engine now initializes and **recursively updates git submodules** on both clone and fetch, so files contributed by a submodule (e.g. an Ansible playbooks repo mounted in the definitions repo) are discovered. Best-effort — a submodule that fails to fetch (SSH-URL, or unreadable by the sync token) is logged and skipped, never failing the sync.
- **Contract:** additive read-only `ScriptVariable` schema + `Script.variables[]` (`{name, default?, line}`) on both byte-identical `openapi.yaml` copies; a `null` default ⇒ required, non-null ⇒ optional.

> **Operational note:** `scripts.variables` is recomputed on the next sync after deploy — existing scripts show no variables until a **Git Pull** re-syncs (the column defaults to `[]`, so pre-sync rows stay valid).

Tests: `variables_test.go` (extractor table tests across the shell family) + a sync→DB round-trip; `submodule_test.go` (`TestCloneOrFetch_PopulatesSubmodules`, plus a gitlink-without-`.gitmodules` warning). Schema-version assertion bumped to **230**. `make verify` green; `tsc -b && vite build` green; embedded `backend/web/dist` rebuilt.

## 0.30.0 — Catalog Folder Browsing

**Date:** Jun 18, 2026

Scripts, jobs, workflows, and schedules can be organized into **sub-folders** in the GitOps repo and **browsed as a file-system tree** in the UI (the scripts-browsing plan). Fixes three live Scripts-catalog gaps found in use and generalizes folder support across all four catalogs.

- **Recursive discovery:** the sync engine now walks `jobs/`, `scripts/`, `schedules/`, and `workflows/` recursively (shared `walkManifests` / `filepath.WalkDir`), so definition files in sub-folders are discovered instead of silently ignored. Each definition records its real nested `source_path`; identity stays `metadata.name`/id, so cross-references and detail routes are unchanged (path-derived names deferred — Q-FB1).
- **Slash-safe script routes:** a sub-folder script's name is its repo-relative path (e.g. `ops-playbooks/site.yml`); detail moved to a trailing-wildcard `GET /scripts/{name...}` and the body to `GET /script-content/{name...}`, so nested scripts open instead of 404ing.
- **Full-catalog Scripts list:** the Scripts view now loads the whole catalog (was page-1 / 50 only) up to a 1000-script cap, above which it falls back to server-side search — fixing silently-hidden, unsearchable scripts.
- **Folder UI:** a reusable breadcrumb + drill-in `FolderBrowser` (+ pure `tree.ts`) renders each catalog's folders; searching flattens to path-labelled results; folder rows are keyboard-navigable (Enter/Space to open, Backspace to go up).
- **Contract:** additive read-only `sourcePath` on `Job` + `Workflow` on both byte-identical `openapi.yaml` copies; the script body endpoint path changed (non-breaking — read-only catalog).

Tests: `tree.ts` unit tests (**vitest**, newly added as the frontend test runner — `npm test`); backend `TestScriptSlashName`, `TestParseJobs_RecursiveFolders`; gitlab + api suites green. Two adversarial-review passes (Scripts integration; Jobs/Workflows/Schedules rollout) — all confirmed findings fixed. `make verify` green; `tsc -b && vite build` green.

## 0.29.0 — Job-Level Env (Composer V2)

**Date:** Jun 18, 2026

Operator-authored **job-level environment variables** (the job-composer-update-2 plan; schema **v221**). A job may now declare an env map injected into **every** run, independent of which schedule (or manual/workflow trigger) fires it. Builds on v0.28.0 (the v1 Composer overhaul), which it depends on for full-state-resend safety.

- **Schema:** migration **221** adds nullable `jobs.env_json` — the first Composer-line migration (additive, reversible).
- **Contract:** additive optional `JobComposeInput.env` (write) + `Job.env` (read, detail) on both byte-identical `openapi.yaml` copies.
- **Runtime merge:** effective run env = **job-env (base) → schedule env → per-run override**; the later layer wins on key collision (manual runs have no schedule layer; workflow steps layer job-env → parent-workflow env → step inputs). Merged at all three enqueue sites — scheduler `fire()`, manual `runJob`, workflow `childEnvJSON` — through a shared `internal/envmerge` helper. A NULL job-env is a strict no-op, so existing runs stay byte-identical.
- **Composer:** a top-level "Environment (job-level)" editor that **coexists** with the per-schedule editor (copy distinguishes the two); the scope-context panel's injected set now includes job-level env.
- **Plaintext:** job-level env is plaintext and **not** redacted (same rule as schedule env); it never enters the `override_json` audit envelope. Secret/env-var references remain deferred (**V2-11**).
- **Deferred:** definition-time multi-host targeting (JC13–JC15) is split out to the jobs-composer-future plan.

Tests: `internal/envmerge` unit tests; scheduler/workflow/manual-run site tests; backend round-trip + JC12 audit-exclusion tests. `make verify` green; `tsc -b && vite build` green.

## 0.28.0 — Job Composer Overhaul (Composable-Primitive Alignment + Round-Trip Safety)

**Date:** Jun 17, 2026

The in-app **Job Composer** is brought into line with the composable-primitive model
— a Job is a binding of **Script × Schedule(s) × Scope × env** — and a live
edit-time data-loss bug is fixed. Delivered as phases **JC-P0…JC-P9** against the
ratified plan the job-composer-update plan (decisions **JC1–JC9**, mirrored into
the architecture notes §12). Almost entirely **frontend**; the only contract change is
**two additive read-only wire fields** (`Job.enabled`, `ScheduleEntry.sourceRef`) —
both projections of existing columns, so **no migration** (schema stays **v220**).
Both `openapi.yaml` copies updated (byte-identical; mirror + route-conformance
green). `go build/vet/test ./...` green; frontend `tsc -b && vite build` green;
embedded `backend/web/dist` rebuilt.

### Fixed

- **Edit-time data loss (JC-P1).** The amadeus-job compose `PUT` is a full-replace
  upsert, but the Composer's edit form sent only a subset of fields — so saving an
  edit silently **stripped** `timeoutSeconds`/`retries`/`concurrencyPolicy`/
  `concurrencyKey`/`sensitiveLogging`/`tags`/inline-schedule env and could
  **re-enable a disabled job** (`enabled` defaults to true when omitted). The
  Composer is now a **full-state editor**: it prefills every `JobComposeInput` field
  from `GET /jobs/{id}` and re-sends the complete set, so an edit preserves
  everything. (`frontend/src/views/JobComposer.tsx`)
- **Inline-schedule edits no longer 422 / corrupt (JC-P3).** The old form flattened
  inline schedule entries into `scheduleRefs`, which then failed to resolve against
  the catalog; the Composer now buckets entries by the new `sourceRef` field.
- **6-field cron display (JC-P0).** The schedule Inventory tab (and the new
  Composer schedule rows) render canonical 6-field crons via a shared 5-field
  projection instead of showing "Invalid expression".
- **Exact `enabled` prefill (JC9).** The Composer reads the new raw `Job.enabled`
  instead of the derived `status`, fixing the D1 lossiness where a
  schedule-paused-but-enabled job prefilled as disabled.

### Added

- **Inline schedule authoring (JC-P3).** Compose **job-local** schedules (name +
  cron + plaintext env) directly in the Composer — sent as
  `JobComposeInput.schedules[]` alongside the reusable `scheduleRefs`. Cron presets,
  live human/next-fire preview, a plaintext-env caveat, and per-schedule env via the
  shared editor. Realizes the **"× env"** binding the Composer previously omitted.
- **Advanced definition fields (JC-P2).** An "Advanced" disclosure exposes
  `timeoutSeconds`, `retries`, `concurrencyPolicy` (+ key), `sensitiveLogging`, and
  `tags` (`requestable` stays preserved-but-hidden per A7/JC7).
- **Scope-context env panel (JC-P4).** A read-only panel distinguishing what is
  **injected at run time** (the firing schedule's env) from what is **available to
  the scope** (vars + secret **keys**, used for SSH-auth + log redaction, not
  auto-injected). Reads a new `GET /env-secrets` fetch — **keys only, `reveal` is
  never called**.
- **Scope-aware host picker + capability/executor guards (JC-P5).** `targetHost`
  becomes a picker over the scope's `hosts`; the executor hard-locks to `runner` for
  ansible/terraform (SSH disabled); an **advisory** scope-vs-run-type capability
  warning appears (never blocks). Scope options are annotated with their declared
  types.
- **Rich reusable-schedule rows (JC-P6).** First-class schedules render as rows with
  a source badge, human cron, next fire, and an env-key summary, plus a **"+ New
  reusable schedule"** deep-link to the Schedule Builder.
- **Effective-binding preview (JC-P7).** A read-only recap —
  `script (runType) × N reusable + M inline × scope (hosts; vars/secret keys) ×
  executor` — of what the job will save as.
- **Primitive cross-links (JC-P9).** From the Composer to the **Scripts** catalog
  (with a lint-warning indicator on the selected script), **Env Vars**, and the
  **Schedule Builder**.
- **Two additive read-only wire fields (JC-P8).** `Job.enabled` (raw flag, distinct
  from the derived `status`) and `ScheduleEntry.sourceRef` (the first-class schedule
  an entry was expanded from; `null` ⇒ inline) — exposed in both serializers and
  `openapi.yaml`. No migration.

### Changed

- **Shared component extraction (JC-P0).** A single `EnvRowsEditor` (used by the
  Composer, the GitLab publish builder, and the Run dialog), a shared 6→5 cron
  projection in `scheduling/cron.ts`, and a shared `isRunnerOnly`/`RUNNER_ONLY_TYPES`
  helper (`frontend/src/runtypes.ts`) — collapsing three forked env editors and two
  module-local copies into one each.
- **Theme-repaint fix (JC-P7).** The Composer's frozen module-level style constants
  (which captured palette colors at import and went stale on theme toggle) are now
  token-rebuilding functions, matching the `components/ui` convention.

## 0.27.0 — Ad-hoc Run Controls (Per-Run Env & Host Overrides)

**Date:** Jun 17, 2026

Manual job runs can now carry **per-run overrides**: ad-hoc environment variables
(F1) and a subset of the bound scope's hosts (F2), captured on the run record for
audit (F3) and driven from the existing Run dialog (F4). The run path also gained
its first **write-side scope-access check** (F-R) — the mirror of the existing run
read filter. Additive only: no change to job composition (Compose stays
Admin-only), Scripts stay Git-only, and the dual-source model is preserved. Schema
**v220** (one additive `runs.override_json` column). Plan and as-built notes:
the architecture update (decisions F1–F4 mirrored into the architecture notes §12).
Both `openapi.yaml` copies updated (byte-identical; mirror + route-conformance
green). `go build/vet/test ./...` green; frontend `tsc -b && vite build` green;
embedded `backend/web/dist` rebuilt.

### Added

- **Per-run environment-variable overrides (F1).** `POST /api/v1/jobs/{jobId}/run`
  accepts an `env` map, and the Run dialog gains a key/value editor. The override is
  injected via the run's existing `env_json` snapshot — so both the in-app SSH
  executor and the runner agent apply it with **no executor change** — and recorded
  in the override envelope. **Plaintext values only** in v1; references to stored env
  vars/secrets are deferred (**V2-11**). Ad-hoc values are fed into the per-run log
  redactor so a mis-pasted secret is still masked in logs (schedule env stays
  plaintext per §3.7). (`backend/internal/api/execution_mount.go`,
  `backend/internal/runner/redact.go`, `frontend/src/views/Jobs.tsx`)
- **Per-run host subset within a scope (F2).** The run endpoint accepts
  `targetHosts[]` and the Run dialog gains a scope-constrained multi-select
  (defaulting to "all hosts in scope"). Each host is validated as a member of the
  bound scope's inventory — a non-member is rejected **422** (`scope_membership`).
  The shared `execspec.ResolveTargets` gained a subset mode (intersected with
  `scope_hosts`); enforced for the SSH executor and amadeus-inventory runners,
  best-effort for local-inventory runners (deterministic enforcement → **V2-12**).
  Free-form open-host targeting (hosts outside any scope) stays **V2**.
  (`backend/internal/execspec/execspec.go`, `backend/internal/sshexec/sshexec.go`,
  `backend/internal/runner/manifest.go`)
- **Override-envelope persistence + audit (F3).** New additive nullable column
  **`runs.override_json`** (migration **220**) records only what the operator
  overrode (`{env, hosts, scope, executor}`); the History run-detail drawer renders
  an "Ad-hoc overrides" section carrying the plaintext caveat. Effective values
  continue to land in `env_json`/`scope`/`target_host`/`executor`.
  (`backend/internal/db/migrations/220_run_override_envelope.{up,down}.sql`,
  `frontend/src/views/history/ExecutionsTab.tsx`)

### Security

- **Run-path scope-access enforcement (F-R).** `POST /api/v1/jobs/{jobId}/run` now
  rejects (**403**) a trigger whose effective scope (job-bound or per-trigger
  override) falls outside the caller's allowed scopes — the write-side mirror of the
  existing run read filter, closing the documented Q-C write-side **scope** gap.
  Empty allowed scopes remain unrestricted (admin/dev). Adding env + host override
  power to the run path is what motivated wiring this now; the per-role `triggerJobs`
  gate stays deferred to the Compose-RBAC work (accepted same-scope residual).
  (`backend/internal/api/execution_mount.go`)

## 0.26.1 — Scripts: Body-Lint Severity Refinements

**Date:** Jun 17, 2026

A follow-up to the 0.26.0 body-lint scan that stops two hygiene-only findings
from reading as hard failures. Severity/labelling only — no rule blocks a sync,
drops a script, or enters `content_hash` (Decision 8 unchanged). Existing
`scripts.warnings` rows refresh on the next sync. `go build/vet/test ./...`
green; both `openapi.yaml` copies stay byte-identical.

### Changed

- **`crlf` is downgraded from `warning` to `info` when every `\r` falls on a
  comment or blank line** (e.g. a CRLF-terminated `#!/bin/bash` shebang). bash
  discards the comment `\r` and all, so these cases are cosmetic and do not break
  `bash -c`; a `\r` on a code line still reports as a `warning`.
  (`backend/internal/gitlab/scan.go`)
- **A present-but-mismatched shebang now reports as `shebang_mismatch` (`info`)
  instead of `no_shebang` (`warning`).** `no_shebang` is reserved for a body with
  no usable `#!` line at all. `#!/bin/sh` is accepted for a `bash` run_type (bash
  is a superset of sh) and `pwsh` for `powershell`, and interpreter detection now
  resolves the `#!/usr/bin/env <interp>` form. Both `openapi.yaml` copies and
  `frontend/src/api/schema.d.ts` document the new `shebang_mismatch` rule id.
  (`backend/internal/gitlab/scan.go`)

## 0.26.0 — Scripts: Body Display & Body-Lint Warnings

**Date:** Jun 16, 2026

Makes the read-only Scripts catalog show what a script actually *does* and flag
scripts likely to misbehave. Motivated by a live CRLF-over-SSH bug: a Windows-
authored bash script saved with `\r\n` terminators fails on the remote host
because the SSH executor runs `bash -c '<body>'` and each `\r` breaks parsing
(`bash: $'\r': command not found`). Rather than silently rewrite the executed
bytes, Cronomicon now makes the body **visible** in the catalog and **warns** so the
operator fixes the source in Git. Plan and as-built notes: the script-upgrade plan.
Schema **v210**. Both `openapi.yaml` copies updated (byte-identical; mirror +
route-conformance green). `go build/vet/test ./...` green; frontend
`tsc -b && vite build` green; embedded `backend/web/dist` rebuilt.

### Added

- **Script body on demand — `GET /api/v1/scripts/{name}/content`.** Expanding a
  `scriptPath` row in the Scripts view now fetches and displays the real file body
  from the synced clone (inline `command`/`script` come straight from the DB).
  Returns `{content, encoding:"utf8"|"binary", truncated, byteLength, runType}`;
  served to any authenticated session (`RequireSession`); 1 MiB display cap
  (execution and content-hashing remain uncapped). Reader errors map to a clean
  **404** (unknown script) or **409** (file unreadable/renamed/unsynced) and never
  leak the absolute filesystem path. The frontend renders loading / empty / binary
  / error / truncated states plus a Copy button (and fixes a `codeBlock` vertical-
  clip bug). (`backend/internal/api/scripts_mount.go`, `frontend/src/views/Scripts.tsx`)
- **Body-lint warnings (`scripts.warnings`, migration 210).** Every script body is
  scanned once per sync — where it is already read to compute `content_hash` — and
  per-script findings are persisted as a JSON array (`TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'`,
  mirroring `jobs.tags`). v1 rules: `crlf` (warning), `non_utf8`/NUL (warning),
  `no_shebang` (warning; multi-line interpreted scripts only), `oversized` (info).
  Surfaced via a new `Script.warnings` field as a highest-severity summary chip on
  the catalog row and a **Lint** section (with a `danger` `AlertBanner`) in the
  detail pane. **Advisory-only:** a finding never blocks a sync, never drops a
  script from the resolved map, and **never enters `content_hash`** (Decision 8
  unchanged). Backfill is automatic — the first sync after deploy recomputes every
  row. (`backend/internal/gitlab/scan.go`, new `WarningChip`/`WarningSummaryChip`
  in `frontend/src/components/ui.tsx`)
- **Shared `execspec.SafeReadRepoFile`.** One path-traversal-guarded repo-file
  reader (Clean → reject `..`/abs → `EvalSymlinks` → `Rel` re-check, optional byte
  cap) now reused by the SSH executor (`ResolveCommand`), the sync hasher
  (`gitlab.readBodyAt`), and the content endpoint — so the guard cannot drift across
  the three readers. New OpenAPI schemas `ScriptContent` + `ScriptWarning`.

### Changed

- The sync script-resolution path reads each `scriptPath` body **once** and both
  hashes and lints the identical bytes (no double read, no hash/scan skew). The SSH
  executor's `scriptPath` branch now routes through the shared reader (behavior
  preserved — full, uncapped body).

### Notes

- `no_shebang` is authoring hygiene only: the executor runs `bash -c`/`perl -e` and
  ignores the shebang, so a missing/mismatched `#!` does not by itself break a run.
- Deferred (see `script-upgrade.md §6/§14`): a scope-aware execution-time
  `possible_secret` lint, and scanning legacy inline-body jobs (v1 covers catalog
  Script definitions only). The rejected alternative — auto-stripping `\r` in the
  interpreter — is recorded as a non-goal (warn, don't rewrite).

## 0.25.0 — Live-App UX & Workflow Polish

**Date:** Jun 16, 2026

Closes the five remaining 🐞 Live-app bugs (LB11–LB15) found while using the
running app. Plan and as-built notes: the bug-fix-5 plan. One backend serializer fix
(LB12); the other four are pure frontend. No migration, no `openapi.yaml` change.
`go build/vet/test ./...` green; frontend `tsc -b && vite build` green.

### Fixed

- **LB11 — Recent Logins rows no longer balloon for users in many AD groups.**
  Settings → Users & Access caps the AD-group pills at 3 with a `+N more` /
  `Show less` per-row toggle (mirroring the Dashboard `+N more` + VariablesTab
  expand idioms), so a heavily-grouped user can't stretch its row and leave the
  table ragged. (`frontend/src/views/settings/UsersAccess.tsx`)
- **LB12 — Workflows "Last Run", "Next Run" and "Result" now reflect real history.**
  The list/detail serializers never joined `workflow_runs`, so Last Run was always
  empty and Result was hardcoded `idle`. Both now join the most-recent run
  (source-qualified per A9, mirroring `scheduleLastRunAt`): `lastRunAt` +
  mapped `status` in both `listWorkflows` and `fetchWorkflowByID`, and `nextRunAt`
  is now also computed in the list path (it was already correct on detail).
  Backend-only — the wire fields already existed. (`backend/internal/api/execution_mount.go`;
  regression `TestWorkflowLastRunPopulated`)
- **LB13 — Schedules now opens on the Upcoming tab.** A bare `/schedules` and the
  `/schedule` redirect land on Upcoming (what operators usually want first) instead
  of Catalog, via a single `DEFAULT` constant so the fallback slug and clean-URL
  index can't drift. (`frontend/src/views/Schedules.tsx`)
- **LB14 — Jobs table no longer clips the ACTIONS column off the right edge.**
  Wrapped in an `overflowX:auto` scroll container with `tableLayout:auto` + a
  `minWidth` equal to the retuned `JOB_COL_W` sum (mirroring the LB10 SSH Targets
  fix), so the table compresses to the card when wide and scrolls — instead of
  clipping Run/Pause/Resume — when narrow. (`frontend/src/views/Jobs.tsx`)
- **LB15 — The "Honest View" note is now a dismissible yellow notification.**
  Replaced the permanent neutral panel with a `type="warning"` `AlertBanner` and a
  session-only dismiss ✕ (the LB5 pattern). (`frontend/src/views/settings/UsersAccess.tsx`)

### Known follow-ups

- **`notifyOnTrigger` for workflows remains always-false.** Folding it into LB12
  was planned, but verification found it has no backend data source at all — no
  `notify_on_trigger` column on `workflows` (or `jobs`), no workflow-definition
  field, and the struct field is never assigned for either. Populating it is a
  feature (new column + write path + migration), out of this serializer-fix batch.

## 0.24.0 — Pre-Production High Findings: Reliability, Runner Security & Workflow Correctness

**Date:** Jun 16, 2026

Addresses the nine 🟠 High pre-production findings (PP-H1…PP-H9) from the go-live
review (the pre-production findings review), plus three tightly-coupled findings folded
in (PP-M6, PP-M2, PP-L15). Plan and as-built notes: the bug-fix-4 plan.
`go build/vet/test ./...` green; frontend `tsc -b && vite build` green.

### Fixed

- **PP-H1 — SSH timeout/kill now actually interrupt a running command.** The
  in-app SSH executor's `runTarget` now watches `ctx.Done()` and
  `Signal(SIGKILL)`+`Close()`es the session (mirroring the runner agent), so the
  A12 job timeout and the operator Kill abort a hung/non-emitting remote command
  instead of leaking the worker goroutine and a concurrency slot forever.
- **PP-H2 — SSH runs no longer stick `running` after a crash.** A startup sweep
  reconciles orphaned `executor='ssh'` runs to `failure`/`queued_reason=executor_lost`
  through the shared terminal seam (metric + notify), and a periodic age-based
  reaper backstops it — freeing the global concurrency slots a crash used to wedge.
  Also folds in **PP-M6** (the executor is bound to the process context so SIGTERM
  unwinds it) and **PP-L15** (a shutdown `WaitGroup` drains background workers and
  in-flight runs before the DB pool closes; terminal writes are detached so a
  killed/timed-out/shutting-down run still records its status).
- **PP-H3 — Runner long-poll enforces token ownership.** `HandlePoll` now 404s
  when the presented runner bearer doesn't own `{id}`, matching the manifest/log
  siblings — closing runner-to-runner impersonation (heartbeat hijack, kill-signal
  swallowing, run theft).
- **PP-H4 — Bastion hop authenticates with the bastion's own key.** `dial()` loads
  the bastion's configured `auth_key_env_var` (falling back to the target key only
  when unset), aligning job execution with the per-bastion "Test" probe and no
  longer leaking the target's private key to the bastion.
- **PP-H5 — `pageSize` is clamped to 200.** A shared `pageParams` helper (api +
  gitlab packages) caps `pageSize` at the OpenAPI maximum across every paginated
  list endpoint, closing the unbounded-`LIMIT` memory-exhaustion vector.
- **PP-H6 — Nightly backup runs on a wall-clock schedule with observability.**
  The retention/backup sweep targets a fixed UTC time (default 02:00,
  `AMADEUS_BACKUP_AT`) and runs a last-success-gated boot catch-up, so frequent
  restarts can't keep pushing the only durable backup past 24h. Adds
  `amadeus_backup_last_success_timestamp_seconds` + `amadeus_backup_failures_total`
  metrics and persists the last-success time. Folds in **PP-M2** (the snapshot
  write is idempotent, so a same-day re-run can't prune-then-fail).
- **PP-H7 — History tabs page server-side.** All five History tabs (Executions,
  Workflow Runs, Change Log, Schedule Pushes, Git Sync) now request one server
  page and read the `total`/`totalPages` envelope, so history beyond 200 rows is
  reachable. Backend-supported filters are sent to the server; the rest refine the
  current page and are labeled as such.
- **PP-H8 — Workflow engine correctness (four bugs).** Child-run identity is now
  per step-node (not per job name), so a duplicate job name or a nested-branch job
  no longer collides on the `runs.id` PK; the workflow finalizes exactly once
  (no duplicate `workflow-end`, no early termination when a branch isn't the last
  step); `markSkipped` defaults `run_type` so an unresolved skipped job's row
  persists; and compose-create rejects duplicate job names (422) as an interim guard.
- **PP-H9 — `paused_jobs` no longer orphaned on git prune.** Migration 200 adds
  source-matched AFTER DELETE cascade triggers (with a one-time sweep of existing
  orphans), plus a defense-in-depth sweep in the git prune — so a removed-then-
  re-added git job/workflow doesn't silently come back paused.

### Added

- `AMADEUS_BACKUP_AT` (daily backup time, default `02:00` UTC) and
  `AMADEUS_SSH_EXECUTOR_STALE_AFTER` (SSH-orphan reaper window, default `24h`).
- Prometheus series: `amadeus_backup_last_success_timestamp_seconds`,
  `amadeus_backup_failures_total`, `amadeus_ssh_orphans_reconciled_total`.

### Database

- Migration **200** (`200_paused_jobs_cascade`) — cascade triggers + one-time
  orphan cleanup for `paused_jobs`. No other schema change.

## 0.23.1 — Pre-Production Blockers: RBAC Enforcement, Path Traversal Guards & Redaction Hardening

**Date:** Jun 16, 2026

Addresses the first two pre-production blocker batches (PP-B1 through PP-B4) found
during the go-live security review (the pre-production findings review). Every mutating
API route now enforces **role-based permissions** via a new `requirePerm` middleware
backed by the built-in role→permission matrix; the frontend mirrors these gates so
operators only see controls they can use. The GitLab publish path is hardened
against **path traversal**, the secret redactor handles **multi-line values** (PEM
keys), and secret reveal is **fail-closed** when the audit write errors.

### Added

- **Permission-matrix RBAC middleware (`requirePerm`)** — A new `requirePerm`
  handler wrapper evaluates the caller's resolved roles against the built-in
  permission matrix (`permsForRoles`) and returns 403 when the required permission
  is not held. Four predicates are defined: `permManageRoles`,
  `permConfigureApp`, `permManageEnvVars`, `permPublishSchedule`. The middleware
  chains `RequireSession → RequireCSRF → permission check`, so every gated route
  gets session, CSRF, and authz in one wrapper (PP-B1).
- **`/capabilities` exposes caller permissions** — The existing feature-flag
  endpoint now returns four additional booleans (`manageRoles`, `configureApp`,
  `manageEnvVars`, `publishSchedule`) reflecting the caller's effective
  permissions, so the SPA can gate admin surfaces without a failed write.
  `Capabilities` TypeScript interface and `fetchCapabilities` updated; defaults to
  all-off on error (PP-B1).
- **`canTriggerJobs` UI helper** — `frontend/src/auth.tsx` exports
  `canTriggerJobs(me)` which checks the caller's roles against the trigger-capable
  set (`admin | approver | operator`). Jobs and Workflows views hide Run / Kill /
  Pause / Resume buttons for Viewers (PP-B1 B1-12). This is a UX stopgap — the
  backend run path is not yet role-enforced (deferred PP-L18/L19).
- **Path traversal guard for file publishing (`validatePublishPath`)** — The
  GitLab publish handler and `Publish()` service both reject `filePath` values
  containing `..` escapes, absolute paths, wrong extensions, or directories
  outside the allowed set (`jobs/`, `schedules/`, `workflows/`). Defense-in-depth:
  the guard runs at both the handler and service layers. `buildDiff` also refuses
  out-of-tree reads (PP-B3). Pinned by `TestValidatePublishPath` and
  `TestPublishScheduleRejectsTraversal`.
- **Multi-line secret redaction** — `addRedactionValue` splits multi-line secret
  values (e.g. PEM private keys) into individual lines and adds each
  discriminating line to the redaction dictionary, so line-by-line log redaction
  masks secrets that span multiple lines (PP-B4a). Pinned by
  `TestMultiLineRedaction`.
- **Fail-closed secret reveal** — `POST /env-secrets/{id}/reveal` now writes the
  audit row **before** returning the plaintext; if the `change_log` write errors,
  the endpoint returns 500 with the value withheld rather than leaking a secret
  without an audit trail (PP-B4b). Pinned by
  `TestRevealFailsClosedWhenAuditWriteFails`.
- **Run-output redaction at display** — `GET /runs/{id}` now masks A12 captured
  `outputs` values against the secret/env-var redaction dictionary at display
  time. The stored `outputs_json` stays raw so inter-job passing still works; only
  the API response is redacted. Fail-closed: if the redactor can't be built, every
  value is masked (PP-B4c). Pinned by `TestRunOutputsRedactedAtDisplay`.
- **RBAC integration tests** — `TestRBACCapabilitiesMatrix`,
  `TestRBACManageRolesGate`, `TestRBACConfigureAppGate` exercise the permission
  matrix end-to-end (trusted-header auth with seeded AD group→role mappings).
- **Bootstrap-admin lockout warning** — `auth.NewService` now warns at startup if
  no admin `ad_group_mapping` exists and `AMADEUS_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_GROUP` is unset,
  so first-boot lockout under enforced RBAC is immediately obvious (PP-B1).
- **Safe GitOps prune guards (PP-B2)** — Each subsystem's GitOps prune
  (`DELETE … WHERE synced_at < ?`) now runs **only** when that subsystem parsed
  cleanly (zero parse / resolve / cross-ref errors). A transient read error, one
  corrupt file, or a mid-rewrite tree no longer deletes the entire catalog of that
  kind. A legitimately empty directory still prunes (real "operator removed all
  defs" delete). Skipped subsystems are logged. Pinned by
  `TestSyncPruneSkippedOnParseError`.

### Changed

- **All mutating settings/access/secret routes now `requirePerm`-gated** — Env
  var and secret CRUD require `ManageEnvVars`; scope, alert, SSH host/bastion,
  settings, and audit-export routes require `ConfigureApp`; roles and AD-group
  mapping routes require `ManageRoles`; the publish endpoint requires
  `PublishSchedule` (PP-B1). Read-only operational endpoints (job list, scope
  list, general-settings TZ) remain session-only.
- **Sensitive reads gated (Q2)** — `GET /settings/gitlab`, `GET /settings/vault`,
  and `GET /audit/export` are now `ConfigureApp`-gated, preventing non-admin
  operators from reading connection credentials and the full audit export.
- **Settings view permission-aware** — Each settings section declares a `requires`
  capability key; sections the caller cannot manage are hidden. Users with no
  settings permissions see a "no permission" message instead of an empty rail.
- **Env Vars view permission-aware** — Variables and Secrets tabs receive
  `canEdit` from `ManageEnvVars`; the Scopes tab from `ConfigureApp`. Mutation
  controls (Create, Edit, Delete, Reveal) are hidden when the caller lacks the
  permission.
- **Jobs view `+ Publish to GitLab` button** — Gated on `PublishSchedule`
  (admin | approver), matching the server `requirePerm` gate.

## 0.23.0 — Dissolve the Schedule Hub: Schedules tabs & the Jobs publish builder

**Date:** Jun 16, 2026

Removes the standalone **Schedule** page (the `/schedule` hub) and redistributes
its three tabs to where they belong. The read-only **Inventory** and **Upcoming**
projections — which span both jobs and workflows — become tabs of the
**Schedules** page; the GitLab **publish builder** moves under **Jobs** as a hidden
"Publish to GitLab" authoring mode. This retires the `Schedule`/`Schedules`
name-and-icon collision in the sidebar (11 → 10 items) and aligns scheduling UX
with the rest of the app's *list + hidden builder* pattern (Jobs→Compose,
Schedules→Schedule Builder, Workflows→Workflow Editor). Frontend-only — no
backend, API, OpenAPI, DB, or type-generation change; every endpoint
(`GET /schedules`, `GET /schedules/upcoming`, `POST /schedules/publish`, …) is
consumed exactly as before.

### Added

- **Schedules is now a tabbed surface — Catalog · Inventory · Upcoming.** The
  first-class schedule-defs catalog keeps its place as the **Catalog** tab; the
  **Inventory** (`GET /schedules`) and **Upcoming** (`GET /schedules/upcoming`)
  projections move in beside it, making Schedules the single complete scheduling
  surface. Tabs deep-link via `?tab=catalog|inventory|upcoming` and mount lazily
  so each keeps its own state.
- **"+ Publish to GitLab" job authoring mode** — the schedule/YAML publish
  builder is now reached from **Jobs** via a hidden `/jobs/publish` route
  (mirroring how Jobs launches Compose), gated on the Compose capability. It
  authors a `kind: Job` YAML and pushes it with the same `If-Match` base_sha
  optimistic-concurrency flow (201 / 412 / 422) as before.
- **History tab deep-linking** — `History` selects its tab from
  `?tab=executions|workflow-runs|change-log|schedule-pushes|git-sync`, so other
  views can link straight to a specific tab.
- **`/schedule` → `/schedules` redirect** so stale bookmarks keep working.

### Changed

- **Dashboard "Upcoming" card now reads `GET /schedules/upcoming`** (7-day window)
  instead of the per-job `schedule` string heuristic, so it is accurate across
  multi-schedule jobs **and** workflows. The "Active Schedules" tile links to
  `/schedules?tab=inventory` and the "Upcoming" card title to
  `/schedules?tab=upcoming`.
- **Sidebar reduced to 10 items** with the duplicate calendar-icon collision
  gone; the Schedules subtitle now reads "Schedule catalog, live inventory and
  upcoming runs".
- **The publish builder no longer embeds its own "Recent Schedule Pushes"
  table** — it links to History → Schedule Pushes, the single source of truth for
  the push audit.
- **Internal restructure** — the shared `views/schedule/` module moved to
  `views/scheduling/`; the builder moved to `views/jobs/PublishBuilder.tsx`.
  Footer version bumped to v0.23.0.

### Removed

- **The standalone Schedule page (`/schedule`, `views/Schedule.tsx`)** and its
  sidebar entry. Its tabs now live under Schedules and Jobs.

**Date:** Jun 16, 2026

Surfaces the S4 provenance columns (`created_at`, `last_modified_at`) across all
four definition-catalog APIs and their list views, adds an operator-facing Git
Pull trigger to the Scripts catalog, migrates the Apprise notification backend to
structured JSON, and lands several UI fixes found during live use (LB8–LB9).

### Added

- **Provenance timestamps on definition resources (V1.1-17)** — Jobs, Workflows,
  Scripts, and Schedule definitions now expose read-only `createdAt` and
  `lastModifiedAt` fields. Cronomicon-source rows carry real S4 provenance dates;
  git-source rows serialize as `null` (the underlying table columns are populated
  by the sync upsert, but the scripts table has no provenance columns until V2).
  Both `openapi.yaml` copies amended; TS client regenerated. Pinned by
  `TestProvenanceColumnsExposed` (list + detail endpoints, both sources).
- **"Created On" / "Last Edited" columns** — Jobs, Workflows, Scripts, and
  Schedules list views each gain two new table columns rendering the provenance

- **Git Pull trigger in Scripts view** — A "↻ Git Pull" button fires

- **Shared `SourceBadge` component** — The per-view inline source badge

### Changed

- **Apprise notification configuration** — Migrate from flat key-value storage to

- **Job Composer enhancements** — `JobComposer.tsx` gains additional form
  affordances carried in from the notification and provenance work.
- **SSH Targets table layout** — Switch from `table-layout: fixed` to `auto` with
  rebalanced column widths (narrower OS/port/zone, wider actions) and a

  buttons at narrow viewports.

- **Runner token reveal (LB8)** — Registration token in the Runners view was not
  displaying correctly on reveal; patched in `Runners.tsx`.
- **Job action button widths (LB9)** — Button widths in the Jobs list were

## 0.21.0 — Schedule Builder: in-app first-class Schedule authoring

Closes the one v20 deferral never picked up — operator (amadeus-source) authoring of
first-class Schedules (the schedule-builder plan). The **Schedule Builder** is the
schedule analog of the Compose (Job) and Workflow Editor surfaces: operators create,
edit, and delete `source='amadeus'` schedules in-app, with no Git round-trip. Git
schedules stay read-only in-app (authored via the publish flow).

### Added

- **Write API** `POST/PUT/DELETE /api/v1/schedule-defs` behind `requireCompose`
  (Admin-only, the same gate as Job/Workflow composition). Create validates the slug +
  cron and 409s on a duplicate amadeus name; edit 409s on a git row and 404s when
  absent; delete blocks with **409** while referenced unless `?force=true`.
- **Schedule Builder view** (`frontend/src/views/ScheduleBuilder.tsx`, route
  `/schedule-builder`, no new nav item): name · cron (preset dropdown + raw input +
  human-readable preview + next-fire times, reusing `schedule/cron.ts`) · env rows ·
  description; create + `?name=` edit modes; capability-gated.
- **Schedules page** (`/schedules`) gains a **+ New schedule** button (Compose only) and
  per-row **Edit**/**Delete** affordances on amadeus rows (with a force-confirm on the
  in-use 409); git rows show a read-only "authored in Git" note.

### Changed

- **Edit propagation (the crux).** New additive column
  `definition_schedules.source_ref` (migration **190**, schema **v190**) records which
  first-class schedule each runtime entry was expanded from (NULL = inline). A schedule
  edit now propagates the new cron/env to **every referencing job/workflow**
  (`UPDATE … WHERE source_ref=?`) instead of going stale in the catalog; a forced delete
  cascades the `source_ref` rows and resyncs the legacy `schedule` display mirror to each
  detached owner's next remaining entry (or `Manual`). `usedBy`/`usedByCount` on
  `GET /schedule-defs` are now exact (counted by `source_ref`, not name-match).
- `scheduleRefs` expansion in both git sync (`mergeScheduleRefs`) and in-app compose
  (`resolveComposeSchedules`) now stamps `source_ref` on the expanded entries.
- OpenAPI (both copies) gains `ScheduleInput` + the three write ops; the TS client is
  regenerated. The mirror byte-identity and spec-conformance guards stay green.
